# Lootpath - the central brain

This document is the single source of truth for what Lootpath is, how it works, every decision made and why, what is verified and what is not, and where the work stands. **Every session updates this file before it ends, after anything is learned, discussed, decided, created or worked on** - not only when a PR changes code. A conversation that settles a question, refutes a premise, or moves the plan is recorded here in the same session, through a docs-only PR if nothing else is in flight. If this file and the code disagree, say so in the PR and fix whichever is wrong; never leave them disagreeing. **A new session reads §0 first**, then the sections §0 points at.

So no second exception was built: the Vault tab says `open the Great Vault, then refresh` when rewards are waiting and none are generated. What did change: the `vault` capture reads on EVERY `WEEKLY_REWARDS_UPDATE` inside the bound and settles on the read that carries rewards, recording each update's stamp and contents; the flush no longer captures the vault at all, because the owner's 19:09:31Z plain read shadowed his 19:09:29Z asked one and was what the companion built `0 vault` from; the companion CHOOSES its vault snapshot - the newest in the reward period that carries links, a read that asked winning among those - and logs which; and the wait indicator says itself where it can be seen, as a chat line at the first load after a refresh, a minimap badge while it stands, and the FIRST clause on the status strip, with the four facts it displaces moved into the tooltip. Eleven guards proven red, five gates green, PR #138 open and not merged.)

Before that: 2026-09-15, night (**C-11a built, PR open** (WKE-586): the `weren't rated this time` header counted pass 1's leftovers - which since C-11 is exactly what passes 2 and 3 go on to rate - so on a run where every pass finished, Equip Now said 25 of the owner's items were unrated and the Vault tab said 29, and both were false. **The items no pass was shown are the LAST pass's `excluded`**, and `ns.Companion.Unrated(verdict, passes)` is the one function all three surfaces take it from: the two tab headers and the `beyond the rating's item limit` tail. Reproduced end-to-end over his own live verdict file (30 documents, 8 scenarios, 3 passes each, every pass 3 leaving 0): the header read 24 for `asOffered` and 28 for the other three, with the names off his own screen, and now reads nothing at all. (321) · into the tier legs`. **Both defects have one root and it is not the document:** the reward LEFT the vault when he took it, so the conversion join stopped recognising the set item as the reward as offered, `setItemKind` read "conversion" as "Catalyst", and the road's `arrivesAt` became the projected 321 instead of the vault's 315 - which is what then put the held 318 under the level gate. Reproduced headlessly over his own 14:27 vault capture, both ways. **The level is out of the identity** (`IsArrivedPick` is the item ID plus "not one of the pick's own keys"); it words the sentence instead - `This is the vault Dreamwatcher legs the plan wanted, at 318. Crest it to 321; refresh to rate it.` and `You've put this on at 318. ...`. **The kind of road reads the SOURCE:** a vault reward is `KIND_VAULT` whether or not his run upgraded it, and `KIND_CATALYST` only when the piece it was made FROM is a different item, so M3-15's vault clone still costs a charge and the leggings never did. **And the join learned that an upgrade is not a conversion, on both sides** - an owned item ID the scan already holds, and a vault index that VOUCHES for what the vault holds - which keeps M3-14's one charge on the bag shoulders. One refusal is deliberately given up and recorded: a genuinely worse second copy of the pick now reads as the pick, under-crested. Nine guards proven red, five gates green, 1198 busted tests. Both tables now say `false`, which is what `Lootpath/UI/VaultPanel.lua`'s own reader has always done and which was measured exact against musl's `mktime` under `TZ=America/Chicago` for a two-minute-old stamp in summer and in winter, across the November fall-back, and for a stamp half a year old. Five guards proven red; 1152 busted and 219 companion tests green. Nothing of it has been on a real screen. See §0, §5, §6, §7, §9, §11.)

Before that: 2026-09-13 (**T-1 built, PR open, not merged** (WKE-560): the headless stub now models each Blizzard widget's OWN mixin chain and nothing more, which closes the 2026-09-10 risk in §11. Every kind and every template `spec/stubs/wow.lua` recognises was diffed, method by method, against Ketho's annotations under `.luals/`; the audit found the dropdown fix of PR #72 was only the visible half. **The real finding was structural, not per-template:** `newRegion` handed EVERY widget the union of Region + FontString + Texture, and `newFrame` handed every frame ScrollFrame's five scroll setters, so a bare `Frame` answered `SetText`, `SetTexture`, `SetTexCoord` and `SetScrollChild`, a `FontString` answered `SetAtlas`, and a `Texture` answered `SetText`. **And the dropdown fix itself still leaked:** it handed `SetDefaultText` to the KIND and subtracted it inside `attachTemplate`, so a `CreateFrame("DropdownButton")` with no template never reached the subtraction and answered it headlessly. ## 0. Where we are (read this first; keep it current)

around the buttons was still the strip. The strip's right edge now ends at `Refresh`'s left, less the same 8 points
R-8 used to stop its text, so the words are where they were and the mouse stops with them. The order in
`buildStatusStrip` is inverted for it: the three buttons are built first and anchored to the FRAME's own right edge at
`UI.STRIP_BUTTON_TOP` (the row's top plus the one point that centres a 20-point button on a 22-point row), and the
strip is built after them and anchored to the leftmost. Anchoring the buttons to the strip AND the strip to a button
is a circle the client cannot resolve, which is what the new guard names. The nudge row is the one thing deliberately
left on the frame's own right edge: it is a row with no buttons on it and a clause that does not wrap, and following
the strip would have cut 248 points off it.

And the words point at the button: `rating your gear, started 3 minutes ago, usually about a minute · Refresh loads it
when it's ready`. `Drift.WAIT_TOOLTIP` says the same in a sentence. Nothing on screen says `click` about the strip any
more, though the strip's wait click still works - it is a second way in, not the promise. Untouched: the six decisions,
the nudge, the strip's tooltip content, the three buttons' own tooltips, `Drift.Click`, and `WAIT_CHAT_LINE`.

**Human-required, on WKE-623:** the owner hovers the gaps between the buttons (nothing happens), hovers the sentence
(the facts), and reads the wait clause after a refresh; screenshot on the issue.

**Before that, 2026-09-22 (C-17 built, WKE-624, PR open: a write into `Data\` that the client is holding is waited out rather than lost.)**
The owner's terminal, 2026-09-21 17:40:23, on `main` `f735faf`: `warning: the status file cannot be written (EPERM:
operation not permitted, rename '...\.CompanionStatus.lua.47652.tmp' -> '...\CompanionStatus.lua'); the log is still
the record`. His SavedVariables had changed a second earlier - he was reloading, and the client reads `Data\*.lua` at
that instant, while Windows refuses a rename over a file another process holds open. That run then FAILED (QE Live
refused the profile) and the strip went on saying `rating your gear, started 3 minutes ago` for the whole of it,
because the failure was never written where the addon reads it. So `output.writeAtomic` - the one function the
verdict, the status file and the log's directory rule all go through - now RETRIES the rename on `EPERM`, `EBUSY` and
`EACCES`: **ten tries over at most ~1.9 s**, 25 ms before the second and doubling to a 300 ms ceiling (25, 50, 100,
200, then 300 five times). The numbers are a choice, not a measurement - nothing here was timed against a real client;
ten because the warning must still arrive while somebody is watching the terminal, ~2 s because that is the order of a
reload's read of one small file and far below the minutes a run takes. When there was a wait, ONE line afterwards and
never one per try: `status file written after 3 tries; the client was reading it`, and `verdict file written after ...`
for the other writer. Any other error - and the tenth try - gives up exactly as before, with the same warning, the
temp file removed and the previous file standing. Unchanged: the temp-file-then-rename shape, the warning text, the
addon. Seven guards proven red; 276 companion tests. See §7 2026-09-22 (C-17), §11.

**Scaled down, and said in the PR:** the issue asked for the retry AND its one log line inside `lib/output.js` alone.
The line cannot reach `Data/companion.log` from there - `output.js` has no logger, `lib/log.js` already requires it,
and the configured sink is built in `companion.js` - so the notice is a callback (`options.onRetry`) that
`lib/status.js` passes through and `companion.js` phrases, two lines in each. That is the smallest wiring that makes
the requirement real rather than dead code.

**Human-required after the merge:** the owner restarts his watcher, and nothing else. The next reload that collides
with a write shows up as the one retry line in `Data/companion.log` instead of the warning.

**Before that, 2026-09-18, afternoon (C-15a built, WKE-620, PR open: a stored rating that is not this character's is dropped at login.)**
The owner refreshed on his Restoration Shaman with C-15 in the game and Equip Now still showed the Druid's fifteen
`you don't own this` rows. C-15 was doing exactly what it was built to do - the chat line said the file on disk did not
say which character it was for - but a gate stops an IMPORT, and the rating on screen had been stored by the Shaman's
FIRST login, before the gate existed. With C-16 unbuilt no Shaman file is ever written, so nothing was ever going to
take it out: the one file that could replace it is refused every time.

So the STORE is swept as well as the file. `Companion.DropForeignImports` runs at every login whichever way the gate
answered - on the Shaman, whose file is refused, and on the Druid, where it runs BEFORE `ImportAll` so an arriving
rating replaces nothing and is compared against nothing. Each store owns its own walk, because the shelves are the
stores' shape and nothing outside them should have to know there are seven: `QEImport.Forget(shouldDrop)` over
`qeImport`, `qeImports`, `qeImportsByScenario` and C-11's `qePassesByScenario`, and `UFImport.Forget(shouldDrop)` over
`ufImport`, `ufImports` and C-7's `ufImportsByLevel`. Both count DISTINCT verdicts by table identity, because one
rating sits on three shelves at once and two ratings gone are two, not six.

**How a stored rating's source and character are told apart, and why it has to be that way round.** `source` is asked
first and it is asked of the field, never of the absence of a `character`: a paste carries no character and never
will - the player went and got that export and put it in the box on this character himself - so a rule keyed on the
missing field would throw away every paste in the game. Only a companion import can be in `db.char` without anyone
having chosen it here. Who it is for is then C-15's own `Companion.CharacterClause`, the same function the file gate
calls, so a stored rating and a file on disk can never disagree about whose they are: no `character` at all is
somebody else's (that is every import stored before C-15, including the one in the owner's Shaman), another name or
realm is somebody else's, a class that contradicts is somebody else's, and a client that names nobody yet - which
`ADDON_LOADED` can be - drops nothing.

One line, in the addon's voice, only when something went:
`dropped a rating that wasn't for this character - /lootpath refresh to rate this one`. No source named, nothing about
a file on disk. `RoadsCache.Changed()` follows a drop as it follows an import, for the sharper reason: the cache may
already hold roads built from what has just gone. Untouched: the file gate, the import path, the flush, `db.global`,
and everything else in `db.char` - `upgradeMap`, `equipNow`, the folds. Twenty guards proven red; five gates green.

**Human-required, on the issue:** the owner logs the Shaman in and screenshots Equip Now - the empty states and the
one chat line. With C-16 unmerged that is the whole check; after C-16 a refresh there rates the Shaman.

**Before that, 2026-09-18 (C-16 built, WKE-619, PR open: the driver puts QE Live on the profile's class and spec before it
imports.)** The owner logged his Restoration Shaman in on `main` `4279b37` and refreshed, twice. `Data/companion.log`
at 19:30:20Z and again at 19:30:57Z: `profile: 16 equipped, 17 in bags, 0 in the bank, 0 vault, 99 lines` ->
`fork already serving http://localhost:3000` -> `welcome dialog: none, the browser profile remembered the character`
-> `FAILED: QE Live refused the profile: You're currently a Restoration Druid but this SimC string is for a different
spec.` -> exit 5, the Druid's file untouched. No Shaman rating was ever written. QE Live holds ONE active character
and checks the SimC header's class line against it (`SimCImportEngine.ts:354`, the message at `:360`), and in eleven
months of this driver **nothing had ever set that character**: `dismissWelcome` was the only place a class was named
at all, and it runs only on a browser profile that has never seen the dialog. So there is now a `character` stage
between the welcome dialog and the first import. It reads QE Live's own header control - the `Current Spec` MUI
`Select` of `QEHeaderClassSelector.js:36-60`, whose `onChange` is `QEHeader.js:134`'s `handlePickPlayerSpec`
(`App.tsx:273-277`), which makes that spec's character active - and when it names another character it opens the menu,
picks the profile's own, and reads the header BACK. The log says `character: Restoration Shaman (switched from
Restoration Druid)` or `character: Restoration Druid (already)`, with its milliseconds, every run. Nothing touches
local storage and nothing patches his fork. Twelve guards, eight proven red; 270 companion tests. See §0, §4, §5,
§7 2026-09-18 (C-16), §11.

**What the build refuted or scaled down, recorded in §7 and in the PR:** (a) the issue read `fork.js:82`'s
`dismissWelcome(page, className)` as the class the driver picks - it is, but **no caller has ever passed one**, so
`opts.className || 'DRUID'` meant every welcome dialog the companion ever answered created a Restoration Druid
whoever the player was; (b) his welcome tiles are captioned by `getShortClassName` (`Welcome.tsx:72-76`) - `Druid`,
`Shaman`, `H Priest`, `D Priest` - so the class TOKEN the old call passed matched the Druid tile only by the luck of a
case-insensitive regex and would have matched **no tile at all** for a Priest; both are fixed by the shared lookup,
which starts from QE Live's own name for the character (`Restoration Shaman`) and derives the tile caption and the
menu item from it. (c) His check is on the CLASS, not the spec: `checkSimCValid` line 354 asks whether the active
character's spec string CONTAINS the header's class word, so a Holy Priest profile would have imported cleanly against
a Discipline Priest. The switch is still made on either half differing, because the numbers QE Live returns are for
the spec its header names (§4, 2026-09-08). (d) `handlePickPlayerSpec` falls back to index 0 when no character of that
spec exists (`PlayerChars.ts:155-163`) - which cannot happen, because `init` auto-adds every one of `CONSTANTS.specs`
that local storage is missing (`:44-54`) - and the read-back guard covers it either way.

**Human-required after the merge:** the owner restarts the watcher, refreshes on the Shaman (the log names the switch
and `Data/QEVerdict.lua` carries `character.class = "SHAMAN"`), then refreshes on the Druid (the switch back);
screenshots of both Equip Now tabs on the issue.

**Before that, 2026-09-18 afternoon (R-7d built, WKE-621, PR open: `last rated` on the strip is this character's rating, not the account's newest read.)**
The same WKE-592 walkthrough that produced R-8 and C-15 left a third finding on the same two screenshots: the strip said `your gear wasn't read at logout - last rated 73 seconds ago` on the owner's Restoration Shaman, whose gear has never been rated at all (the run failed, `companion.log` 19:30:58Z), and `last rated 75 seconds ago` on his Druid, whose rating on screen was written 2026-09-17T01:14:58Z. Both ages were the Shaman's refresh capture. The cause: `Drift.gearUnreadText` took its age from `Companion.GearUnreadAtFlush()`'s `inventory` snapshot, and `db.global.captures` is ACCOUNT-wide - so the number was whichever character read last, and a read is not a rating. `GearUnreadAtFlush` stays the GATE (the last unload really did refuse the gear); the CLOCK is now `Drift.PlanStamp()`, this character's own stored verdict, which is the same stamp the tooltip's `Rated ... ago` counts from. With nothing rated on this character the clause says the fact and stops - `your gear wasn't read at logout` - because `last rated` with nothing rated is a number about somebody else; the chat line keeps its tail either way, since a chat frame has no button on it. Four guards proven red (5, 1, 1 and 6 failures). See §7 2026-09-18 (R-7d), §11. **The owner owes one screen:** the strip on the Druid after a real logout, its age matching the tooltip's `Rated ... ago` line; screenshot on WKE-621.
**Before that, 2026-09-18, afternoon (R-8a, WKE-618 built, PR open: the strip's three buttons sit ABOVE the strip.)**
The owner, hours after R-8 merged: "unable to refresh, nothing happens when I click it or any of the other buttons." His

PARENT's plus one, so the moment those buttons stopped being the strip's children they stopped being above it, and the
strip has swallowed every press on all three since. The fix is a level and nothing else: `ns.UI.STRIP_BUTTON_KEYS` names

`buildStatusStrip` and again in `UI.RefreshStrip` right after the strip's own `SetShown`, because no exported
documentation says what a re-show does to two siblings that share a level. There is deliberately no third raise in
`UI.ShowTab`: every other show reaches `UI.RefreshStrip` anyway, so a third one is code no test could turn red. Parentage, anchors, sizes, labels, tooltips, the strip's mouse
and its `OnMouseUp` are untouched; the NineSlice at 500 was never the cause. **Two premises corrected:** the stub did NOT
record `SetFrameLevel` - it learned it in this build, defaulting to the parent's level plus one, which is the
relationship the owner's own `/fstack` shows - and nothing under `.luals/` or in any fixture confirms the issue's claim
that a re-show reorders same-level siblings, so the build re-asserts rather than relying on it. Six guards proven red,
five gates green, 1449 busted tests. **Human-required after the merge:** the owner clicks `Refresh` (the reload comes),
`Import...` (the dialog opens) and `Options` (the settings page opens), and runs `/fstack` over `Refresh` to see the
button above the strip; screenshot on WKE-618. See §6, §7 2026-09-18 (R-8a), §11.

**Before that, 2026-09-18 (R-8 built, WKE-616, PR open: the strip's refresh is a button.)**

His words: "we should just make this a button that will run that command for the user when they click it." So a third `UIPanelButtonTemplate`, `Refresh`, sits on the strip's row to `Import...`'s left, and its click is `ns.Drift.Click()` - the one function the strip's wait click and `/lootpath refresh` already shared, so a rating that is ready loads and anything else refreshes and nothing gains a new power. It is on the row in every state, including over H-1's Coming soon screen where `Import...` and `Options` already stay; in combat it greys out like the Equip buttons. Its tooltip is one line saying what THIS press will do: `rate what you wear now - takes a reload`, `load the rating that's ready - takes a reload`, or `not in combat - the reload is blocked there`. And the command comes off the STRIP: the gear-unread clause stops at the age, while the CHAT line - said once at a login where there is no button - keeps `· Refresh in the window, or /lootpath refresh`. **Before that, 2026-09-18 (C-15, WKE-615 built, PR open: a rating is for ONE character, and the file says which one.**
The owner logged an old Restoration Shaman in on the account his Druid is rated on, the same morning: Equip Now showed

logs in loads it. So the companion now says who it rated - `character = { name, realm, class }`, the class being

`Companion.Startup` gates on it before anything is parsed or stored and says one line, **`this rating is for Hotornot
on Area 52 - /lootpath refresh to rate this character`**; `/lootpath status` says the same; a file that names no
character at all (every file written before this one) is refused the same way, because a rating that cannot say who it
is for cannot be trusted to anyone. `SpecClause` compares the class BEFORE the spec name, which is the half that
matters: `Restoration` matches `Restoration` across Druid and Shaman, so the spec line never fired and H-1's healing
gate let it through as well - a Restoration Shaman IS a healer. Nothing new is drawn: the Shaman sees exactly what a
fresh character sees. The paste box, the loop, the flush, `db.global.captures`, H-1 and `QEImport.Store` are untouched.
Six guards proven red, five gates green, 1436 busted tests and 258 companion tests. **Human-required:** the owner

The honesty phrases, the sub-header, "Why this?" and the item's own road line are CUT, not shortened; the crest quote came ON without the money. And his global rule of the same evening - never "the plan", "your plan" or "this plan" - is a `spec/voice_spec.lua` guard over both halves plus every tooltip block, and the word is swept off the load lines, the nudge, the spec-mismatch line, the bag diagnosis, Options, the glossary and the scenario name, which is now **this week's picks** with its key unchanged. Three of the table's own renderings were corrected against the code and are in the PR. See §0, §7 2026-09-17 (UX-3), §11.

**What the build refuted or scaled down, each recorded in §7 and in the PR:** the table's row 3 carried the owner's
own draft `Wear these - 1.2% over your Lynx buckle.`, and no document carries a percent for a bag pick - a set
verdict is "in your best set", not a figure, and the Keep road's own percent belongs to a whole-set swap that can
involve another slot - so the sentence reads `Wear these - better than your <what you wear>.`, the comparison
without an invented number. The table's line-3 examples wrote `The Coiled Altar` as the instance; on the owner's own
hover that is the BOSS (`The Coiled Altar - The Venomous Abyss`), so the rule it stated - the instance name alone -
renders `The Venomous Abyss, Mythic raid`, and the difficulty label is the client's own string and is not shortened
to `Mythic`. And row 15's premise, that the crest step is "the slot's other road" on a worn piece, does not hold on
the committed week: the Upgrade road sits in the same group as that piece's own Keep road, so it is never one of the
slot's OTHER roads; the line is built and tested off the owner's own vendor transcript instead, and whether it ever
reaches a screen is his to see.

**As of 2026-09-17 (UX-5, WKE-614 built, PR open: the Upgrade Map's by-run view is Run Tiles and the tab's header is one row).** The owner's finding on WKE-592 was two things at once - "There is a lot of text and I'm trying to do more with being minimal, using visuals and keeping the text simple and warm" and "The top portion with buttons and dropdown also looks very smooshed, let's space it out and make things look more symmetrical" - and this is both.

**The header is one row.** Title and a hint icon at the left edge; the `By slot | By run` segment, the sort control and the difficulty control right-packed from the panel's right edge, `Panel.HEADER_GAP` (10) apart. That 10 is the Adventure Guide's own gap between its two loot filters (`Blizzard_EncounterJournal.lua:453`), and those two filters carry no label words either (`Blizzard_EncounterJournal.xml:1956-1957` declares them as two bare `WowStyle1DropdownTemplate`s), which is why `View:`, `Sort:` and `Difficulty:` are gone: each control's caption is its label. The two sort BUTTONS are gone with them - the order is a dropdown now, `Best upgrade first` / `Most upgrades first` - and the shut difficulty control says the difficulty and its key level without the row count, which moves onto the menu row.

**The six paragraphs are on the hint.** `Panel.NOTE`, `RUN_NOTE`, `model.keyLevelNote` and `model.exportNote` are `Panel.HintLines` in that order, verbatim, in the icon's tooltip - the pattern M5-1b built for Equip Now. `upgradeDocumentsNote` is on NO surface of this view: it names a source's documents, which the 2026-09-11 voice rule forbids. It stays on the model and in `Panel.RunLines`, which is what `/lootpath status` reads.

**The answer is one sentence, above the list, with a form per source kind.** `Panel.RUN_ANSWER` is one table of seven strings and `Panel.RunAnswer(model)` picks by `Panel.RunAnswerKind(run)`: a dungeon is run, a raid is raided, a delve is done, a craft is got crafted, either sorted by count names the count, and a map with nothing rated says so. The item is named through `ns.Roads.ShortName` - which already carries its own "the", so the shapes never write one - and the percent is the run's own `bestPercent` printed exactly as the badge prints it. `RUN_HEADLINE_BEST` / `_COUNT` / `_NONE` are gone.

**The list is tiles.** One element is a ROW of up to four runs (`Panel.ELEMENT_RUN_ROW`), and the drawer a tile opens is one element directly under that row (`Panel.ELEMENT_DRAWER`), one open at a time. A tile is `(list width - three gaps) / four` and the Adventure Guide's own 174:96 of that in height: **172 x 95** at this panel's width, measured, where the direction page drew 172 x 97. The art is the file the walk has recorded since M5-3, cropped by Blizzard's own tex coords for that file (`left=0 right=0.68359375 top=0 bottom=0.7421875`, `Blizzard_EncounterJournal.xml:328`) rather than stretched. The badge is the card's own string on a dark plate, the pips are one per drop lit per rated drop and capped at twelve, Delves and Crafting carry none (their denominator is rated items, not a run's drops), and a run with nothing rated is at half weight with `no drop is an upgrade` where its difficulty would be - still clickable, because it was looked at and not left out. Delves asks the client for `ui-journeys-delve-card` at draw time and falls back to a mosaic of its four best rows' own icons; Crafting is always that mosaic; nothing draws a texture the client did not name.

**No number changed.** Every percent on screen is the export's own, transported; the pips are two counts drawn, not arithmetic on a rating. 13 guards proven red. `spec/voice_spec.lua` stays green. **Human-required after the merge:** the owner opens By run in Restoration and clicks Voidscar Arena, Delves and Crafting - whether 172 x 95 of art reads at his scale, whether the delve atlas answered at all, and whether the sentence reads like guild chat (§11).

**What the product does today (all merged and in the owner's client):**
- **The loop:** `/lootpath refresh` takes the `env`, `inventory`, `vault` and `currencies` snapshots and reloads - **and since R-7 (WKE-579) the same four are taken at `PLAYER_LOGOUT` too**, though **since R-7c (WKE-594, PR open) a real logout is known never to read the gear**, so a `/reload` or a refresh is what captures gear and a logout keeps what the last one captured, with the strip and the load line saying so when the plan is older than the player thinks; **since R-7a (WKE-582, PR open) that event is understood as what it is - an unload, which a `/reload` is too - so the captures run on both and are labelled `flush` rather than `logout`, and no capture list keeps more than `ns.CAPTURE_HISTORY` (4) snapshots** - since M3-16 it waits for the vault capture's own question to the client before it reloads, and says `waiting for the vault` on the strip while it does - **and since M3-16a (WKE-581, PR open) that question is asked once at login instead, so the wait is the exception and not the rule; when it does happen the refresh asks for the reload with a box rather than calling `ReloadUI` from the wait, which the client refuses**; the companion (`tools/companion`, `node companion.js --watch`) reads the SavedVariables, builds the SimC profile, drives the owner's local QE Live fork headless and writes `Lootpath/Data/QEVerdict.lua`; a second `/lootpath refresh` loads it. No `/simc`, no browser, no paste. A refresh with unchanged gear costs nothing (C-4). Twelve Top Gear documents come back per run - `asOffered` / `catalyzed` / `maxed` x Dungeon / Raid (C-6) - plus the Upgrade Finder at +2, +4, +6, +8, +10 and Raid (C-7); all three QE Live import boxes are set explicitly, both upgrade boxes off by default (C-5). **Since R-6 (WKE-578, PR open) the loop announces itself:** a second row under the status strip reads `your gear changed since this plan (2 items) · click to refresh` whenever a gear key has appeared, gone or changed since the plan was written, the launcher wears a small gold badge while it is up, and the click runs `ns.Companion.Refresh` - the same function `/lootpath refresh` runs. After that reload the WAIT takes the strip's own first clause - `rating your gear, started 30 seconds ago, usually ready in about 45 seconds · click to load it`, counting, with the four facts it displaces in the strip's tooltip and the click on the strip's own row - the launcher keeps its badge while it stands, and the chat frame says `your gear is sent; the rating usually takes about 3 minutes. The window says when it's ready.` once at that load (M3-16b, WKE-583, PR open; R-6 had it on the second row, where the owner could not find it). **Since R-6a (WKE-590, PR open) that chat line is one of five and the load after a refresh always says one of them** - the run was skipped as unchanged, it failed, it beat the reload, no companion has ever been seen, or it is still going - out of one decision the strip reads too, so a plain `/reload` later is silent and the two surfaces cannot disagree about one run.
- **Equip Now:** QE Live's `asOffered` top set joined to the scan by exact item key; Equip and Equip all work in game (521), and **since E-1 (WKE-604) they equip by bag and slot rather than by name**, so two copies of one item can no longer be confused for each other - **and since E-1a (WKE-605, PR open) that holds for an EMPTY slot too**, whose destination slot is asked of the client rather than taken from what is worn, with the by-name call deleted; a vault option in his best set is a pointer to the Vault tab, not a "not owned" swap (541). **Since 550 (M5-1, PR open) a row is an item line** - the item's own icon, a quality-tinted `WhiteIconFrame` border, the item level in the icon's corner, the name in quality colour, a grey second line and a status badge - a swap is drawn as worn icon → arrow → best icon with the Equip button, the five counts are chips above the list, and the list scrolls. **Since M5-1a (WKE-597, PR open) it scrolls from its first row:** a new row set opens at Head, the same row set drawn again keeps where the player was reading, opening the tab starts at the top, and the list's top hangs off whichever of the note line and the chips actually has text.
- **Upgrade Map:** by slot (every drop by item level, his `upgradePercent` where a key-level document carries the item at the client's level - the cross-level join, 545) and by run (best upgrade / most upgrades, never probability-weighted - 542); dungeon runs rank since 545. **Since 552 (M5-3, PR open) both views are a `WowScrollBoxList` over a data provider**: by slot is a collapsible section per slot, headed by the icon and level of what that slot wears, over M5-1 item lines whose second line is `boss - instance, difficulty`, with `[owned 305]` as the Owned tag and his verdict as the badge with `(at +6)` in grey after it; by run is a card per run - instance art, name, difficulty, `best +1.83%` as the badge, the drop count in grey - that opens onto its rated drops. One difficulty dropdown replaces the row of buttons. Which sections are shut and which cards are open is remembered per character.

- **Vault:** the real reward shape (538); one line per scenario under each gear option (540, and since 548 there are **four** scenarios, `asOffered` / `catalyzed` / `thisWeek` / `maxed`, with `thisWeek` the default highlight); a headline block leading with his pick under the owner's chosen scenario, "none - nothing beats your set; closest: …" when that is the truth, the five Mistcrest counts from the client, and the Catalyst charge (544/548), which 546 now reads by currency ID - Venomblight Manaflux 3465 - so the line says "needs a Catalyst charge (you have 1 of 8)" off the live client and keeps saying "not readable" over the 2026-09-08 transcript, which genuinely does not know. **547 (M3-12, PR open):** a reward the client has not loaded yet reads `name pending (item 275547) - level pending` - or `Preyhunter's Lantern (from the last capture) - level pending` when a stored vault snapshot names the same reward - never `[] (nil)`; the client is asked for the item and the tab redraws once when it answers, and its counts, its scenario lines and the pick are unchanged because the key was never lost. **555 (M3-14):** a **fifth** headline line under the four scenario lines - `one charge (this week, Catalyst used once): catalyze your Hide of Pestilence (302) into the tier chest - 1.73% behind` - read off the `thisWeek` document's own alternatives, and `not in QE Live's export - no set he ranked spends the charge just once` when none of his sets qualifies. It is absent entirely when the question does not arise (no `thisWeek` document, the Catalyst box off in the run that made one, or no inventory scan). **556 (M3-15, PR open) corrects what "the charge" counts:** converting a Great Vault reward spends one too, so every clone is counted and on the owner's own documents that fifth line is the absence sentence; the scenario lines gained the vault half of the catalyze sentence - `and catalyze your Hide of Pestilence (302) into the tier chest and the vault's Scavenger's Spaulders (308) into the tier shoulder` - which is said even with no bags read.

Every scenario's line is in the cell's tooltip, verbatim from `Panel.ScenarioLine`, so the hover and the text panel cannot disagree. The scenario dropdown sits on the tab. **Writing an issue (owner's rule, 2026-09-09; check before every hand-out):** every Lootpath issue an agent will pick up carries, in its own text under "Working in this repo", BOTH of these, with the commands: (1) create your own git worktree before the first edit (`git fetch origin`, `git worktree add C:\Code\lootpath-<n> -b lp-<n>-<slug> origin/main`, `.	oolsetch-libs.ps1`, `.	oolsetch-annotations.ps1`; never edit `C:\Code\lootpath` itself; remove and prune after the merge); (2) rebase onto `origin/main` before opening the PR and again before merging (`git fetch origin`, `git rebase origin/main`, resolve, re-run `.	ools\check.ps1`, `git push --force-with-lease`), because several PRs land beside yours and a conflicting PR gets no CI run. An issue without both is not ready. An owner-run issue that commits anything (a transcript, a screenshot README line) carries them too. `CLAUDE.md` "How work moves" states the same rule. **And the board tracks the work (owner's rule, 2026-09-16): the moment an agent starts on an issue, whoever launched it moves the issue to In Progress; when its PR merges (or the owner's step is done, for an owner-run or proposal issue) it goes to Done - a PR whose body says `Closes WKE-<n>` does that itself, a docs-only or proposal PR does not.**

**Hazards a new session must know:** **The companion reads capture snapshots, not live gear** - which is why `/lootpath refresh` takes them (C-3, merged in PR #31). `simc-profile.js` builds the profile from the newest `env`, `inventory` and `vault` snapshots in `db.global.captures`; on 2026-09-07, when refresh only reloaded, the first companion run produced a profile with `spec=guardian` from the 09-05 capture, missing `region`/`level`/`race` because that `env` capture predates S-2's reads. **Until the client is synced to `main` at or past 85dcacc**, the real loop is still `/lootpath capture env`, `/lootpath capture inventory` (bank open if wanted), `/lootpath capture vault`, `/lootpath refresh`, wait for the companion's "wrote" line, `/lootpath refresh`; after it, the two refreshes are the whole loop, and opening the bank first is the only thing left to remember. **Linear closes an issue when a merged PR's title or body names it** - docs-only PR #20, titled "Brain: WKE-530 UI polish filed", marked WKE-530 Done before a line of it was built; the 530 agent found the issue closed and worked it anyway. Name an issue in a PR title only when that PR completes it; in a docs PR write "the 530 issue" or put the ID in the body after "Closes WKE-" is filled or removed. Also: an agent's mis-quoted path left an empty `C:\Code\lootpath-530;C` directory on disk (deleted 2026-09-06 21:5x); check `ls C:\Code` after a session ends. `tools\sync.ps1` is a manual step, and the client silently runs whatever was pushed last - check the AddOns folder's timestamps against `main` before asking the owner to run a capture (found 2026-09-06: the client was one day and five files behind). Several sessions run at once, one issue each, so **create your own worktree before the first edit** (CLAUDE.md, §12); two sessions collided in the shared checkout on 2026-09-06. A PR that conflicts with `main` gets no CI run at all, so zero checks means rebase, not broken CI. Ketho's annotations are one patch behind the client (§11). `jq` is not on this machine. **`stylua` and `lua-language-server` are winget installs that are not on the default PATH of a fresh shell**, so a session prepends `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\JohnnyMorganz.StyLua_*` and `...\LuaLS.lua-language-server_*\bin` (or refreshes `$env:Path` from the User scope) before running the gates. Until PR #16 a missing tool was reported as PASS, because the command-not-found error left `$LASTEXITCODE` at 0; `tools\check.ps1` now fails that gate and names the tool, so a green means the gate ran. **Proving a guard red destroys uncommitted work unless you commit first**: on 2026-09-15 the R-7 session broke a guard, ran the spec, and restored with `git checkout -- Lootpath/` - which reverted not the one broken line but every uncommitted addon change it had made that session, and the next two guards silently found no pattern to break. Commit the build, THEN break and restore; a `git status` between guards is what catches it. **A cached fixture is shared mutable state**: `spec/helpers/replay.lua` memoises transcripts, so a test that edits one must copy it first (§7). **`tools\sync.ps1` copies and never deletes** (2026-09-17): a file the repo removed or renamed stays in the game's AddOns folder until someone deletes it by hand; harmless while nothing references it, but after a rename check the game folder against `git ls-files`.

**Where things live:** the fork at `c:\Code\qe-live-fork`; transcripts under `spec/fixtures/captures/`; expected outputs under `spec/fixtures/expected/`; every gate locally via `.\tools\check.ps1`; the memory copy of this file that Claude Code sessions carry must be regenerated from this file whenever it changes.

## 1. What Lootpath is

**One sentence:** Lootpath puts QE Live's gear answers inside World of Warcraft, next to the loot they are about.

**The three promises, on one in-game frame:**
1. **Equip Now** - what you should be wearing right now, from what you own, with one-click equip.
2. **Upgrade Map** - for each gear slot, which dungeon boss or raid boss drops a candidate, and (where QE Live has ranked it) how much better it is.
3. **Vault** - which Great Vault option to take this week.

**The product rule, above every other rule:** **Lootpath never computes a healer value.** Every healing number on screen is QE Live's, transported unchanged from its export. Lootpath's own work is the scanner (gear, bags, bank, vault), the loot map (Encounter Journal walk), matching, and display. No network, no backend, no behaviour in combat, no estimate of its own to fill a gap.

**It is for healers, and since H-1 (WKE-596, 2026-09-16) that is ENFORCED rather than assumed.** In any spec whose role the client names as something other than `HEALER`, Lootpath draws one `Coming soon` screen, says nothing in place, and refuses to store that spec's gear as what you wear - so the three promises below are always about a healing set. A role the client does not name is never gated, because at a load and at a flush it names none.

**Who it is for, in order:** the owner (MVP = the owner alone, on one character); then healers generally; DPS via Raidbots/MythicSim output is a later extension of the same import interface, not an MVP goal.

**Why this exists:** the audience's whole gearing loop today is alt-tab: `/simc` in game, paste into QE Live in a browser, read the answer there, alt-tab back and try to remember it at the vault or when a drop appears. QE Live is right about the math; everything around the math happens where the game cannot see it. Mr. Mythical solves this in-game for DPS with a SimulationCraft-trained model; SimulationCraft cannot model healing, so no healer equivalent could be built that way. Lootpath is "Mr. Mythical for healers" with QE Live as the brain.

## 3. The ecosystem, stated precisely (premise-checked 2026-09-03/05)

| Tool | What it does | Relation to Lootpath |
|---|---|---|
| **QE Live** (questionablyepic.com/live, Voulk) | Healer gearing brain: Top Gear (best set from what you own + vault), Upgrade Finder (values drops you do not own, by boss), Vault, trinket analysis. Web only. | **The brain.** Lootpath is the in-game reader of its output. |
| **Mr. Mythical** (addon) | In-game equip/loot/vault/crest recommendations from a neural-net DPS model. `/mrdps`. | The shape Lootpath copies, for healers. DPS only; cannot do healers. Open-source reference for journal walking and loadout ranking (respect its licence; mirror patterns, copy nothing). |
| **Pawn** | Same-slot item comparison in tooltips from imported stat weights (QE Live and WoWAnalyzer export weights for it). | Already owns tooltip comparison. **Lootpath does not do tooltips.** |
| **GearingWise, GearWish** | Tooltip upgrade advisor; loot wishlist. | More reasons tooltips are not a gap. |
| **Healer Stat Weights** | Computed healer weights live in-game; 234K downloads; appears unmaintained. | Proof the in-game healer audience exists. |
| **Raidbots / MythicSim** | DPS sims; Droptimizer output consumed by addons. | The DPS import path later; not MVP. |
| **WowCoach.gg** | AI log coaching, $5.99-12.99/mo, no visible traction. | The rejected product shape. AI is never the pitch. |

**The gap, exactly:** not "stat comparison for healers" (Pawn), not "loot source lists" (the Adventure Guide), but **QE Live's verdicts shown in-game next to the loot map and the vault.** That combination exists nowhere.

**Economics:** side project that pays for itself at most. Free addon, tip jar later. Comparable free-plus-Patreon tools: QE Live, Mr. Mythical, wowaudit (patron count NOT public; the "3,400" figure from an early draft was unverified and is withdrawn).

## 4. QE Live: everything we know (all read from its public source, branch `dev`)

- Repo: github.com/Voulk/QuestionablyEpic. **No licence file** = all rights reserved. Actively pushed (2026-09-02). We read it for understanding and schemas; we copy no code and no data tables.
- **Top Gear exports.** `src/General/Modules/TopGear/Report/TopGearJSONExport.ts`, present since at least 2026-05-20 (last touched by "handle duplicates"). Schema string `"qe-live-droptimizer"`, `version: 1`. Payload:
  ```
  { schema, version, exportedAt (ISO), player: {name, realm, region, spec, gameType: "Retail"|"Classic"},
    contentType, reportId,
    topSet: { score (hardScore), stats (setStats), items: [Item] },
    differentials: [ { scorePercent, hpsDifference, items: [Item], gems: [int] } ] }
  Item = { slot, id, level, bonusIDs: [int], gems: [int], enchant: string, tertiary: string, setId: int, isVault: bool, isExclusive: bool, source: {} }
  ```
  Sign conventions: `scoreDifference` (exported as `scorePercent`) is a percent where **positive means the alternative is worse**; `rawDifference` (exported as `hpsDifference`) is a raw score delta where **negative means the alternative is worse**. Stated in the exporter's comment *and* confirmed by the arithmetic (§9, 2026-09-06; **corrected 2026-09-08 - the Retail path is `TopGearEngine.ts`, not `TopGearEngineShared.js`, and it DOES scale `rawDifference` by the player's HPS**). The SIGNS are unchanged by that correction. Pinned as named constants in `QEImport` and again in its spec.
  `topSet.items` are the chosen items of the best set (falls back to the full list if none flagged). `differentials` = alternative sets: only the items that differ from the top set, with the delta.
  It is a **file download** (`qe-droptimizer-<name>-<id>.json`), not a clipboard copy. **Nothing on GitHub consumes this schema** (code search 2026-09-04).
  **Refuted 2026-09-06 (WKE-527): there is no Download JSON control.** `downloadTopGearJSON` has no caller anywhere in `src`, in any of his 20 branches (`git grep` across `upstream/*`); the exporter has one commit and is dead code. The live site cannot produce the file today. The owner's fork branch `lootpath/upgrade-finder-export` wires it (Export menu: Download JSON, Copy JSON). Until that lands upstream, the owner gets an export by running the fork locally (`npm start` in `c:\Code\qe-live-fork`, import `/simc`, Top Gear, Export > Download JSON); the engine is the same code as the site. **Done once, 2026-09-06:** the control produced a well-formed `version: 1` file on the first try (§9).
  **Upgrade Finder report shape (read 2026-09-06):** the report page holds the *shortened* object `shortenReport` stores via `addUpgradeReport.php`: `{ id, playername, realm, region, spec, contentType, gameType, ufSettings, equippedItems: Item[], results[] }` where each `results` entry is `processItem`'s `{ item (id), level, dropLoc, dropType, dropDifficulty, score, rawDiff, percDiff }` plus `source {instanceId, encounterId}` and `slot` added by the page. **`percDiff` and `rawDiff` are `new - base`: positive means an upgrade**, the opposite sign to the Top Gear differentials. The fork's `qe-live-upgradefinder` v1 export names them `upgradePercent` / `hpsGain` (see `docs/qe-live-pr.md`).
  **His checks:** `.eslintignore` ends with a bare `src/`, so his ESLint config lints nothing in the source tree and has no TypeScript parser; `tsc --noEmit` on `dev` reports 205 errors; `react-scripts test` is the runnable check.
- **`dropLoc` is four words, and two of them are not a boss (read off the eight committed exports 2026-09-13/14, R-4/WKE-565; the rows are `ns.Roads`' craft and delve roads by slot and the by-run view's two cards).** `Dungeon` and `Raid` are the drops the Encounter Journal walk can find; `Delves` and `Crafted` are the two the walk cannot, and every committed export carries **33 delve rows and 18 crafted ones** beside its drops - the same 51 rows, at the same item levels, in all eight. On both, `dropType` is null and `dropDifficulty` is the empty string, so neither the drop/max/bonus tie-break nor a difficulty means anything for them. Their `source` is a sentinel rather than an instance: `{ instanceId: -98, encounterId: -98 }` on every delve row, `{ instanceId: -4, encounterId: <n> }` on a crafted one, where `n` is an index into his profession table (1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7 appear) and is carried, never turned into a profession name. Delve rows arrive at **321** and crafted rows at **331**; `settings.craftedStats` (`Crit / Haste`) is the stats line those crafted rows assume and **`settings.craftedLevel` is an INDEX, not an item level** - it is 2 in every export while the rows it produced are 331, the same trap `settings.dungeon` is. Measured: the five key-level dungeon documents agree about all 51 rows to the last digit, and the Raid document differs on 33 of them, so **what moves these numbers is the content type, not the Mythic+ key**.

- **Upgrade Finder does NOT export.** `UpgradeFinderReport.js` has no export/copy/download path; `UpgradeItemData.js` is marked "Currently unimplemented". The in-memory result (`runUpgradeFinder`, `UpgradeFinderEngine.js` ~line 105) is `UpgradeFinderResult { itemSet, differentials, contentType, id }` where each item possibility carries `source[0].instanceId` / `encounterId` (used by `getSetItemLevel`) and differentials carry score deltas. An export mirroring Top Gear's is roughly 50 lines - in his repo.
- **QE Live remembers ONE active character, in the browser's local storage, and refuses a profile for any other (read 2026-09-18, C-16/WKE-619).** `PlayerChars.init` (`General/Modules/Player/PlayerChars.ts`) reads `allChar` and `activeChar` out of local storage and **auto-adds a character for every one of `CONSTANTS.specs` that is missing** (lines 44-54), so every healer spec always exists whatever the profile held; `activeChar` is the index of the one every page values. The import checks it: `checkSimCValid` (`General/Items/GearImport/SimCImportEngine.ts` line 354) asks whether the active character's spec STRING contains the SimC header's class word, and line 360 writes `You're currently a <spec> but this SimC string is for a different spec.` into `#SimCError` when it does not. **So the check is on the class, not the spec** - a Holy Priest string imports against a Discipline Priest - while the NUMBERS are still the selected spec's (2026-09-08 above). He offers two controls for changing it and the companion drives the second: the welcome dialog (`General/Modules/Welcome/Welcome.tsx`, tiles captioned by `getShortClassName` at lines 72-76 - `Druid`, `Shaman`, `H Priest`, `D Priest` - answered once per browser profile), and the header's **`Current Spec`** MUI `Select` (`General/Modules/SetupAndMenus/Header/QEHeaderClassSelector.js` line 37 for its `InputLabel`, lines 38-60 for the menu, its options being `classNames[gameType]` at lines 15-31), whose `onChange` is wired at `QEHeader.js` lines 131-135 to `App.tsx`'s `handlePickPlayerSpec` (lines 273-277): it looks up the character of that spec and makes it active. His header renders that control **twice** - the mobile `Drawer` is `keepMounted` (`QEHeader.js` line 297) and the desktop `Grid` at line 315 draws the same `drawer` - so one of the two is always `display: none`. He names a character by spec and class in one string (`Restoration Shaman`), which is what both lists hold.
- **Vault reaches QE Live via the SimulationCraft addon**: `simc-addon/core.lua` ~line 1294 reads `C_WeeklyRewards:HasAvailableRewards()`, `GetActivities()`, `GetItemHyperlink(rewardInfo.itemDBID)` and exports the options. QE Live marks them `vaultItem`/`isVault`.
- **Relationship history:** Voulk reviewed Healper's advice layer harshly and correctly (2026-09-01, Discord). Lootpath must read as the opposite: computes nothing, defers to his engine, drives users to his site. Outreach is the owner's (QE-2), after there is a working addon to show, leading with "your export has no consumer; here is one, plus two buttons" - a copy-to-clipboard control and the Upgrade Finder export, offered as a PR from the owner's fork. Never mention Healper unless he does.
