## 5. Data flow (the round-trip)

1. In game: SimulationCraft addon `/simc` (includes equipped, bags, and vault when available) - copy.
2. Browser: run **Top Gear** (M+ by default), Export > **Download JSON**. **On the companion's path this is driven headlessly, and since C-5 the two upgrade checkboxes are set explicitly before Submit** (both off by default), so a vault option and the gear it would replace are valued at the same point on their upgrade tracks; the pair is recorded in `Data/QEVerdict.lua` as `qeSettings`. **Until the fork's PR lands upstream that control exists only on the fork**, so the owner runs it locally (`npm start` in `c:\Code\qe-live-fork`) rather than on questionablyepic.com/live.
3. In game: `/lootpath`, paste the JSON text into the editbox. **The box takes either export** (M3-6): `UI.ImportAny` reads the `schema` string out of the text and hands it to `QEImport` (Top Gear) or `UFImport` (Upgrade Finder); each validates schema, version 1 and Retail for itself and stores its verdict in SavedVariables with its `exportedAt`. A third schema is refused by name, naming both the ones Lootpath reads.
4. `Inventory` scans; `Journal` walks (cached); `Vault` reads; `Match` joins the Top Gear verdict to the inventory by item key, and the Upgrade Map joins the Upgrade Finder verdict to the journal by itemID + item level.
5. Three panels render. Equip Now can equip out of combat.

Constraints that shape it: addons have **no network** and **cannot read files** (hence paste); SavedVariables flush **only on `/reload` or logout**; secret values apply in combat/encounters/M+/PvP (spike-verified they lift out of combat; the guard stays on every read regardless); the bank is readable only while the bank frame is open.

**Since C-6 (WKE-540) step 2 is not one Top Gear run but one per named scenario, and each is its own IMPORT.** QE Live's three import checkboxes act at import (`runSimC` is handed their state at Submit), so asking "what is this vault option now" and "what is it through the Catalyst" means pasting the same profile again with different boxes. The four are fixed and named: `asOffered` (all off), `catalyzed` (catalyze on), **`thisWeek` (vault upgrade + catalyze, ALL off - M3-13)**, `maxed` (all three on). Top Gear only; the Upgrade Finder is not a scenario question and rides in whichever pass already asks for the configured `qeAutoUpgradeVault`/`qeAutoUpgradeAll` pair with catalyze off - the `asOffered` pass under the default, an import of its own otherwise. **Since C-12 (WKE-577) each what-if is asked when ITS OWN question has an answer**, not when the vault has gear: `catalyzed` when QE Live made a Catalyst clone out of what the character holds, `maxed` when something came back above the level the `asOffered` import valued it at, `thisWeek` when either. The gate is settled inside the run, after that pass's import, off the pool QE Live built - his `Item.canBeCatalyzed` and his `CONSTANTS.itemLevelCaps` are what decide, and Lootpath restates neither - so a skipped pass costs its Top Gear documents and not its import. A vault section with gear in it, and `--force`, waive the gate outright; the gate fails open when there is no pool to read. Each Top Gear document records its `scenario` and the three boxes that produced it; the addon files verdicts under `(content type, scenario)` and **Equip Now and the Upgrade Map read `asOffered` and nothing else**.

**Since C-7 (WKE-543) step 2 is not one Upgrade Finder run but one per Mythic+ key level.** His Upgrade Finder values every dungeon drop at the single key `ufSettings.dungeon` names, so the dungeon Upgrade Finder is run once per level in `upgradeFinderKeyLevels` (default `+2, +4, +6, +8, +10`) and each document records `keyLevel`; the addon files an Upgrade Finder verdict under `(contentType, keyLevel)` and the Upgrade Map reads the one matching the level its walk previewed.

**Since C-11 (WKE-572) step 2 is not one Top Gear run per scenario but a SEQUENCE of runs inside each one.** A non-patron's Top Gear answers a question about thirty items (`TopGear.tsx:177`) and the owner's page draws 63 cards, so one pass leaves the rest unrated: on the 2026-09-14 11:42 run, 33 cards left out of every Catalyst pass, 22 of them trinket rows, every one of them reading `not rated · beyond the rating's item limit` in game. Each later pass keeps the cards QE Live made ACTIVE at import - the equipped set, the vault options and their clones, his own `SimCImportEngine.ts:712` and `Item.ts:174` - deselects the bag items the previous pass clicked, and spends the room on cards no pass has asked about yet. **Every pass is its own document over its own pool**, carrying `pass` and the `considered` list beside C-8's `excluded`; nothing is merged and no two numbers are combined. Pass 1 is the plan and nothing else is: an item's RATING comes from the pass that considered it, while the best set, the plan sentence, Equip Now and the Upgrade Map read pass 1 alone. The bound is `topGearPasses` (default 4) and is in the fingerprint.

**The companion path (decision 2026-09-07; S-1/S-2 spikes, C-1/C-2 build it):** the same round-trip with no human in the middle. (1) **`/lootpath refresh` takes the `env`, `inventory` and `vault` captures, in that order, and then reloads**, so what reaches disk is the gear the character is wearing now rather than whatever was last captured by hand (C-3, WKE-536; before it refresh only reloaded and the companion valued the newest stored snapshot, which on 2026-09-07 was two days and one spec old). A plain `/reload` still flushes, and still flushes only what was already captured. (2) A Node companion on the owner's PC (`tools/companion/`) watches that file, builds the SimC text profile from Lootpath's own records (mirroring the SimC addon's Unlicense exporter), drives the owner's local fork at localhost:3000 headless to run Top Gear and Upgrade Finder for Dungeon and Raid, and writes the four JSON documents as Lua strings into `Interface\AddOns\Lootpath\Data\QEVerdict.lua` (temp file + rename). (3) `/reload` again: the addon loads that file - it is in the `.toc`, a committed placeholder ships with the addon - and runs each document through the same `QEImport.Parse` as a paste, pins and refusals included. The paste box stays as the manual path. **Both halves are built.** C-1 (WKE-533, PR #27) is `tools/companion/`: it finds the SavedVariables by glob under `WTF\Account\*` (the account name is never written into the repo and never printed), reads them with S-2's reader and builds the profile with S-2's builder (both lifted into `tools/companion/lib/`, so there is one copy of each and not two), drives the fork through Playwright with a persistent browser profile, and writes the chunk temp-file-then-rename. **The addon half (C-2, WKE-534, PR #25):** `ns.Companion` at load, `/lootpath refresh` for both reloads, the source named on screen, and a repo sync that no longer overwrites the companion's file. The file shape it reads is §6's contract, and it is what C-1 must write. This is the Raider.IO pattern: their desktop client writes score databases into the addon folder the same way. Floor: two reloads, zero alt-tabs; nothing in the client can go lower, because SavedVariables reach disk only on reload and addon files load only on reload. **The second reload is free (C-4, WKE-537, PR #32):** every `/reload` writes SavedVariables and the watcher fires on every write, so step (3) used to start a QE Live run of its own over the same gear - 17.7 s and four byte-identical documents, measured on the owner's machine 2026-09-07 21:07. The companion now fingerprints the profile it is about to ask QE Live about (SHA-256 over the profile text with its four volatile header lines removed), remembers in `.state/last-profile.json` the fingerprint of the last verdict it actually wrote, and skips the run when the fingerprint agrees, the remembered path is the file this run would write, and that file is still on disk; it logs one line instead. `--force` runs regardless. The debounce (1500 ms) is untouched and was never the answer: two reloads twenty seconds apart really are two writes and the second must be READ, because the owner may have opened the bank and captured between them - it is the profile, not the write, that decides. **The loop now says what it is doing (C-9, WKE-559):** the companion writes `Data/companion.log` (every line it prints, rotated at 200 KB) and `Data/CompanionStatus.lua` (`state`, `stage`, the stamps, the exit code) beside the verdict at every stage change, the addon loads that second chunk from its `.toc` like any other file, and the window's status strip carries one clause of it - so step (3) can tell a run that died from a run that had nothing to do, which from inside the game it could not (§11, 2026-09-09). A logon Task Scheduler task (`tools/companion/install-startup.ps1`) starts the fork and the watcher, and a lock file makes a second watcher exit 7 rather than race the first.

**Since C-15 (WKE-615) the file says WHO it rated, and step (3) refuses it for anybody else.** `Data/QEVerdict.lua` is one file per machine and the addon loads it at every character's login, so the last character to refresh used to hand its rating to whoever logged in next - on 2026-09-18 that put fifteen Druid pieces on a Restoration Shaman's Equip Now tab. The file now carries `character = { name, realm, class }` beside `writtenAt`: the name and realm are the `env` capture's own `UnitName("player")` and `GetRealmName()`, and `class` is `UnitClass`'s class TOKEN (`DRUID`), which is the same word on every locale where the localised first return is not. **The writer refuses to write a file without a name and a realm** - a file that cannot say who it is for cannot be trusted to anyone - and `class` is optional only because a transcript captured before the field was carried has none. On the addon side `Companion.Startup` compares all three against the same three client calls BEFORE anything is parsed or stored, imports nothing on a mismatch and says one line, `this rating is for Hotornot on Area 52 - /lootpath refresh to rate this character`; `/lootpath status` says the same; a file with no `character` is refused the same way, with `this rating doesn't say which character it's for - /lootpath refresh to rate this one`. The paste box is untouched: a paste is the player's own act. **What follows from one file: the LAST character to refresh owns it, and every other character keeps its own last import in its own `db.char`** - which is the right shape, because `db.char` was never the problem - so an alt shows what it last imported for itself, or the empty states, and nothing of the main's.

**Since C-16 (WKE-619) step 2 begins by putting QE Live on the character step 1 captured.** QE Live holds one active character and refuses a SimC string whose class is not that character's (§4), and until C-16 the driver never set it: on 2026-09-18 the owner's Restoration Shaman was refused twice, at 19:30:20Z and 19:30:58Z, with `You're currently a Restoration Druid but this SimC string is for a different spec.` and exit 5. So the profile's `identity` - C-15's `class` TOKEN and `spec` NAME, the same two fields the verdict file carries - travels into the driver, and a `character` stage sits between the welcome dialog and the first import. **A class QE Live has no character for is refused before the browser is opened**, one line at exit 5, because nothing downstream could do anything about it and H-1's healing gate should have stopped the profile long before. Otherwise the driver reads his header's own `Current Spec` control, leaves it alone when it already names this character (`character: Restoration Druid (already)`), and otherwise opens the menu, picks this character and reads the header back (`character: Restoration Shaman (switched from Restoration Druid)`) - his control, his click, his state; nothing writes local storage and nothing patches his fork. A spec his menu does not offer is exit 5 rather than a nearest match. **The driver does not loop:** the switch is asked for once and a `different spec` refusal after it is still QE Live's own message at exit 5. The welcome dialog's path is unchanged and now shares the same lookup, so the tile it clicks is the profile's own class rather than the `DRUID` every run passed before.

**Since C-16a (WKE-622) the character the driver is handed is real, because the spec no longer comes from the one snapshot that can never carry it.** C-16 switched QE Live on `identity.spec`, and `identity.spec` was `specInfo[2]` of the NEWEST `env` snapshot - which is always a flush, and **a flush names no spec at all**: `GetSpecializationInfo` answers id 0 and nothing else at `PLAYER_LOGOUT` (R-7b measured it; §7, 2026-09-22 has the owner's four snapshots). `/lootpath refresh` ends in a `/reload`, so the refresh's own `env` is followed within a second by that reload's flush `env`. So C-16's switch never ran once: three runs on 2026-09-21 logged `character: not named by the capture (0 ms)` and then QE Live's `You're currently a Restoration Druid but this SimC string is for a different spec.`, and every profile header since S-2 has said `spec=unknown`. The spec is now read by **one reader used by both the SimC header and the companion's `identity`** (`characterSpec`, `simc-profile.js`): the class token, name and realm stay the newest snapshot's, and the SPEC is the newest snapshot that NAMES one, walked newest-first, bounded to the same `player` and `realm` and never reading forward of the snapshot the run was built on. A borrow says which read it came from in one line beside `vault read used:` - `spec from the 17:39:15 refresh read; the flush names none`. **And it is only ever four snapshots deep** (`ns.CAPTURE_HISTORY`), so four flushes after the last refresh nothing names a spec: that character falls back to QE Live's own character for its CLASS, which his retail menu gives exactly one of for the Druid, Shaman, Paladin, Monk and Evoker - and TWO of for the Priest, who is therefore refused before the browser is opened, one line at exit 5: `no capture names this Priest's spec - /lootpath refresh in the spec you heal in`. The addon, the flush, the verdict file's shape and `ensureCharacter` itself are unchanged: a flush cannot answer this and the fix was never in the client.

**Since C-15a (WKE-620) the STORE is swept at login too, because a gate on the file was never a gate on `db.char`.** `Companion.Startup` calls `Companion.DropForeignImports()` after `CharacterRefusal` has said its line and before `ImportAll`, on both paths: the refused path is the alt whose file belongs to somebody else, and the imported path sweeps first so an arriving rating replaces nothing and is compared against nothing. The rule is `Companion.IsForeignImport(verdict)` - `source` is the companion's AND `Companion.CharacterClause(verdict.character)` has something to say - which asks the same two questions in the same order the file gate asks them: **a paste is kept whoever pasted it**, because a paste carries no `character` and never will, and only a companion import can be in `db.char` without anyone having chosen it on this character. Each store owns its own walk and the caller owns the rule: **`ns.QEImport.Forget(shouldDrop)`** over `qeImport`, `qeImports`, `qeImportsByScenario` and `qePassesByScenario`, **`ns.UFImport.Forget(shouldDrop)`** over `ufImport`, `ufImports` and `ufImportsByLevel`; both return how many DISTINCT verdicts went, counted by table identity because one rating sits on three shelves. A drop says one line - `dropped a rating that wasn't for this character - /lootpath refresh to rate this one` (`Companion.DROPPED_LINE`) - calls `ns.RoadsCache.Changed()` and redraws the window if it is open; a login that dropped nothing says nothing. `upgradeMap`, `equipNow`, the folds and all of `db.global` are untouched.

**Since R-7a (WKE-582) step 1's own occasion is named for what it is: the flush.** `PLAYER_LOGOUT` fires when the interface is unloaded, which a `/reload` does as surely as a logout, and nothing at that moment can tell the two apart - only the next load can (`PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` carries `isInitialLogin, isReloadingUi`), and by then the snapshot is written. So the sequence runs on both, which is the reason the second reload of the loop carries the gear the player is in rather than the gear of two steps ago, and everything it stores says `flush`. The companion's line follows: `run after a logout or reload (gear captured at the flush)`. **And no capture list grows without limit any more:** `storeSnapshot` keeps the newest `ns.CAPTURE_HISTORY` (4) per name, because the loop writes four snapshots per reload and two reloads per refresh and nothing ever removed one (§7).

**Since R-7 (WKE-579) step 1 also happens on its own, at the flush.** `PLAYER_LOGOUT` runs the same four captures `/lootpath refresh` runs - `env`, `inventory`, `vault`, `currencies` - with no reload, nothing asynchronous and no vault interaction. **Read R-7c below before this paragraph is used for anything: the promise it was built for is retired.** The companion does wake on that write and does rate it while the player is away, and on a `/reload` the flush genuinely carries the gear - which is what makes the second reload of the loop carry what the player is wearing. On a real LOGOUT it carries `env`, `vault` and `currencies` and no gear at all. A forced logout in combat captures nothing, because nothing in Lootpath runs in combat.

**Since R-7b (WKE-591) that promise carries a caveat, and it is measured rather than assumed.** "Log out and your plan is current next login" is only as true as the read the flush gets, and on a REAL logout - not a reload - the client has answered the equipment scan with nothing at least twice: the owner's 19:19 flush on 2026-09-15 and his 22:11:52 one the same night, both `equipped 0` with every bag record answering `numSlots 0` and the whole capture 0.58 ms, against `equipped 15` and 14-30 ms on every reload flush and every refresh beside them. The `env` read of the same flush still answers `UnitLevel 90` and `UnitClass Druid`, so the character is there and the item layer is not. Three things follow. (a) That read is now REFUSED rather than stored, so the newest good `inventory` snapshot stays the newest and the plan the player logs in to is the last real one rather than nothing. (b) The companion refuses a profile with no equipped gear before it opens the fork. (c) Whether the gear is gone one event earlier or merely late is **not known**: the addon counts equipped links at `PLAYER_LEAVING_WORLD` and carries the count into the flush's `env` snapshot, and the owner's next real logout on the merged build is what reads it. **That read is taken and (c) is answered: see R-7c below.**

**Since R-7c (WKE-594) the promise is retired, and the caveat is a sentence on screen.** The measurement R-7b asked for came back on the owner's 14:25:58 logout of 2026-09-16, the first on the merged build (`spec/fixtures/captures/Lootpath-20260916-142559.lua`): `leavingWorld = { equipped = 0, elapsedMs = 0.069 }` **and** `flushRefusals` naming `inventory`, with no inventory snapshot stored. The gear is already gone one event earlier, so neither `PLAYER_LEAVING_WORLD` nor `PLAYER_LOGOUT` can read it and moving the sequence between them would change nothing - four real logouts, four empty reads, against `equipped 15` in 14-30 ms on every reload flush beside them (§9). So: **a `/reload` or a `/lootpath refresh` is what captures gear; a logout keeps what the last one captured.** Nothing player-facing says or implies otherwise, and `spec/drift_spec.lua` keeps it that way - a string that puts a logout together with capturing, or with the plan being current, fails the build. The flush is unchanged: `env`, `vault` and `currencies` are worth having at a logout and are still taken, the empty read is still refused, and `leavingWorld` stays on the `env` snapshot as the permanent record of the measurement (0.07 ms). What is new is that the player is told. When the newest `env` snapshot is a flush whose `flushRefusals` name `inventory` and no `inventory` read since is newer, `ns.Drift.Decide` answers a **sixth** state, `gearunread`, and both its surfaces say the same sentence: `your gear wasn't read at logout - last rated 17 hours ago · /lootpath refresh to rate what you wear now`. It is last of the six, behind every refresh state, because a player who has just clicked is owed the answer to the question he asked; and it is self-healing rather than sticky - a reload or a refresh stores a read newer than the refusal and it stops being said, with nothing clearing a flag. The companion says which read it rated in the same case: `run after a logout that could not read the gear; rating the inventory read of <stamp>`, and when that read is itself empty the exit-8 refusal follows as before - now logged `skipped:` rather than `FAILED:`, which is the word its own status file has used since R-7b.

**Since M3-16a (WKE-581) the vault's question is asked at login, not inside step 1, and a reload that cannot be immediate is a click.** M3-16 put `OnUIInteract` where its answer was wanted - inside the `vault` capture, which the refresh then had to wait for - and that wait is what broke the reload: the client refuses a `ReloadUI` it cannot attribute to the player's own hardware event, and one called from an event continuation is not that (§7, §11). So the first `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` of a session asks the same question - the same `OnUIInteract`, the same bounded wait for `WEEKLY_REWARDS_UPDATE`, the same `CloseInteraction` on every path out - with **no capture and no reload**, and simply leaves the client holding its own data. By the time the player types `/lootpath refresh` the activities carry their rewards, the vault capture has nothing to ask for, all four captures finish inside the slash command's own execution, and `ReloadUI` is the player's action exactly as it was before M3-16. When the login ask failed, timed out or never ran, the chain still captures and still waits, but it **never calls `ReloadUI`**: it shows `Gear captured. Reload to send it?` with Reload and Not now, and the click on Reload is the hardware event. R-6's `refreshStartedAt` stamp is written on that path too, so the strip's wait line stands with the same reload behind its click and a player who chose Not now is not stranded. The login ask is never in combat; a login that lands in a fight asks at `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`.

**Since M3-16b (WKE-583) the vault's question is asked properly and is known not to be enough.** Three changes to step 1 and one to step 2, all off the owner's reset day (2026-09-15, §9). (a) The `vault` capture reads on EVERY `WEEKLY_REWARDS_UPDATE` inside the bound and settles when a read carries rewards or the bound ends, the way Blizzard's own frame re-reads while it is shown; `interact.updates` records each update's stamp and what it carried, and `CloseInteraction` still runs once at the end. (b) The flush no longer captures the vault at all - `Companion.FLUSH_CAPTURES` is `env`, `inventory`, `currencies` - because a read that cannot ask can only shadow one that did, which is what the owner's 19:09:31Z flush did to his 19:09:29Z refresh. (c) The companion CHOOSES its vault snapshot instead of taking the newest: of the reads for the same reward period, the newest that carries reward links, and among those the newest that asked; the log says which. And the finding the three sit under: **on reset day the client has not been given the week's rewards at all, and `OnUIInteract` does not fetch them** - the Great Vault window is what generates them, so the Vault tab says `open the Great Vault, then refresh` rather than sending the player round the loop (§7).

**Since R-6 (WKE-578) the player is told when step 1 is due, and told again while step 5 is happening.** The round trip above is unchanged; what changed is that nothing in it has to be remembered. `ns.Drift` keeps the key set the plan was written over, re-reads it on `BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED`, `PLAYER_EQUIPMENT_CHANGED`, `WEEKLY_REWARDS_UPDATE` and `ITEM_UPGRADE_MASTER_UPDATE` (debounced 0.5 s, never in combat), and the window says `your gear changed since this plan (n items) · click to refresh`. After the reload, `db.global.drift.refreshStartedAt` - written immediately before `ReloadUI`, which is what puts it on disk - keeps the row up as `rating your gear, started …, usually ready in about … · click to load it` until a plan newer than that stamp loads, C-9 reports a FAILED run, or ten minutes pass.

**Since R-6a (WKE-590) the load that reload produces always says one line, and that line and the strip are one decision.** M3-16b gave the chat frame the wait's own sentence, because the load is the moment the player is looking at it; but the test was `Drift.Waiting`, which is true only while a rating is still COMING. On 2026-09-15 at 17:22 the owner reloaded, ran `/lootpath refresh`, landed back in game and saw nothing: C-4's fingerprint had skipped the run in under a second, the status file said `skipped` before the reload had finished, and the wait correctly had nothing to wait for. Correct, and silent at exactly the moment he had asked a question. So `ns.Drift.Decide(now)` is now the single reading of `refreshStartedAt` against the status file and the loaded plan, and it answers one of five things: **skipped** (C-4's fingerprint matched) `your gear hasn't changed since the last rating, so the plan you have is current.`; **failed** (C-9) `the rating failed at <stage>; see companion.log.`; **done** (a plan written since the click - the run beat the reload) `rated just now; the plan is current.`; **unseen** (no status file at all) `the companion hasn't been seen; is it running?`; and **waiting** (a run genuinely going, or one still to come) M3-16b's line unchanged. `Drift.LoadLine` says it once at the load and `Drift.Waiting` reads the same answer, so the strip stops counting in exactly the four cases the chat line answers with something else - which `skipped` and `unseen` did not do before, and would have left `rating your gear` on the strip over a run that had already ended. Every state but the wait clears the stamp with the line, so a plain `/reload` later says nothing; the wait keeps it, because the strip counts from it and a second reload while the rating is going is still waiting.

---

## 6. Architecture

One shipped package `Lootpath/` (what the packager zips) plus `spec/` (tests) and `tools/` (dev scripts). One namespace table `ns` shared via `.toc` load order; modules register on `ns`; no globals except the slash handler.

`Lootpath/Media/` (UX-4b, UX-4c) is the one folder in the package that is not Lua: five TGAs - `mark16-edge`, `mark16-fill`, `mark64`, `wordmark`, `icon256` - rendered from `tools/media/svg/` and committed, because the packager ships what is in the repo and nobody installing Lootpath should need Node. Nothing under `Lootpath/` is in `.pkgmeta`'s `ignore:` list, so the folder ships with no packager change; `spec/media_spec.lua` reads `.pkgmeta` and proves it. The three white-with-alpha files - the two 16-point layers and `wordmark` - are TINTED at draw time from `ns.UI.BRAND_HEX` and `ns.UI.MARK_EDGE_COLOR`, so the brand colour is a Lua string and not a re-render; `mark64` and `icon256` carry the colour baked in, because the `.toc` metadata line and an addon-site tile cannot tint anything. **The 16-point mark is TWO files on purpose (UX-4c):** a keyline is a second colour and one texture carries one tint, so `mark16-edge` is the dilated silhouette of both chevrons and `mark16-fill` the two bodies, drawn at the same anchor with the edge underneath and no offset between them. Since **UX-4d** both bodies are at FULL alpha (the lower chevron's 65% is gone - the owner asked for one colour), each band is a unit thicker on the 16-unit grid, and the brand is `#FFB3DB`. At that thickness the edge file no longer covers MORE texels than the fill - both cover 126 of 256 - so the keyline is proven per texel and alpha-weighted in `spec/media_spec.lua`, and `tools/media/contact-sheet.mjs` decodes every TGA back to a PNG contact sheet over a dark and a busy ground at 1x/3x/6x, tinted from the addon's own constants. `ns.UI.MEDIA` (in `UI/ItemLine.lua`) is the only place a texture path is spelled out, and `ns.UI.MARK_EDGE_COLOR` beside it is the only place the keyline's near-black is.

| `tools/companion/` (C-1, WKE-533, plus C-4; NOT shipped in the addon zip - `.pkgmeta` ignores `tools`) | the local companion: SavedVariables -> SimC profile -> QE Live in the owner's fork -> `Data/QEVerdict.lua` | `companion.js` is the CLI (`--watch`, `--profile-only`, `--config`, `--out`, `--force`) and owns the exit codes (0 ok, 1 usage/config, 2 no SavedVariables, 3 profile incomplete, 4 fork unreachable, 5 QE Live refused, 6 write failed, 7 a second watcher, 8 no equipped gear, **9 an empty slot QE Live insists on (C-14)**). **C-14 (WKE-603) put a refusal and a read where a twenty-second retry used to be:** `lib/profile.js` mirrors QE Live's own `checkSlots` (`TopGear.tsx:307`, which the `Go!` button's `disabled` calls at `:852`) over the slots the profile is actually wearing - `missingSlots(equippedSlots)`, one item in each of the ten armour slots and two rings and two trinkets, weapons deliberately NOT mirrored because a SimC profile cannot say whether a main hand is a two-hander - and `once()` refuses before the fork with exit 9 and a `skipped` status naming the slot; `lib/fork.js` `clickGo()` reads `isEnabled()` before every `Go!` (Top Gear and the Upgrade Finder) and throws a one-sentence `REFUSED` naming the pool instead of clicking a disabled button; `lib/status.js` `oneSentence()` writes the first line of a `message` with the escapes out and a 200-character cap, in `status.failed` and again in `render`, and the whole text stays in `companion.log`. **`lib/lua-savedvariables.js` and `lib/simc-profile.js` are S-2's, lifted out of `tools/companion-spike/` rather than copied**: C-1 wrote its own pair first, in parallel, and threw them away when S-2 merged, because S-2's mirrors the SimulationCraft addon's own offsets and slot tables, reproduces the client's `# Checksum:` with adler32, and enforces QE Live's two line-index rules itself. `lib/profile.js` is the thin part C-1 adds: one `{ ok, text, warnings, counts }` shape so a bad transcript is a named exit code rather than a stack trace, and the spec check. `lib/fork.js` is S-1's driver with a persistent browser profile (the welcome dialog is answered once) and `npm start` when nothing answers; **since C-5 (WKE-539) it also sets QE Live's two upgrade checkboxes itself before Submit** - `CHECKBOX_LABELS` names all three by the JSX string literal each is rendered with (`SimCraftDialog.js` lines 122-133; they are NOT `translate.json` keys), the two it was asked about are clicked only when they are wrong, both are read back, a click that did not take or a label that is not on the page is a `DRIVE` failure (exit 4) rather than a guess, `autoCatalyze` is never touched, and `settingsFrom()` reduces the per-box detail the log wants to the two booleans the writer records. **Since C-6 (WKE-540) the driver's unit of work is a PASS, not a document**: `configLib.plannedPasses(config, { hasVaultGear, force })` hands it an import plus the documents that import can answer, and `run()` re-imports the profile at the head of every pass because the boxes act at import. `lib/luawriter.js` renders the chunk; `lib/output.js` writes it to a temp file beside the target and renames, so the client never reads half a file and a failed run leaves the last good verdict alone; `lib/watch.js` gives one run per `/reload` (debounce plus two stats that agree on the size). **`lib/fingerprint.js` is C-4's (WKE-537): the profile decides whether QE Live is asked at all.** Since C-6 it also hashes the named scenario list (adding a scenario is a new question and must cost a run; reordering one must not). Since C-5 it hashes **the profile and the two QE Live upgrade settings together** - a canonical `# qeSettings autoUpgradeAll=... autoUpgradeVault=...` line appended to the kept lines, keys sorted - because the same gear asked about with `autoUpgradeVault` flipped is a different answer. It hashes the built SimC profile with four volatile lines removed - the identity line and `# Inventory captured ...` (both carry the capture stamp), `# Built by ...` (it names the tool, not the character) and `# Checksum:` (adler32 over the body, so it follows the stamps) - and remembers `{ hash, writtenAt, verdict }` in `<stateDir>/last-profile.json` after each verdict is safely written, never before. `once()` skips the QE Live run when the hash matches, the remembered path is the file this run would write, and that file still exists; `--force` overrides, and a missing, unreadable or hash-less state file runs and says why, because forgetting must cost a run and never skip one. The profile is what is hashed, not the SavedVariables: anything the profile does not carry cannot change QE Live's answer. The fork driver is injectable through `once(config, log, args, deps)` for exactly one reason - so a guard can prove the browser was NOT opened. **The file it writes is C-2's contract, not its own:** `ns.companionVerdict = { writtenAt, companionVersion, profileCapturedAt, qeSettings = { autoUpgradeVault, autoUpgradeAll } (C-5, booleans; the file-level pair, and since C-6 the Upgrade Finder's), exports = { { schema = "qe-live-droptimizer"|"qe-live-upgradefinder", contentType = "Dungeon"|"Raid", keyLevel (C-7, Upgrade Finder only), scenario (C-6, Top Gear only, one of the three names), qeSettings = { autoUpgradeVault, autoUpgradeAll, autoCatalyze } (C-6, per document, read back off his page), bytes, json } ... } }` - the writer REFUSES a Top Gear document with no scenario and an Upgrade Finder document that claims one, for the reason it refuses a key level on the wrong kind: a document filed under the wrong question is a wrong answer that looks right - `json` is QE Live's export text verbatim, so `ns.Companion` feeds it to the same `ns.QEImport.Parse` a paste goes through and every pin and refusal still applies. **Since C-9 (WKE-559) it writes two more files, and only ever into that same `Data/` folder:** `Data/companion.log`, every line it prints with a full ISO stamp instead of the terminal's clock, rotated at 200 KB keeping one `.1` (`lib/log.js` gained `consoleSink` / `fileSink` / `tee`, and a sink that cannot write is reported ONCE and then goes quiet - a companion that dies over its own log is worse than one that says nothing about it); and `Data/CompanionStatus.lua` (`lib/status.js`), C-9's contract above, written at EVERY stage change through the verdict writer's own escaper and `output.writeAtomic`. `lib/output.js` now owns one directory rule for all three files (`dataDir`: the Data folder may be created, the AddOns folder never). `--profile-only` writes the log and NOT the status, and `--out` moves both beside the file it writes: a dry run must not overwrite what the game is about to read. `lib/lock.js` is "never two watchers" enforced rather than remembered - `<stateDir>/watch.lock` holds the pid, a second `--watch` exits **7** naming it, and a lock whose process is gone is taken over and said so, so a machine that lost power mid-run never needs a file deleted by hand. `start-companion.ps1` (the fork if nothing answers its port, then `node companion.js --watch`), `install-startup.ps1` and `uninstall-startup.ps1` register and remove the at-logon Task Scheduler task for the current user; The fork driver itself is not mocked - it is proven by a recorded run (§9); **neither is the Task Scheduler task, which is the owner's reboot (WKE-559)** |

**Since M5-1c (WKE-617) an Equip Now row is measured, not assumed.** `ns.UI.ItemLine.Height(size)` answers how tall a line of that icon size takes - `math.max(size, NAME_HEIGHT + SECOND_GAP + SECOND_HEIGHT) + LINE_PAD`, 36 at the default 34-point icon - and `ItemLine.Create` sets the frame to it and keeps it on `line.lineHeight`, so a caller can put something under a line before the client has laid anything out. `EquipPanel.RowHeight(hasNote)` is `LINE_TOP + ItemLine.Height()` plus, when there is a note, `NOTE_GAP + NOTE_HEIGHT`; `EquipPanel.ROW_HEIGHT` (38) is now only the default a row frame is built at and what the list frame is sized from before a draw, and a guard holds it equal to `RowHeight(false)`. `row.note` hangs off `row.line`'s `BOTTOMLEFT`, not off the row's top, and `anchorLine` has ONE vertical rule for both layouts - the line's top is the row's top and a pair only moves it right by `PAIR_INSET` (46), with `row.worn` centred on the line's icon. The overflow line's own gap (`OVERFLOW_GAP`, 4) is counted into `panel.list`'s height with it.

**SavedVariables (AceDB):** `db.char.qeImport` (the most recent Top Gear verdict + exportedAt), **`db.char.qeImports[contentType]`** (one verdict per QE Live content type, so a Raid paste does not lose the Dungeon one; since C-2 a verdict also carries `source`, and a companion one `companionWrittenAt` / `companionVersion`, so where it came from survives a reload), **`db.char.ufImport` and `db.char.ufImports[contentType]`** (the same pair for Upgrade Finder exports, M3-6 - separate keys, so neither kind can overwrite the other, and a companion one carries the same `source` fields), **`db.char.qeImportsByScenario[contentType][scenario]`** (C-6: one Top Gear verdict per named scenario, with `"unknown"` as the shelf for a name this build does not know; `qeImport` and `qeImports` are written for `asOffered` alone, so everything that read them before C-6 keeps reading what the character has now), **`db.char.ufImportsByLevel[contentType][keyLevel]`** (C-7: one Upgrade Finder verdict per Mythic+ key level, with the string `"unknown"` as the shelf for an export that does not say which key it was run at; `ufImports` is untouched beside it and still holds the most recent verdict for the content type, so everything written before C-7 keeps reading what it always read - **the cost is that a five-level refresh stores five dungeon verdicts rather than one**, which is the feature and not an accident), `db.global.journalCache[key]`, `db.profile.settings.vaultScenario` (C-6, one of `ns.QEImport.SCENARIOS`; **its default is `thisWeek` since M3-13**, and it moves the Vault tab's highlight only - `qeImport` / `qeImports` stay the `asOffered` shelves whatever it says), `db.profile.settings.contentType` (**`"Dungeon"` or `"Raid"` - QE Live's own strings; it read `"Mythic+"` until M2-2 and could never have matched an export**). Captures write raw returns under a `captures` table pulled by `tools/sync.ps1 -Pull`. **`db.global.drift` is R-6's two remembered facts (WKE-578):** `refreshStartedAt`, the ISO stamp written just before the first reload, and `runSeconds`, how long the last finished rating run took - global, because the companion is one per machine. **Every capture snapshot also carries `trigger`** (`"refresh"` while `ns.Companion.Refresh` drives the chain, `"command"` for one typed by hand), which is the only thing in the file that says how a capture was taken.

**Since C-11 (WKE-572) a Top Gear verdict is identified by content type, scenario AND pass, and only pass 1 is the plan.** `ns.QEImport.PassKey(verdict)` reads a missing or unusable `pass` as `FIRST_PASS` (1), so every paste and every file written before C-11 says exactly what it said. `Store` files a pass above 1 under **`db.char.qePassesByScenario[contentType][scenario][pass]`** and touches none of `qeImport`, `qeImports` or `qeImportsByScenario`; a new pass-1 import for a content type and scenario CLEARS that subtree first, because the later passes of the run before it rated a pool the new file has just replaced. `ForPass` and `Passes(contentType, scenario)` (pass order, pass 1 never among them) read them back, and `Existing` compares like with like so the second document of a run is not read as a repeat of the first. `Modules/Companion.lua` reads `pass` and `considered` off each export entry and carries both onto the verdict; `Companion.IsConsidered` is `IsExcluded` under another name, because a pool is one list of cards and "did this pass see it" must not be a second answer to "did this pass leave it out". **Which list is which (C-11a, WKE-586):** `considered` is what THIS pass was shown, `excluded` is what THIS pass could not fit, and the items no pass was shown are the LAST pass's `excluded` - the one list the header line and the `beyond the rating's item limit` tail may be read off, through `ns.Companion.Unrated`. The companion writes its file-level `excluded` as that same last pass (`lib/fork.js` ~988); the addon reads the pass shelf instead, which is the same answer per scenario rather than per file, because the Catalyst passes have clones to leave out that the base pass never had.

**Since H-1 (WKE-596) one function decides whether Lootpath says anything at all.** `ns.Companion.Gate()` answers nil - the addon behaves as it always has - or `{ role, spec, healer }`, the three facts every gated sentence is made of. It is nil when the client names the role `HEALER` and nil when the client names NO role, which is the rule the whole gate turns on (R-7b: the spec read is empty at `ADDON_LOADED` and at every flush). It is read live on every ask and never cached; `ns.Companion.CurrentRole` is `GetSpecializationInfo`'s fifth return and `ns.Companion.HealingSpecName` walks `GetNumSpecializations()`. The sentences are `Companion.GateLine` (the load line, `/lootpath status`, and the words the window's screen says), `Companion.GateRefreshLine` and `Companion.GateCaptureReason`; the screen's own three lines are `ns.UI.ComingSoonModel`. The surfaces that ask it: `ns.Glow.Wants`, `ns.UI.Tooltip.Answer` and `.Append`, `ns.Drift.Check` and `.LoadLine`, `ns.UI.ShowTab` / `.Refresh` / `.StatusStripModel`, `Companion.Refresh`, `Captures.lua`'s `inventory` refusal and `Core.lua`'s `statusCommand`. Nothing else in the addon reads a role, and no class or spec table of ours exists.

**Libraries (all licence-checked, recorded in `Lootpath/Libs/LICENSES.md`):** LibStub (public domain), CallbackHandler-1.0 and AceDB-3.0 (Ace3 BSD-style, clause quoted in LICENSES.md: embedding permitted, "redistribution of a stand alone version is strictly prohibited"), rxi/json.lua 0.1.2 (MIT; vendored verbatim plus a six-line footer that sets `ns.json`, because the WoW loader discards a chunk's return value). Ace3 arrives as packager externals from the wowace SVN trunks in CI and from the WoWUIDev/Ace3 GitHub mirror locally (`tools/fetch-libs.ps1`); both directories are gitignored. Nothing else without a licence line.

**Test harness (M0-1):** `spec/stubs/wow.lua` installs a fake client into `_G` (shapes from Blizzard's docs, build tuple from the spike capture; placeholders, never wiki) and `spec/helpers/addon.lua` loads the `.toc` file list in order with `(addonName, ns)` varargs; a fake `LibStub("AceDB-3.0")` deep-copies the defaults. Fixtures under `spec/fixtures/` win over the stub whenever they disagree.

**One widget carries one widget's methods (T-1, WKE-560, 2026-09-13).** The stub gives a kind or a template only what that class or that mixin chain has, read under `.luals/vscode-wow-api/Annotations/` and cited at the file and line in the block that models it. A `Frame` has no `SetText` and no `SetTexture`; text setters are a `FontString`'s (and four of them an `EditBox`'s), texture setters are a `Texture`'s, the five scroll setters are a `ScrollFrame`'s, and `SetDefaultText` is `DropdownSelectionTextMixin`'s, which only `WowStyle1DropdownTemplate` mixes in. **Since R-8a (WKE-618) a stub frame also carries a LEVEL** - `SetFrameLevel` / `GetFrameLevel` (Frame.lua:441, :176), defaulting to the parent's plus one, which is what the owner's own `/fstack` reads on a real client - because a level is what decides which of two overlapping frames takes a click, and until this issue nothing headless could see one. **Missing the other way is deliberate and safe:** a method no panel calls is simply not modelled (`CheckButton:SetChecked`, `DropdownSelectionTextMixin:SetSelectionText`, `DropdownButtonMixin:Pick`), so a panel that starts calling one fails headlessly first - a gap turns a test red where the client would have been fine, while a superset turns a test green where the client breaks. **A template is ADDED to, never subtracted from:** the caption surface is attached to the one template whose mixin has it rather than handed to every dropdown and taken back, because a widget built without a template never reaches the subtraction. **Nothing that is not the client's sits in a Blizzard method slot:** the stub's own affordances - firing an `OnEnter`, picking a menu row by index, acquiring a pooled frame, reading a tooltip back - live on `widget.stub` (`button.stub:Enter()`, `dropdown.stub:Pick(2)`, `world.tooltip.stub:Text()`), so a panel that reached for one in the client would index a nil field on the first frame. `spec/stubs_spec.lua` locks all of it: every removal is asserted absent on the widget that does not have it and present on the one that does.
