## 7. Decisions log (dated; do not reopen without a new entry here)

**2026-09-22 (R-8b, WKE-623) - a surface that takes the mouse ends where its controls begin, and copy that asks for a click names the thing to click.**
The owner on 2026-09-21, hovering his own window on `main` `f735faf`: "if I hover between the 3 buttons, I'll still see the tooltip as if I'm hovering over the text to the left. I also don't like this copy that just says 'click to load it'... click what?" Two decisions, one row.

**The rectangle.** R-8a (2026-09-18) raised `Refresh`, `Import...` and `Options` above the strip so each takes its own press, and that is still true; what it left is that the strip is the whole width of the frame and is mouse-enabled for M3-16b's wait click, so the empty space between and around the three buttons hovered the strip's tooltip and answered the strip's click. A row that hosts controls ends at them: the strip's `TOPRIGHT` is now `refreshButton`'s `TOPLEFT` less `UI.STRIP_TEXT_GAP` (8), which is exactly where R-8 already stopped the strip's TEXT, so nothing the player reads moved a point and the mouse now stops with the words. The creation order in `buildStatusStrip` is inverted for it - the three buttons first, hanging off the FRAME's own right edge at the strip's row, then the strip off the leftmost of them - because anchoring the buttons to the strip and the strip to a button is a circle the client cannot resolve; that circle is what `spec/ui_spec.lua`'s "hangs the three buttons off the frame, not off the strip" guard exists to catch. The one point of vertical difference is named rather than repeated (`UI.STRIP_BUTTON_LIFT`: a 20-point button centred on a 22-point row starts one point lower, so the strip's `TOPRIGHT` lifts it back). **The nudge row is deliberately not moved:** it is the row below, it carries no buttons, and its clause does not wrap, so following the strip's new edge would have taken 248 points off a sentence that can already be too long.

**The words.** `Drift.WAIT_LINE` was M3-16b's `rating your gear, %s · click to load it`, written when the strip's own row was the only clickable thing in the window. Since R-8 the `Refresh` button on that same row runs the same `Drift.Click`, and its own hover already says `load the rating that's ready - takes a reload`. So the clause names it: `rating your gear, %s · Refresh loads it when it's ready`, and `Drift.WAIT_TOOLTIP` says the same in a sentence. Nothing on screen tells the player to click a surface that has no edges. The strip's own `OnMouseUp` wait click stays - a second way in costs nothing and the players who found it keep it - but it is no longer what the sentence promises. `Drift.WAIT_CHAT_LINE` is untouched: it is read in the chat frame, where there is no button to point at, and it already says "The window says when it's ready."

Unchanged by this decision: the six `Drift.Decide` states, the nudge row's own clause and click, the strip's tooltip content, the three buttons' tooltips, `Drift.Click`, and R-8a's `UI.RaiseStripButtons` with its four guards. Six guards proven red. **Human-required:** the owner hovers the gaps (nothing), hovers the sentence (the facts), and reads the wait clause after a refresh.
**2026-09-22 (C-17, WKE-624) - a rename the client is holding is waited out, not lost: every write into `Lootpath/Data/` retries on `EPERM`, `EBUSY` and `EACCES`, ten tries over at most ~1.9 s, and says so once when it had to.**

  - **What the owner saw.** 2026-09-21 17:40:23, `main` `f735faf`: `warning: the status file cannot be written (EPERM: operation not permitted, rename 'C:\World of Warcraft\_retail_\Interface\AddOns\Lootpath\Data\.CompanionStatus.lua.47652.tmp' -> '...\CompanionStatus.lua'); the log is still the record`. The SavedVariables had changed at 17:40:22 - he was reloading, and the client reads `Data\*.lua` as it loads. The run then failed and the strip kept the PREVIOUS status, `rating your gear`, for three minutes, because the failure had nowhere to land. The warning was doing its job; the write was the thing that should not have been given up on.
  - **Why the collision is structural and not bad luck.** Windows refuses a rename over a file another process holds open. The addon's own refresh IS a `/reload`, so the two moments that most want to write a status - a run starting and a run dying - are exactly the two most likely to land on a load. Every file the companion puts in that folder goes through one `writeAtomic`, so one retry covers the verdict, the status file and anything added later.
  - **Ten tries, 25 ms doubling to a 300 ms ceiling, ~1.9 s in all, and these are a CHOICE.** Nothing in this repo has timed a real client's read of a `Data` file; what is known is that it is one small file read once during a load, and that a companion run takes minutes. Ten keeps the warning arriving while a person is still watching the terminal; the ceiling is what bounds the wait rather than the doubling's own tail; ~2 s is two orders below the run it protects and one above a file read. The wait is SYNCHRONOUS (`Atomics.wait`), because every writer here is, and an async hop would let a later stage write the same file underneath this one. `options.sleep` exists so the guards record the wait instead of serving it.
  - **Three codes and no others.** `EPERM`, `EBUSY`, `EACCES` - what a foreign handle produces. A wrong path or a folder that went away answers `ENOENT`, and it will answer the same in two seconds, so it is thrown at once. The temp file STAYS on disk between tries (it is the whole rendered chunk, and rewriting it each time would be work for nothing) and is removed on the final failure, so the folder the addon loads out of never keeps a `.tmp`.
  - **One line, after the fact, never per try:** `status file written after 3 tries; the client was reading it`, and `verdict file written after N tries; ...` for the other writer. A line every 25 ms would be noise about a second nobody was hurt by. A write that succeeded first time says nothing at all.
  - **Where that line is phrased, and why not in `output.js`.** The issue put both the retry and the line in `lib/output.js`. `output.js` has no logger and cannot hold one - `lib/log.js` already requires it, and the configured file-and-terminal sink is built in `companion.js` - so the retry raises `options.onRetry(tries, target)` and the callers phrase it: `lib/status.js` passes the recorder's own `onRetry` straight through, `companion.js` supplies both closures over `log`. Two lines in each, and the alternative was a requirement that shipped as dead code.
  - **Unchanged:** the temp-file-then-rename shape, the directory rule (the `Data` folder is created, the AddOns folder never is), the warning text on a final failure, C-9's rule that a failed write leaves the previous file in place, and the addon, which reads nothing new.
**2026-09-22 (C-16a, WKE-622) - a flush names no spec, and the newest `env` is always a flush: the companion's identity takes its spec from the newest capture that NAMES one, and a character whose captures name none falls back to QE Live's only healer for its class, or is refused when he has two.**

  - **What the owner saw.** His C-16 companion restarted at 17:37:56 on 2026-09-21 and he refreshed three times on his Restoration Shaman. Every run logged `character: not named by the capture (0 ms)` and then `FAILED: QE Live refused the profile: You're currently a Restoration Druid but this SimC string is for a different spec.` - 17:38:43, 17:39:20, 17:40:24. C-16's switch, which exists precisely to stop that refusal, never ran once.
  - **The evidence, read off his own SavedVariables with `tools/companion/lib/lua-savedvariables.js` on 2026-09-22.** His `db.global.captures.env` held four snapshots for Blueheeler-Arthas, every one of them naming `class = { "Shaman", "SHAMAN", 11 }` and `player = { "Blueheeler" }`: **17:39:15 `trigger = "refresh"`, `specInfo = { 264, "Restoration", ... }`; 17:39:16, 17:40:19 and 17:42:49 all `trigger = "flush"`, `specInfo = { 0, [7]=0, [9]=0, [10]=true, n=10 }`** - an id of 0 and no name at all. R-7b recorded the same thing a week earlier about the 2026-09-15 logout flush, and `spec/fixtures/captures/empty-equipment-flush.lua` carries it.
  - **So the newest `env` snapshot is the wrong one to read a spec from, always, and not by accident.** At `PLAYER_LOGOUT` the client still answers `GetSpecialization` with an index but `GetSpecializationInfo` comes back empty, and `/lootpath refresh` ENDS in a `/reload` - so a refresh's `env` is followed within a second by that reload's flush `env`. Every `env` list the companion has ever read is topped by a flush. `profile.js` read `packValue(env.data.specInfo, 2)` off that one snapshot and `simc-profile.js` read the same field the same way, which is why `identity.spec` was undefined on every run since C-16 and why every profile header written since S-2 has said `spec=unknown`. QE Live never noticed the header, because `checkSimCValid` (`SimCImportEngine.ts:354`) matches the CLASS word and not the spec - so a Shaman profile went to whatever character the browser was holding, which was the Druid.
  - **The addon cannot help, and was not changed.** The client answers no spec at the flush; there is nothing for a capture to read and nothing to store. The fix is in what the companion reads. The flush, `Lootpath/Captures.lua`, the verdict file's shape (C-15's `character` block) and `ensureCharacter` itself are all untouched.
  - **One reader, used by both the header and `identity`.** `characterSpec(list, chosen)` in `simc-profile.js`: the class token, name and realm come from the chosen (newest) snapshot as before, and the SPEC is the first snapshot, walking newest-first, whose `specInfo[2]` is a non-empty string. `readTranscript` puts its answer on the transcript as `envSpec`, `buildProfile` takes `specName` from it and `profile.js` takes `identity.spec` from it, so the `spec=` line and the character QE Live is put on can never be two different answers.
  - **The borrow is bounded three ways, because a name carried too far is worse than none.** (a) **Same character:** the candidate's `player` and `realm` must equal the chosen snapshot's, because the capture store is account-wide and the Druid's refresh sits in the same list as the Shaman's flush - borrowing across that is the exact failure C-15 was filed over. (b) **Never forward:** a snapshot newer than the chosen one is skipped, so `--env-snapshot` still means what it says. (c) **Four deep:** `ns.CAPTURE_HISTORY` is 4, so the fourth flush after a refresh pushes that refresh's `env` off the end and nothing names a spec at all - which makes the fallback below a real case and not a corner one.
  - **A borrowed spec says so, in one line, beside `vault read used:`** - `spec from the 17:39:15 refresh read; the flush names none`. For the same reason M3-16b's line exists: a choice between snapshots decided what was rated, and the log should not be silent about it. Null when the newest snapshot named the spec itself, because then there was no choice to make.
  - **The class-only fallback, and the one class it cannot serve.** When no kept capture names a spec, the character falls back to QE Live's own character for its CLASS. His retail menu (`classNames.Retail`, `QEHeaderClassSelector.js` lines 15-23) lists **exactly one healer** for the Druid (Restoration), Shaman (Restoration), Paladin (Holy), Monk (Mistweaver) and Evoker (Preservation) - so for those five there is nothing to choose - and **two** for the Priest, `Holy Priest` and `Discipline Priest`. Which of the two a Priest heals in is not something a companion may guess, so a spec-less Priest is refused **before the browser is opened**, exit 5, one line: `no capture names this Priest's spec - /lootpath refresh in the spec you heal in`. `fork.js`'s `QE_CLASS_SOLE_SPEC` is the five, and `character.test.js` DERIVES that table from his own menu list and fails if the two ever differ, so it is his table and not ours.
  - **A capture that names no CLASS is still not a refusal.** That is a capture too old to say, it stays `character: not named by the capture`, and the import speaks for itself - unchanged from C-16.
  - **And a profile that still cannot name a spec keeps `unknown` and says so.** The header keeps `# <name> - unknown - ...` and the build carries one warning: `no capture names this character's spec, so the profile says "unknown"; a logout flush never names one - /lootpath refresh in the spec you heal in`. Nothing is written as a measurement that was not taken.

**2026-09-18 (C-15a, WKE-620) - a gate on the file is not a gate on the store: a rating for somebody else that a login before C-15 had already written into this character's `db.char` is dropped at every login, and one line says so. This closes the caveat C-15 left in §11.**

  - **What the owner saw, and why C-15 could not have caught it.** After refreshing on his Restoration Shaman, Equip Now on the Shaman still showed the Druid's fifteen `you don't own this` rows. C-15 was working: the chat line said the file on disk did not say which character it was for, and nothing was imported. But the rows came from the Shaman's OWN `db.char`, written by the Shaman's first login months of reloads before the gate existed. C-15 recorded in §11 that the gate stops the import and does not clear what was stored; with C-16 unbuilt no Shaman file is ever written, so the only thing that could have replaced those rows is the one thing the gate refuses. Nothing was ever going to take them off the screen.
  - **So the store is swept, at login, whichever way the gate answered.** `Companion.DropForeignImports()` runs after `CharacterRefusal` has said its line and before `ImportAll`. Both paths need it: the refused path is the owner's Shaman, where the file is the Druid's and so is what is stored; the imported path is the Druid himself, where sweeping FIRST means an arriving rating replaces nothing and is compared against nothing, so `Existing`, the `unchanged` branch and the stale-file comparison all see an empty shelf rather than a foreign one.
  - **Each store owns its own walk, and that is why there are two functions rather than one.** `QEImport.Forget(shouldDrop)` sweeps the four Top Gear shelves - `qeImport`, `qeImports`, `qeImportsByScenario` and C-11's `qePassesByScenario` - and `UFImport.Forget(shouldDrop)` sweeps the Upgrade Finder's own three, `ufImport`, `ufImports` and C-7's `ufImportsByLevel`. The shapes are the stores' and nothing outside them should have to know there are seven shelves; the Upgrade Finder half is NOT a second call into QEImport's, because none of its shelves is a Top Gear shelf and a document is keyed by content type AND key level. **Each counts DISTINCT verdicts by table identity**, because one rating is on three shelves at once: two ratings gone are two, not six. Neither knows what makes a rating foreign - the predicate is the caller's.
  - **How a stored rating's source and its character are told apart, in that order.** `Companion.IsForeignImport(verdict)` asks `SourceOf(verdict) == SOURCE_COMPANION` first, off the `source` field, and never off the absence of a `character`. **A paste carries no character and never will** - the player went and got that export and put it in the box on this character himself, which is his own act - so a rule keyed on the missing field would throw away every paste in the game. Only a companion import can sit in `db.char` without anyone having chosen it here. Who it is for is then C-15's own `Companion.CharacterClause(verdict.character)`, the SAME function the file gate calls, so a stored rating and a file on disk can never disagree about whose they are: no `character` at all is somebody else's (every import stored before C-15), another name or realm is somebody else's, a class that contradicts is somebody else's, and a client that names nobody yet - which `ADDON_LOADED` can be - drops nothing at all.
  - **One line, once, only when something went:** `dropped a rating that wasn't for this character - /lootpath refresh to rate this one`, on `ns.Companion.DROPPED_LINE`. What happened and the one thing that fixes it; no source named, nothing about a file on disk, no offer to repair anything, and never the word "plan". A login that dropped nothing says nothing, which is every login on a rated character.
  - **`RoadsCache.Changed()` after a drop**, as an import calls it (R-2), and for the sharper reason: the cache may already hold roads built from the rating that has just gone, and a hover would otherwise carry it. The window is redrawn too, but only if it is already open.
  - **Nothing else is touched.** `db.global`, the flush, the file gate, the import path and the paste path are unchanged, and inside `db.char` so are `upgradeMap`, `equipNow` and the folds: which slot sections the reader has shut is a fact about this character and has nothing to do with whose rating was stored.
  - **The Upgrade Finder store needed its own path but not its own rule.** The issue left open whether it would; it does, because its three shelves are its own, and it does not, because a Top Gear rating and an Upgrade Finder document written by one companion file name the same character and are dropped by one predicate.
  - **Not on a real screen.** Twenty guards proven red over the stub, including the owner's case end to end (the Shaman's login refuses the file AND empties the store). What no test here can say is how the empty Equip Now and the one chat line read at a login the player asked nothing at.

**2026-09-18 (C-16, WKE-619) - QE Live values the character its own header names, so the driver names it before it imports. Through his control, once, read back, and said on the log every run.**

  - **What the owner saw.** `main` `4279b37`, the C-15 companion running since 14:20 local, logged in as his Restoration Shaman and refreshed. `Data/companion.log` at 19:30:20Z and 19:30:57Z, twice the same: `profile: 16 equipped, 17 in bags, 0 in the bank, 0 vault, 99 lines`, `fork already serving http://localhost:3000`, `welcome dialog: none, the browser profile remembered the character`, then `FAILED: QE Live refused the profile: You're currently a Restoration Druid but this SimC string is for a different spec.` and `warning: that run failed with exit code 5; the previous verdict file is untouched`. No Shaman rating has ever been written on that machine.
  - **The cause, and how long it had been there.** `checkSimCValid` (`SimCImportEngine.ts:354`) tests the SimC header's class line against the ACTIVE character's spec string and `:360` writes the message above. The driver had exactly one place where a class was ever named - `dismissWelcome`, which runs only when the welcome dialog is up, which with a persistent browser profile is once ever - and **no caller had ever passed one**, so `opts.className || 'DRUID'` was the whole of it. The fork was on a Restoration Druid because that is what the owner's browser profile was set to and nothing had asked it to be anything else since.
  - **His control, not his storage.** The spec lives in local storage (`PlayerChars.saveAllChar`), and writing it there would be patching his app from outside. The driver uses what a player uses: the header's `Current Spec` MUI `Select` (`QEHeaderClassSelector.js:37` for its label, `:38-60` for the menu), whose `onChange` is `QEHeader.js:134`'s `props.handlePickPlayerSpec` - `App.tsx:273-277`, which finds the character of that spec and makes it active. Nothing of his source is copied and nothing is edited (§8: read, never copy).
  - **The name is built from the client's two halves, and the class half is the only table restated.** `identity.class` is `UnitClass`'s TOKEN (`SHAMAN`) and `identity.spec` is the spec's NAME (`Restoration`), which are C-15's two fields; QE Live spells the pair as one string (`Restoration Shaman`). `fork.js`'s `QE_CLASS_WORD` is six tokens to six words and nothing else, because requirement 3 - a class he has no character for is refused **before a browser is opened** - cannot be answered off a page that is not open. Which SPECS he rates is never restated: that is settled against his own menu, and a spec it does not offer is exit 5 with both names in the line.
  - **One lookup for the welcome tile and the menu item.** Both start from the same name. His tiles are captioned by `getShortClassName` (`Welcome.tsx:72-76`), which prints `H Priest`, `D Priest` and otherwise the spec name's second word - so `welcomeTileLabel("Restoration Shaman")` is `Shaman` and `welcomeTileLabel("Holy Priest")` is `H Priest`. The old call passed a class TOKEN into a case-insensitive `^...$`, which matched his `Druid` tile by luck and would have matched **no tile at all** for a Priest.
  - **Read back, and asked once.** `handlePickPlayerSpec` falls back to index 0 when no character of that spec exists (`PlayerChars.ts:155-163`); that cannot happen today because `init` auto-adds every missing spec (`:44-54`), but a click that did not take would otherwise import against a character nobody chose, so the header is read again and a disagreement is `DRIVE`. And the driver **does not loop**: a `different spec` refusal after the switch is still one `REFUSED` at exit 5 carrying QE Live's own words, because asking the same question twice would only put his sentence on the log twice.
  - **Two of his controls, one of them rendered twice.** `QEHeader.js` draws its `drawer` inside a `keepMounted` mobile `Drawer` (`:297`) AND in the desktop `Grid` (`:315`), so `Current Spec` matches two controls at every width and one is `display: none`. The driver finds the VISIBLE one rather than taking `.first()`, and a header with none visible, or none at all, is a named `DRIVE` failure.
  - **Scaled down, and said in the PR.** His check is on the CLASS, not the spec - line 354 asks whether the active character's spec string contains the header's class word - so a Holy Priest profile would have imported cleanly against a Discipline Priest and the issue's "a different spec" framing is half right. The switch is still made when either half differs, because the numbers are the selected SPEC's model (§4, 2026-09-08), and being refused was never the only way to get a wrong answer.
  - **Not on a real fork yet.** Every figure here is read off his source or asserted against a page double; no browser was opened by this session and the owner's own watcher and fork were never touched. The owner restarts the watcher, refreshes on the Shaman and then on the Druid, and the log's own `character:` lines are the proof.
**2026-09-18 (R-7d, WKE-621) - an age on screen belongs to the thing the words name. `last rated` is the age of THIS character's rating; the account's newest gear read is the gate, never the clock.** The owner read both screenshots on the WKE-592 walkthrough, `main` `4279b37`: `your gear wasn't read at logout - last rated 73 seconds ago` on a Restoration Shaman whose gear has never been rated (its run failed, `companion.log` 19:30:58Z), and `last rated 75 seconds ago` on the Druid whose rating on screen was written 2026-09-17T01:14:58Z - the file on disk. Both numbers were the Shaman's refresh capture.

  - **The cause, and the distinction it missed.** `Drift.gearUnreadText` formatted `STRIP_GEAR_UNREAD` / `LOAD_GEAR_UNREAD` with `inventory.capturedAt` from `Companion.GearUnreadAtFlush()` - the newest `inventory` snapshot in `db.global.captures`. That store is ACCOUNT-wide and that snapshot is a READ of the gear, not a rating of it. R-7c wrote it that way on purpose ("the newest stored read's, because that read is what the plan on screen is about"), and on one character it was very nearly right; on an account with two, it says another character's clock in a sentence about this one. **Refuted here, and the refutation is the decision:** the newest read is not what the rating on screen is about.
  - **The gate and the clock are different questions.** `GearUnreadAtFlush` is unchanged and still the gate: it answers whether the last unload refused the gear, which is true of the CLIENT and worth saying to whoever is logged in. The clock is `Drift.PlanStamp()` - `verdict.companionWrittenAt or verdict.exportedAt` off `ns.UI.ActiveVerdict()`, stored in `db.char.qeImports`, per character - which is the thing the words claim and the same stamp `Tooltip.RATED_AGO` counts from, so the strip and the tooltip now say the same number.
  - **No rating, no age.** A character with nothing stored gets the fact and nothing else: `your gear wasn't read at logout`. `last rated` with nothing rated is a number about somebody else, and silence would drop a fact the player needs. A stamp that cannot be parsed is treated as no rating rather than as a wrong second, the way `ns.EpochFromISO` is treated everywhere else.
  - **Two surfaces, one read (R-8's rule, kept).** Four constants now instead of two - `STRIP_GEAR_UNREAD_BARE`, `STRIP_GEAR_UNREAD`, `LOAD_GEAR_UNREAD_BARE`, `LOAD_GEAR_UNREAD`, the chat pair being the strip pair plus `GEAR_UNREAD_TAIL` - but still one helper and one age, so the strip clause and the login chat line cannot disagree about when the gear was last rated. The chat line keeps its tail in both cases, because the way out is the same whether or not anything has been rated.
  - **Unchanged on purpose:** the six decisions and their order, `Companion.GearUnreadAtFlush` itself, the Refresh button and its tooltip, `UI.StatusStripModel`'s handling of `gearClause`, and every word of the sentence other than where the age comes from.
  - **Not on a real screen yet.** The owner reads the strip on the Druid after a real logout: the age must be the rating's, matching the tooltip's `Rated ... ago` line, and on a character that has never been rated the clause must stop at `logout`.
**2026-09-18 (R-8a, WKE-618) - a control on a mouse-enabled row must be raised above it, or the row eats the click.** The owner, the afternoon of the day R-8 merged: "unable to refresh, nothing happens when I click it or any of the other buttons." His `/fstack` over `Refresh` on `main` `4279b37`, HIGH strata, top down: `LootpathMainFrame.NineSlice` at 500, then `LootpathMainFrame.statusStrip` at **2**, then `LootpathMainFrame.refreshButton` at **2**, then the button's own textures, `LootpathMainFrameText` at 2, and `LootpathMainFrame` at 1. The strip was above the button at the same level, so it took every press on all three.

  - **The cause is H-1a plus the strip's mouse, and both halves are correct on their own.** The strip is `EnableMouse(true)` with an `OnMouseUp` because M3-16b put the wait's click on the row the wait's sentence is written on. H-1a (WKE-606) moved `Options` and `Import...` off the strip and onto the FRAME, because a child of a hidden frame is hidden with it and those two stay on screen over the Coming soon screen; R-8 built `Refresh` the same way for the same reason. But a frame's default level is its PARENT's plus one, so the moment they stopped being the strip's children they stopped being above it: frame 1, strip 2, buttons 2. Before H-1a they were the strip's own children at 3 and the strip's mouse never mattered - which is why this was invisible for two issues.
  - **The fix is a level, not a re-parent.** `ns.UI.STRIP_BUTTON_KEYS` (`refreshButton`, `openImportButton`, `optionsButton`) and `UI.RaiseStripButtons(frame)`, which puts every key it names at `strip:GetFrameLevel() + 1`, guarded on the setter the way the file guards `SetEnabled` and `SetMotionScriptsWhileDisabled`. One list, so a fourth button on this row cannot forget. The parentage, the anchors, the sizes, the labels, the tooltips, the strip's mouse and its `OnMouseUp` are all untouched.
  - **It is re-asserted after the redraw's show.** `UI.RefreshStrip` raises again right after its own `statusStrip:SetShown`. The other `SetShown`, in `UI.ShowTab`, has no raise of its own: `UI.SelectTab` calls `UI.Refresh` straight after it and every path through the window reaches `UI.RefreshStrip`, so a third call is code no guard could prove red - the tab-click guard proves the click is covered by these two instead. **This is belt and braces, and said so on purpose:** the issue's premise was that "a frame shown after its same-level siblings is drawn - and hit - above them", and nothing under `.luals/` or in any committed fixture confirms or denies it. `SetFrameLevel`'s exported documentation (Frame.lua:441, SimpleFrameAPIDocumentation:1175) says nothing about show order at all. Re-asserting costs three assignments per redraw and is true whichever way the client behaves; the alternative would have been a guess.
  - **The stub learned frame levels for this.** `spec/stubs/wow.lua` had no `SetFrameLevel` and no `GetFrameLevel` - the issue said it recorded them and it did not - so a frame now carries `frameLevel`, defaulting to its parent's plus one, which is the relationship the owner's `/fstack` shows on the real client. That default is what makes the guards meaningful: with it, dropping the raise puts all three buttons at the strip's own level and the tests go red.
  - **The NineSlice at 500 is not the cause and was not touched.** `NineSlicePanelTemplate` declares `frameLevel="500" setAllPoints="true"` (`Blizzard_SharedXML/Mainline/SharedUIPanelTemplates.xml:381`); neither it nor `NineSlice.lua` enables the mouse, and Blizzard's own portrait frames take clicks through it.
  - **Not on a real screen.** Three clicks and one `/fstack` are the owner's, and §11 carries the general hazard.

**2026-09-18 (R-8, WKE-616) - a sentence that spells out a command beside the button that would run it is asking the reader to type what he could press. The strip's refresh becomes a button; the command stays in chat.** The owner read his own strip on `main` `fba70b3`, 2026-09-18 morning (the WKE-592 walkthrough, screenshot there): `your gear wasn't read at logout - last rated 15 hours ago · /lootpath refresh to rate what you wear now`. His words: "we should just make this a button that will run that command for the user when they click it."

  - **The button is a third `UIPanelButtonTemplate` on the strip's row**, `Refresh`, to `Import...`'s left, and its click is `ns.Drift.Click()` and nothing new. That is the one function M3-16b and `/lootpath refresh` already share: it reloads when a rating is waiting and runs `ns.Companion.Refresh()` otherwise. So the button gains no power - it is a second door onto a path that was already there, and an `OnClick` is the hardware event `ReloadUI` has required since M3-16a. Nothing about `Drift.Decide`, the six decisions, the wait's own strip click, the chat command or the nudge row changed.
  - **It is always on the row, in every state**, including over H-1's Coming soon screen, where `Import...` and `Options` already stay (H-1a): a refresh is never wrong to offer, and a press in a non-healing spec reaches `Companion.Refresh`, which refuses with the gate's own line, captures nothing and reloads nothing. In combat it is greyed out like the Equip buttons rather than left to be refused: `Companion.Refresh` would refuse anyway, and a button that looks pressable and is not is a worse answer than one that looks locked.
  - **The tooltip says what THIS press will do, not what the button is.** The two acts are not the same - one sends the gear away, the other brings a rating back - and both cost a reload, which is the fact worth saying before the screen goes dark: `rate what you wear now - takes a reload`, `load the rating that's ready - takes a reload`, and in combat `not in combat - the reload is blocked there`. One line, no source, and the word "plan" is not in any of them (the 2026-09-16 rule, guarded by `spec/voice_spec.lua`).
  - **The command comes off the STRIP and stays in CHAT.** `Drift.LOAD_GEAR_UNREAD` was one string on two surfaces; it is now two endings on one fact. The strip's clause stops at the age, because the button is a hand's width to its right. The chat line - said once at the login after a logout that read no gear, where there is no button on the surface at all - keeps a short tail that names the button first and the command second: `· Refresh in the window, or /lootpath refresh`. The age is one read either way, so the two cannot disagree.
  - **Scaled down, and said in the PR:** the issue asked for every other strip clause and the nudge row to be swept for a written-out `/lootpath refresh` the same way. Read against the code, there is nothing else to sweep. The only strip clause carrying the command was this one; `Drift.NUDGE_LINE`'s `click to refresh` names no command and its row IS a button already (R-6); the three other places the command is written in player-facing text - `Drift.LOAD_SKIPPED_EMPTY`, `Drift.LOAD_SKIPPED_SLOT` and the wait's chat line - are chat only, and the chat frame is exactly where the command belongs. `UI/VaultPanel.lua` and `UI/UpgradeMapPanel.lua` write it inside their own panels, which is not the strip and not this issue. **Also left alone on purpose:** the tooltip block's last line, `Rated 1h ago · /lootpath map` (UX-3, WKE-599) - a tooltip has no button to point at, which is the same reason the chat line keeps its tail.
  - **Not on a real screen yet.** Whether three buttons fit the row beside the facts at `UI.WIDTH` 760, and whether the greyed button reads as locked rather than broken, are eye tests: the owner logs in after a real logout, reads the strip without the command, presses Refresh and watches the reload come.

**2026-09-18 (C-15, WKE-615) - a rating is for ONE character: the verdict file names who it rated, the addon refuses it on anyone else in one line, and the spec check compares the class first.**

  - **What the owner saw.** 2026-09-18 morning, `main` `fba70b3`, an old Restoration Shaman logged in on the same account as his rated Druid: Equip Now showed `Nothing you're wearing is rated yet.` over fifteen `you don't own this` rows of Druid pieces beside the Shaman's own worn icons, and the status strip said `last rated 15 hours ago`. His words: "It looks as though it's trying to add items from 'hotornot' my druid." (WKE-592 finding, screenshot there.)
  - **The cause, and what it was NOT.** `Companion.Startup` calls `ImportAll(ns.companionVerdict)` at load for whichever character is logging in, and `QEImport.Store` puts the result in `db.char` - the RIGHT store, filled from the wrong file. `Data/QEVerdict.lua` is one file per machine, listed in the `.toc`, loaded by every character; it carried `writtenAt`, `companionVersion`, `profileCapturedAt`, `documents`, `qeSettings`, `excluded`, `scenarioNote` and `profileVaultCount`, and not one word about whose gear it was. The companion has always KNOWN - `tools/companion/lib/profile.js` builds `identity = { name, realm, spec }` out of the newest `env` capture - and simply did not say.
  - **Why nothing already in the addon caught it.** `SpecClause` compares `verdict.spec` against the live spec name by lower-case substring, and QE Live's own `player.spec` is `Restoration Druid` while the client's answer on the Shaman is `Restoration`: a containment either way is agreement, so the spec line never fired. H-1's healing gate let it through for the same kind of reason - a Restoration Shaman IS a healer, and the gate reads the ROLE. Neither is wrong; neither was ever about identity.
  - **The fix, one field and one gate.** The companion writes `character = { name = ..., realm = ..., class = ... }`. `name` and `realm` are the capture's own `UnitName("player")` and `GetRealmName()`; `class` is `UnitClass("player")`'s SECOND return, the class TOKEN, because the first is localised and no comparison may be built on it. `luawriter.render` **refuses** to write a file whose character has no name or no realm, the way it refuses a file with no documents. The addon reads it in `Companion.FileCharacter`, compares it in `Companion.CharacterClause` against `Companion.CurrentCharacter()`, and `Companion.Startup` runs that gate BEFORE `ImportAll` - because the failure being prevented is a STORE.
  - **The line, and that there is exactly one of it.** `this rating is for Hotornot on Area 52 - /lootpath refresh to rate this character`, in the addon's own voice: what it is, who it is for, and the one thing that fixes it. No source named, nothing about a file on disk, no "plan", and no offer to repair anything. `/lootpath status` says the same string. A file that names no character at all says `this rating doesn't say which character it's for - /lootpath refresh to rate this one`.
  - **A file with no `character` is refused, deliberately.** That is every file written before this one, including the one on the owner's disk right now. It is treated exactly as a mismatch is, and for the same reason: a rating that cannot say who it is for cannot be trusted to anyone. One `/lootpath refresh` replaces it, and the addon says so in the line itself.
  - **The class is compared before the spec name, and a class mismatch is never a spec line.** `SpecClause` now asks the character question first, off the `character` the import carries onto the verdict, and only then falls through to the substring comparison of spec NAMES. The substring match itself is kept untouched - it exists because the client and the export word specs differently (`Restoration` against `Restoration Druid`), which is R-7b's own entry - and the token is what the collision needed. Switching spec would not fix a rating for somebody else, so that case never says "switch and refresh".
  - **The client's nil is not a mismatch.** When `UnitName("player")` or `GetRealmName()` answers nothing - which at `ADDON_LOADED` it can - the gate is DOWN and behaviour is today's. A gate keyed on nil would refuse every file at the one moment it has nothing to go on, which is R-7b's and H-1's rule, applied again.
  - **The paste path is untouched.** A paste is the player's own act: he asked for THIS export on THIS character by pasting it. A verdict that carries no `character` - every paste, and every verdict stored before this - is not refused by `SpecClause` either.
  - **What is deliberately NOT built:** per-character verdict files. One file per machine is the contract (decision 2026-09-07), the companion is one watcher over one SavedVariables path, and the consequence is recorded rather than engineered around: the LAST character to refresh owns the file, and every other character keeps its own last import in its own `db.char` (11).
  - **Nothing new is drawn.** The Shaman sees exactly what a fresh character sees: no import, the empty states every tab already has, and the strip saying there is no rating. The loop, the flush, `db.global.captures`, H-1's role gate and `QEImport.Store` are all unchanged.

**2026-09-18 (M5-1c, WKE-617) - a row's note hangs off the LINE, and a row is as tall as what is drawn in it.** The owner's screenshot on WKE-592 (`main` `fba70b3`) had the not-owned sentence printed over the row's second line on all eight not-owned rows.

  - **The cause, read off the code and then off the stub.** `row.note` was anchored `TOPLEFT` to the row at `-ROW_HEIGHT` (38). On a row with no worn icon the item line started at `-2` and is 36 tall, so it ended at exactly -38 and the note began on the pixel the line ended on. On a swap-shaped row - which is every ghost row, because a ghost has a worn icon, an arrow and the empty item button - the line was anchored to `row.arrowText`'s `TOPRIGHT` plus (4, **6**), and `arrowText` is centred on the worn icon, which sits below the row's top: the line's top was BELOW -2 and its bottom well past -38, so the note was drawn over the line's own second line. The row's height was `ROW_HEIGHT` plus `NOTE_HEIGHT` - a constant plus a constant, never where the line actually ended.
  - **A line reports its height.** `ItemLine.Height(size)` is the taller of the icon column and the name-plus-second-line column, plus the frame's two points of clearance: `math.max(size, 16 + 1 + 14) + 2`. At the default 34-point icon that is **36**, exactly what `Create` already set the frame to, so no existing caller moves; at the Vault tab's 32 it is 34, also unchanged. Below 31 the text column wins, which is the case the old `size + 2` got wrong and nobody had hit.
  - **One vertical rule for both layouts, which is decision 3 of the issue answered YES.** The line's `TOPLEFT` is the ROW's `TOPLEFT` at `-LINE_TOP` (2) on every row; a pair only moves it right by `PAIR_INSET` = `WORN_ICON_SIZE + ARROW_GAP + ARROW_SIZE + LINE_GAP` = 24 + 2 + 16 + 4 = **46**. The `+6` that lifted the line above the arrow is gone, and the arrow is centred on the line instead of the line hung off the arrow: `row.worn` is anchored at `-(LINE_TOP + (ItemLine.ICON_SIZE - WORN_ICON_SIZE) / 2)` = -7, where it used to sit at -4, and the arrow is still `LEFT` of the worn icon's `RIGHT`, so it follows. The branch in `anchorLine` is deleted; one `paired and PAIR_INSET or 0` is all that is left of two layouts.
  - **The note begins where the line ends.** `row.note` is `TOPLEFT` to `row.line`'s `BOTTOMLEFT` at `-NOTE_GAP` (2), `RIGHT` to the row as before, still no `SetWidth`. It narrows by the pair inset on a swap row, which is the sentence sitting under the item it is about rather than under the row's left edge.
  - **And the row is as tall as that.** `EquipPanel.RowHeight(hasNote)` = `LINE_TOP + ItemLine.Height()` (+ `NOTE_GAP + NOTE_HEIGHT` with a note). Measured over the owner's own export on the stub: a row with a note **54 -> 56**, a row without one **38 -> 38**, the list's height **652 -> 656**, the note's top **-38 -> -40**. `ROW_HEIGHT` stays at 38 as the frame's build default and the list's pre-draw size, with a guard holding it to `RowHeight(false)` so the two cannot drift. The overflow line's 4-point gap is counted into `used` with the line itself, which it was not before.
  - **What was NOT touched:** `Describe`, `Drawn`, the marks, the bar, the fold, `Equip`/`EquipAll`, the note's words, and every number on screen. This is anchors and heights only.
  - **One premise scaled down:** the issue asks for tests in `spec/ui_spec.lua` / `spec/equippanel_spec.lua`; the second file does not exist in this repo, so the seven guards are in `spec/ui_spec.lua` (six) and `spec/itemline_spec.lua` (one).

**2026-09-17 (UX-3, WKE-599) - the voice is reopened on purpose: the tooltip block is rewritten short, warm and plain, and "the plan" leaves every screen.** What changed is the SHAPE and the TONE of surface 1 and one word everywhere; the principles behind them stand. `docs/ROADS-UX.md`'s surface 1 and "Copy voice" are rewritten to match, and principle 16's "the plan comes first" keeps its meaning and loses the word.

"There is a lot of text and this sounds very AI written. It needs to be short, concise, warming to the player and easy for them to understand what this is trying to tell them." Every one of those six lines was surface 1 as written and as amended by R-2a, built to the letter. **The letter is what read as machine-written**, which is why this entry exists rather than a defect.
  - **The copy set was approved BEFORE anything was built.** Step 1 wrote every block the addon can produce, as it would read, in an 18-case table on the issue, with the seven readings the brief did not settle spelled out and the alternative named for each. The owner, 2026-09-17: "I'm good with all recommendations." So the table is the specification and this build is its execution; the readings are his, not the build's.
  - **The block, in four lines at most.** `Lootpath · <slot>` and nothing else. Then the item's part of the plan as one warm plain sentence a friend would say - verb first, the reason after a dash, second person, no fragments, no middots, a number only when it IS the reason (`Keep these on.`, `Pass - use your Dreamwatcher legs.`, `Catalyst these - tier shoulders.`, `Grab this - crest it after.`, `Crest these to 321 - then refresh.`). Then the ONE other road that GAINS, as `Better: <item> (<level>), <badge> · <instance>, <difficulty>`. Then `Rated 1h ago · /lootpath map`, the age in the shortest unit rounded down and the one place a command lives.
  - **What was CUT rather than shortened.** The four honesty phrases lose their line: three of the four are not actionable from a tooltip and the fourth's cure is on line 4. That makes the "new since the last refresh", "beyond the rating's item limit" and "no rating" blocks read identically, which is the honest consequence of the trade and which the owner accepted with his eyes open (reading 3 named it and offered the alternative). The sub-header goes with the roads it headed. "Why this?" goes and its DESTINATION stays, on line 4 - principle 9 wanted the destination, not the question. The item's own road line goes for anything you hold, because it restated the sentence above it. **And one thing came ON:** the crest quote (M3-17b), on the one road whose cost the vendor has actually quoted, because since that capture it is the only fact on that road a reader can act on; the money is dropped, being never the reason you would or would not crest. R-2a's rule stands everywhere else, and the panel keeps every clause the block drops.
  - **`/lootpath refresh` follows `staleBags` and not the strip's amber.** The brief said "when the strip is already amber"; those are two different facts (`slotRoads.staleBags` is "this slot's bags hold something the rating never saw"; `VaultPanel.IsVerdictStale` is "the export predates the weekly reset") and they fire at different times. Reading 6 kept today's rule, because it is the one that means the rating is behind the world in THIS slot - which is why the owner's own two hovers end on `/lootpath map`.
  - **The plural is the garment's.** "Keep these on." over leggings and "Keep this on." over a chest, off `ns.Roads.SLOT_PLURAL` - the five slots whose word in `SLOT_WORD` is already a plural. A slot that table does not name is singular, and nothing is guessed.
  - **Three of the table's own renderings were corrected against the code**, and each correction is in §0 and the PR: the bag pick's percent (row 3) is a figure no document carries, so the sentence names what comes off without one; `The Coiled Altar` is the BOSS and the instance is `The Venomous Abyss`, so the stated rule (the instance alone) renders that, with the client's own difficulty label unshortened; and the crest road is never one of a worn piece's "other" roads on the committed week, so row 15's line is built and tested off the vendor transcript rather than found on a hover.
  - **The no-"plan" rule is global and guarded.** The owner, 2026-09-16: never say "the plan", "your plan" or "this plan". `spec/voice_spec.lua` fails on all three in any player-facing string, in both halves, and `spec/tooltip_spec.lua` fails on them in any tooltip block over the owner's week. **The guard's constant half had to grow to catch the first thing it was pointed at**: `ns.Drift` and `ns.Companion` were outside the walk, which is how `rated just now; the plan is current.` sat on three surfaces while this file passed - the rendered half never reaches a load line, because a load line is said once, after a refresh, on the reload. Both modules are in the walk now.
  - **What the word became, one surface at a time.** The load lines and the nudge and the spec-mismatch line say `rating` or `what you have` (`rated just now; you're up to date.`, `your gear changed since this rating (2 items)`, `you're in Guardian; this rating is for Restoration Druid`). The bag diagnosis says `the map`. `no plan stored` is `no rating stored`. The Vault tab's R-3d headline is `Your vault was generated after this rating. Refresh.` The charge footnote is `You could catalyst ... too`. **And the scenario NAME is `this week's picks`** - the internal key `thisWeek` is untouched, and the Explain glossary word moves with it (`picks:` instead of `plan:`), because the word Explain matches has to be a word that is on the screen.
  - **`ns.Roads.ItemSentence` is still the one place a case is decided**, and `ns.UI.Tooltip.Lines` is still the one model the tooltip and every text test read. The road model is unchanged; the one field added is on a STEP, not on a road - the crest cost step now carries its own tooltip form of the quote, built by the same formatter as the row's, so the two cannot quote different figures.

**2026-09-17, evening (UX-5, WKE-614 BUILT) - the by-run view is Run Tiles, the header is one row, and two of the direction page's own figures were corrected by measurement.** What shipped is the five answers as the owner gave them: the drawer lists rated drops only, four tiles across, Crafting is the four-icon mosaic, Delves is `ui-journeys-delve-card` with that mosaic as its fallback, and the answer sentence has one form per source kind. **2026-09-17 (M5-2c, WKE-609) - the window is 760 wide, the addon is dark only, and the vault grid gets the space it was already sitting in.** The owner answered M5-0's window question on WKE-598 on 2026-09-16 night, question 5 of five: **"keep it dark and grow to 760."** That closes what M5-2 left open on 2026-09-09 - the window had stayed at M2-2's 620 x 640 while the mockups were drawn at 760 because nobody had answered - and it closes the light-skin half too. **No light skin is ever built.** The UX-2 canvas drew both; the addon is dark, the way the client is. There was no half-built light-skin token to remove: grepped, there is none. Four things were settled while building it.

  - **The height did not move, and nothing asked it to.** The answer was about width. 640 still holds the body every panel draws into, so growing it would have been this session's opinion rather than the owner's.
  - **One width, and every panel derives from it.** `UI.PANEL_WIDTH` = `UI.WIDTH` - `UI.PANEL_INSET_LEFT` - `UI.PANEL_INSET_RIGHT` = **734**, which is exactly what the window's two corner anchors give a tab's panel (the strip starts `UI.STRIP_INSET` = 12 in, a panel hangs two points further in off its BOTTOMLEFT, and a panel's BOTTOMRIGHT is 12 in from the frame's right). Those two margins are now the ONLY numbers in a panel's width that are not derived from `UI.WIDTH`, and the anchors themselves are written in the same constants, so the arithmetic and the geometry cannot drift apart. The three 620-era constants are gone: `EquipPanel`'s 560 and the `UI.WIDTH - 32` the window handed it, and the 560 `UpgradeMapPanel` and `VaultPanel` each kept. **The window no longer hands a panel a width at all** - a second copy of one number is only somewhere for the two to disagree.
  - **A panel's default is what its anchors would have made it, and the rows follow the panel at layout time.** In the client two corner anchors size a panel and a `SetSize` at Create is overridden; headless, the stub resolves no anchors and the `SetSize` is all there is. Making the default equal the anchors' own answer is what lets a render test build a panel on its own and still be measuring the window's geometry. Equip Now's rows go further and re-read `panel:GetWidth()` on every refresh, falling back to the Create default while the client has not laid the panel out yet.
  - **The vault's content frame tracks its scroll frame, and the scrollbar's inset is not taken off twice.** The scroll child was created at `PANEL_WIDTH - 40` = 520 and never resized - the defect V-5a's agent found on 2026-09-16 and left, because it was sizing and not art. `Panel.ContentWidth` asks the scroll frame, because the 26 points the scrollbar wants are ALREADY in that frame's own BOTTOMRIGHT anchor, so its width is the usable span; the panel's own width less `SCROLL_INSET` is the fallback for the state the client has not laid out yet, which is also the only state a headless test can be in. `Panel.Refresh` re-asks it every draw. **Measured after the change: the content frame is 708 wide and each of the three cells 186, against 124 while it was frozen at 520.** The banner keeps V-5a's 132: the room the window gained goes to the cells, which is the side V-5a had to squeeze. One consequence, recorded because it moved a V-5a guard: at 620 the cell was narrow enough that a cell background's WIDTH decided the atlas's fit; at 760 the height does, so the art now fills the cell's height and stops short of its width. Same one scale factor, other binding side.

**2026-09-17 (UX-4b, WKE-611) - Lootpath owns a shape and a colour, and both were measured before they were drawn.** The owner answered WKE-602's four questions: candidate **A, the Waymark**; "I'd like to have our own branded color"; the spec icon stays on the minimap launcher (593 stands); and a name-mark "with our own branded font".
