  - **The colour is `#FF1A8C`, and it was chosen by arithmetic rather than by eye.** A sweep of 4,800 colours was scored on two numbers at once: WCAG contrast against the two grounds a mark lands on, and CIEDE2000 distance from every colour it must not be read as. The forbidden set is the client's own item qualities (poor, common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary, artifact, heirloom - taken both as the client's canonical hexes and as the copies Baganator keeps in `API/ItemButton.lua:19-27`), QE Live's `#FFDF14` and `#C16719`, plain red, and the two neighbours in the bag corner. **Those two were decoded, not guessed:** `Pawn\Textures\UpgradeArrow.tga` - the file Baganator's own `API/Pawn.lua:93-100` names for its corner widget, so it is literally the art two corners away - is a 32-bit RLE TGA whose brightest green is **#42FD02**, and `Pawn\Textures\PawnIcon.tga` is **#A4DBFF**. Neither addon sets an RGB for its mark; both bake it into art, which is why reading the files was the only honest way to get the number. The winner's worst confusion is **epic purple at CIEDE2000 25.2** and its contrast is **5.34** on the near-black keyline and **3.63** on white, so it reads on the dark bag ground and on Blizzard's pale frame both. The whole magenta-rose band is the free space in the client's colour vocabulary; nothing in WoW's quality ladder is pink.
  - **QE Live's gold keeps its job, and that is why the mark gives it up.** R-2b filled the bag mark with `ItemLine.TONE.better` so the mark and the Vault tab's pick edge would "mean the same thing in the same colour". What UX-4b separates is the two MEANINGS, which were never one: the gold says *better*, which is QE Live's word about an item, and the mark says *this is Lootpath*, which is about no item at all. Every number and the Vault tab's edge stay gold. **Nothing else on screen changed colour.**
  - **The colour lives once.** `ns.UI.BRAND_HEX` in `UI/ItemLine.lua` - the file that owns hex-to-tint and loads first - and every surface that draws a mark tints a white texture with it. Changing the brand is a one-line edit, which is what "we can iterate" needs. The two textures that CANNOT be tinted where they are used (`mark64` behind the `.toc` icon line, `icon256` on the listing tile) carry the hex baked in, in `tools/media/svg/`, and moving the brand means moving it there too and re-rendering.
  - **The word is `Lootpath` in Alegreya SC Bold, SIL OFL 1.1** (`tools/media/fonts/`, from `google/fonts/ofl/alegreyasc`). It is a small-caps face, so the name sets itself as a full cap L with small caps after it - spelled, not shouted. **The licence line went into `Lootpath/Libs/LICENSES.md` in its own commit, before the font or any render of it entered the repo**, which is the rule that file exists for. The face is dev-time only: it is rendered into textures and the shipped zip carries no font. Bitter, which the proposal page set its own headings in, was the first candidate and was dropped for a measured reason - `google/fonts` ships it only as a variable font (`Bitter[wght].ttf`), as it does Cinzel, and resvg's variable-font support is not something to bet a wordmark on; Alegreya SC and Spectral SC still ship static Bold files.
  - **The renderer is resvg through Node, and it was picked by looking.** The machine has no Inkscape, no ImageMagick and no `resvg` on `PATH` (`C:\WINDOWS\system32\convert.exe` is Windows' NTFS converter, not ImageMagick's), and Node 22.15.0 was already there. `@resvg/resvg-js` 2.6.2 (MPL-2.0) installs with a prebuilt Windows binary. It writes PNG and the client does not read PNG, so `tools/media/render.mjs` takes its RGBA pixmap and writes the TGA itself: **uncompressed 32-bit BGRA, bottom-left origin, descriptor 0x08**, which is the shape Pawn's own shipped TGAs carry. Power-of-two sides, refused at render time if not. Never a `.blp` - the client reads TGA unconverted and a BLP would need a tool nobody here has. `npm install && npm run render` under `tools/media` is the whole re-render.
  - **`SIZE` went 15 to 16, which is R-2b applied to art.** `mark16.tga` is sixteen texels square, drawn on a 16-unit grid as its own reduced form - one thick chevron - rather than a 64-point drawing shrunk. A mark drawn at 15/16 of itself is a mark nobody drew. The badge is the same `mark16` and NOT `mark64`, for the same rule: it is nine points, and the 16 is the nearer drawing.
  - **The `.toc` line is `## IconTexture: Interface\AddOns\Lootpath\Media\mark64`, and it is the mark rather than the tile for a read reason.** Blizzard's `AddonList.lua:376` and `AddonCompartment.lua:86` read that one metadata key, and the compartment's own initialiser does `texture:SetSize(16, 16)`. A 256-point tile with a wordmark in it, drawn at sixteen points, is a smudge. So the compartment entry that had no icon at all now has the mark, and `icon256.tga` stays what it is - the tile the addon site shows.
  - **The version left the title.** The title is the name-mark and carries no words, so `UI.VersionText()` is the last line of the status strip's tooltip - which is where a reader already goes to ask how old any of this is. It is never on the strip's own line, which is for facts that change.
  - **Three premises of the issue did not survive the code, and the built thing is narrower than the asked thing in each.** (a) The issue said the Blizzard bag adapter draws `WHITE8X8`. It did not: it drew `evergreen-weeklyrewards-reward-selected` stretched over the whole item button with `SetAllPoints` - the same 214 x 121 banner R-2b took OUT of the Baganator corner for being a smear, left behind in the one adapter R-2b did not touch. Both adapters now draw the same Waymark, the same 16 points, in the same top-right corner, and the tests assert the two adapters' constants are equal. (b) The issue said the listing icon is wired "via `.pkgmeta` / the packager". It is not: `.pkgmeta` has no key for a project icon and the BigWigs packager sets none - the tile is uploaded on the addon site by the owner. What `.pkgmeta` DOES settle is that nothing under `Lootpath/` is ignored, so the whole `Media/` folder ships with no change at all, and a test reads `.pkgmeta` and proves it. (c) The issue said `## IconTexture` should name `icon256`; the 16 x 16 above is why it names `mark64` instead.
  - **What was NOT done, deliberately.** The minimap launcher's icon is untouched (593, and the owner's own answer 3). No frame is reskinned and no second meaning is added, so `docs/UI-POLISH.md` 4f and `docs/ROADS-UX.md`'s "no custom skin" are read exactly as the proposal read them - 4f's own "the badge is the one shape a reader learns once" is the thing being drawn, and 4f's last sentence, that the accent colour is QE Live's gold, is now half true and is superseded here for the MARK only.
  - **`spec/media_spec.lua` checks the art as files, because pixels are the owner's.** It parses each shipped TGA's 18-byte header - image type 2, no colour map, 32 bpp, descriptor 0x08, the declared size, both sides powers of two, and a byte count that is exactly header plus four per pixel - proves no `.blp` exists, proves the `.toc`'s icon line names a file that is there and carries no extension, proves `.pkgmeta` ignores nothing that would drop the folder, proves the font's licence line is present, proves no font is inside the shipped folder, and walks `ns.UI.MEDIA` asserting every constant points at a file on disk. **12 guards proven red.**

**2026-09-16, night (V-5, WKE-600) - the Vault tab's grid is Blizzard's Great Vault, read live, and two of the issue's own premises did not survive the code.** The owner had both windows open side by side: Blizzard's with row art, a lock and a fraction on every cell, one Dungeons cell unlocked and glowing at `Mythic 10`; Lootpath's with nine flat dark cells carrying a threshold sentence each and nothing else, under `The vault hasn't generated this week's rewards yet. Open the Great Vault once, then refresh.` - with that very window open on the other monitor. His words: "I'd love to see our vault page mimic what Blizzard's looks like, and be up to date... More focus on imagery and simplicity to convey maximum knowledge to the player."

  - **The decision is mirrored, not the pixels.** `WeeklyRewardsActivityMixin:Refresh` (`.luals/` `Blizzard_WeeklyRewards.lua`) branches on exactly one line - `self.unlocked or self.hasRewards` - and sets one of two atlases. `Panel.Cell` now copies that line as a line and names the same two atlases, plus the `activities-icon-checkmark` tick that mixin shows on the same condition, plus the corner text `:SetProgressText` writes: nothing while a cell holds a reward, the level text once it is unlocked, the client's own `GENERIC_FRACTION_STRING` fraction otherwise - and nothing at all on an incomplete cell while `CanClaimRewards()` is true, which is what Blizzard does too. Every FrameXML global and every atlas is asked for at runtime; a build without one loses a word or a texture, never the cell.
  - **A Heroic dungeon week and a Mythic one are both `level = 0`,** which is `WeeklyRewardsUtil`'s own recorded comment (`HeroicLevel = -1, MythicLevel = 0`, "in activity data both of these are level 0 and are differentiated by difficultyID"). So the tell is asked for - `C_WeeklyRewards.GetDifficultyIDForActivityTier(activityTierID)` against `DifficultyUtil.ID.DungeonHeroic`, exactly as `IsCompletedAtHeroicLevel` asks it - and never inferred from the level.
  - **The row art IS reachable by atlas, against the issue's own fallback.** The issue allowed for the Raids / Dungeons / World backgrounds being addon-private files. They are not: `WeeklyRewardsMixin:OnLoad` passes `evergreen-weeklyrewards-category-raids`, `-category-dungeons` and `-category-world` to `SetUpActivity`, which sets them on the row header's Background. The XML declares that texture with no `atlas` and no `file`, so those three Lua strings are the entire source. Lootpath draws them, and the `-header` / `-divider` fallback the issue described was not needed.
  - **Premise refuted: `claimID` is not a claimed marker.** The issue proposed reading a claimed cell off "`claimID` set on any activity". On the owner's own 2026-09-08 transcript `claimID` equals `id` and is present on every activity that HAS a reward, at a moment when `CanClaimRewards()` was true and nothing had been claimed. It names the reward a claim would ask for. `Modules/Vault.lua` records it as the client gives it, a guard in `spec/vault_spec.lua` pins that reading, and the claimed question stays exactly where V-3 (WKE-587) put it: the addon's own snapshot memory.
  - **Premise refuted: there is no claimed cell to draw, and Blizzard has no claimed treatment to copy.** The issue asked for the claimed reward drawn in its cell with "Blizzard's claimed treatment". `WeeklyRewardsActivityMixin` has no claimed branch at all - after `ClaimReward` Blizzard's own dialog calls `HideUIPanel(WeeklyRewardsFrame)` and the frame is never repainted - and a claimed week, by V-3's own definition, is one whose live option list carries NO rewards, so no cell holds a reward for such a treatment to land on. A claimed week therefore draws nine honest live cells and says what happened in V-3's own sentence. No fourth state was invented, and no dead branch was left behind.
  - **Premise corrected: the grid was already live.** The issue read `Panel.Model` as taking rewards from the newest `vault` capture. It does not and did not: `Panel.Gather` calls `ns.Vault.Options()`, which is `C_WeeklyRewards.GetActivities()` plus the three state reads, every refresh; the capture is used only for a pending reward's remembered NAME and for `ClaimedThisPeriod`'s memory, which is what the issue itself asked for. What was genuinely missing was three things, and those are what V-5 built: two unread client facts (`claimID`, the difficulty ID), one unread frame state (`AreRewardsForCurrentRewardPeriod`), and a redraw on the vault's own event.
  - **The window now redraws on `WEEKLY_REWARDS_UPDATE`,** which Blizzard's own frame re-reads on while it is shown. That is what makes the grid live rather than as-of-the-last-open. **Nothing about M3-16a/b moved:** no capture is taken on this path, and `C_WeeklyRewards.OnUIInteract` / `ns.VaultInteract` is not called from the grid, from `Vault.Options` or from the event - reading activities is free, GENERATING rewards is the one login ask and it stays there. A guard asserts zero calls on the stub's own `world.vault.interact` record, on the model path and on the drawn path.
  - **`AreRewardsForCurrentRewardPeriod` earns one sentence and no action.** `HasAvailableRewards()` true with it false is what Blizzard's own `UpdatePreviousClaim` puts its PreviousRewardNotification up on, and the tab had no way to say it: `Panel.PREVIOUS_PERIOD_NOTE` says the waiting rewards are an earlier week's and nothing about what becomes of them. Kept as the client gave it - nil is a client without the read and is not false - and `spec/helpers/replay.lua` was corrected to match: it turned an absent recording into `false`, which would have made the 2026-09-08 transcripts assert a period fact nobody ever asked the client for.
  - **The ungenerated sentence is reworded, because the owner read it beside the open window.** "Open the Great Vault once, then refresh" is the remedy for M3-16b's state - rewards the client has been told about but not given - and is still on `OPEN_VAULT_NOTE`, which is chosen first. The other state, a week that has simply earned nothing yet, now reads `Nothing to take from the vault yet this week. Each cell below shows what it still needs.` and points at a grid that, since this issue, carries every cell's own progress.
  - **The legend went, for simplicity.** `Rated options show their value. Other options are listed by item level only.` explained a badge that says it itself and cost the grid a line on a tab whose whole subject is nine cells. `Panel.NOTE` is gone, the header's note font string with it, and WKE-530 finding 3's guard - which kept the legend to exactly one - now keeps it at none, naming the sentence so putting it back anywhere fails.
  - **`Panel.Lines` is unchanged in shape** (M5-4's rule): the same notes, headline and per-option lines in the same order, with the reworded sentence and the one new note flowing through `NoteLines` so the text list and the grid cannot disagree. V-3's claimed line stays where V-3 put it, above the grid rather than below it, because moving it would be the only place the drawn tab and `/lootpath status` differ in order - see 11.
  - Ten guards proven red one at a time, restored with a clean tree between each: the no-`OnUIInteract` assertion, the locked/unlocked atlas choice, the corner fraction, Heroic-vs-Mythic, the row art, the legend's absence, the `WEEKLY_REWARDS_UPDATE` redraw, the reworded sentence, the previous-period note, and the `claimID` reading.

**2026-09-16, night (M5-1a, WKE-597) - Equip Now opens at its first row, and READING 1 held: a residual scroll offset, not the note line's height.** The owner's screenshot, bank closed, 15 already best: under the chips and the `(bank closed - open it to include bank items)` line the first visible row was Shoulder, cut off at the top, and Head was not on screen at all. The issue named two candidate causes and the stub decided between them before anything was built, which is the order this repo works in.
  - **The evidence, three probes over the drawn panel** (a throwaway spec, run and deleted; every figure printed by it). **(a)** `panel.scroll`'s top anchor was `TOPLEFT -> panel.summary BOTTOMLEFT, 0, -8` and the first row's was `TOPLEFT -> panel.list TOPLEFT, 0, 0` - **identical with the note line empty (bank open) and non-empty (bank closed)**. So the note's own height cannot move a row inside the list: an empty line could only move the WHOLE list up, showing more, never cutting its top. **That rules reading 2 out**, and the owner's screenshot had the hint on screen anyway. **(b)** Nothing ever set the offset: `panel.scroll.verticalScroll` was `nil` after a refresh, and an offset of `60` set before a refresh was still `60` after it. **(c)** Blizzard's own source, read from Ketho's annotations rather than guessed (`Blizzard_SharedXML/SecureScrollTemplates.lua`): `ScrollFrame_OnScrollRangeChanged` re-applies `math.min(scrollbar:GetValue(), yrange)` to the bar when the child is re-sized - it **clamps the offset, it never clears it** - and `UIPanelScrollBar_OnValueChanged` is `self:GetParent():SetVerticalScroll(value)`, so the bar is the authority and a frame scrolled to 0 over a bar still holding 60 does not stay at 0.
  - **What that makes the fix.** `EquipPanel.ScrollToTop` clears **both**: the bar's value and the frame's scroll. `EquipPanel.RowSignature` keys a row set by its slots and its rated items **in order, and by nothing else** - not the status, not the badge, not where the item is - so a new import or a different match starts at the top while equipping a swap, a bag update or a redraw in combat leaves a player reading half way down exactly where they were. `UI.ShowTab` to Equip Now starts at the top, because the offset survives the tab being hidden.
  - **And the half that holds whichever reading is right.** `EquipPanel.AnchorScroll` hangs the scroll frame's top off the LAST header element that actually has text - the note line when it has some, the chips when it does not, the header when there are no chips - at `EquipPanel.TOP_GAP`. An empty font string still occupies a line, and the top of the list must not depend on whether this character's bank happens to be open. The fixed `panel.summary` anchor in `Create` is gone; `Create` and every `Refresh` both call `AnchorScroll`.
  - **The owner's answer is still outstanding and cannot overturn this.** The question posted on the issue - does a wheel scroll UP bring Head back - would, if answered **no**, mean the offset was not what hid it; the anchor half already covers that case, and the remedy left over for it (an explicit height on the empty note line) would come back here as its own entry. Nothing here waits on it.
  - **The stub gained the template's own scroll bar**, modelled to those two handlers and no further: `UIPanelScrollFrameTemplate`'s `ScrollBar` (`@field ScrollBar UIPanelScrollFrameTemplate_ScrollBar : Slider`), whose `SetValue` records the value and pushes it into the parent's `SetVerticalScroll`. Its min/max are recorded and no range is invented, because no test reads one.
  - **Proven red, one at a time (seven):** the bar's `SetValue(0)` in `ScrollToTop`; the signature being recomputed at all in `Refresh`; the `signature ~= panel.rowSignature` test (every refresh jumps to the top and a bag update throws the reader back); the note-is-empty branch in `AnchorScroll`; the note-has-text branch; the `UI.ShowTab` hook; and the signature's status-independence (adding `row.status` to it). Each broken alone with the build already committed, run, and restored, with `git status` clean between them.
**2026-09-16 (H-1, WKE-596) - the healing gate, and why `nil` is not gated.** The owner, that evening: "Lootpath is strictly to help healers. When I change my spec, Lootpath still attempts to tell me in my bags and in the UI that I need to equip my healing gear. It should only do that in my healing spec. I'd like a Coming Soon screen for any other spec, and nothing about healing items when I'm not healing."

  - **Keyed on the ROLE the client names, never on a class.** `ns.Companion.CurrentRole` reads `GetSpecializationInfo`'s FIFTH return (Ketho's `SpecializationInfoDocumentation.lua:82-100`: `specId, name, description, icon, role, primaryStat, ...`), and `"HEALER"` is the string Blizzard's own frames compare against (`ClubFinder.lua:827`, `Blizzard_CompactRaidFrameManager.lua:1177`). `ns.Companion.HealingSpecName` walks `GetNumSpecializations()` (a global only - `Core/Data/Wiki.lua:5896`; `C_SpecializationInfo` has no twin of it) and asks about each index, so the sentence says `Restoration` for a Druid and the right word for a class Lootpath has never heard of, out of no table of ours.
  - **`nil` is NEVER gated, and this is the decision the rest rests on.** At `ADDON_LOADED` and at every flush the client names no spec at all - R-7b's own finding, measured on four real logouts - so a gate keyed on "not HEALER" would silence the whole addon at exactly the moments it has nothing to go on. An unknown role behaves as it did before H-1. Breaking that one test fails seven tests across the suite, which is the guard.
  - **The role is read live, on every ask, and nothing caches it.** The first build memoised the answer and dropped it on `PLAYER_SPECIALIZATION_CHANGED` / `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD`; the suite refused it - the R-7b tests set the spec after the load and the remembered answer was still the spec from before it. **A cache a test cannot see is a gate a test cannot prove.** The two events are what REDRAW the surfaces (the window registers one already, and `ns.Drift.EVENTS` gained it), which is a different job from reading the role.
  - **The capture is refused, not the read.** The `inventory` capture's `refuse` answers `you're in Guardian; Lootpath rates healing gear, so this read is not stored` on R-7b's own path: nothing stored, the newest good read stays newest, and a flush records it in `flushRefusals` on its `env` snapshot. `env`, `vault`, `currencies` and `upgrade` capture exactly as before - `env` is what records which spec it was. The companion is untouched (it rates the newest inventory read, which after this is always a healing one) and `profile.js`'s `specMismatch` stays as it is.
  - **R-7b's spec clause is not retired, but it no longer speaks in a gated spec.** The gate supersedes it there - the screen already names the spec, what is rated and the spec to switch to, so the strip drops the clause while the screen is up and one thing says it. The clause still says what it always said on the path that survives: a role the client does not name, off the newest `env` capture.
  - **What is silent, and where the gate is asked.** `ns.Glow.Wants` (one question, every bag adapter), `ns.UI.Tooltip.Answer` AND `Append` (the hover path and the Vault cell's own lookup), `ns.Drift.Check` (the nudge row, the minimap badge, and the bag marks already drawn, taken down on the spec change), `ns.Drift.LoadLine` (the screen's sentence and nothing else), `statusCommand` (that sentence first, everything it printed still printed), `ns.UI.ShowTab` / `Refresh` (the panels hidden, the tabs disabled, the screen drawn), and `ns.Companion.Refresh` (says which spec to switch to, returns before the first capture). The minimap icon keeps showing the current spec, which is 593's.
  - **One premise of the issue was refined and is recorded in the PR:** it asked for `UI.Tooltip.Available()` to answer false. `Available` is the CLIENT-capability probe `Install` reads once at load - making it role-aware would print `this client has no TooltipDataProcessor.AddTooltipPostCall` at a login in a tank spec and leave the post-call uninstalled for the session, so the block would not come back on a spec change without a reload. The silence is built where an answer is made instead, which is what the issue's own words ask for (no block, no header, no "Why this?").

**2026-09-16 (C-14, WKE-603) - the companion refuses a profile QE Live will not rate, and nothing it says is longer than a sentence.** The owner's screenshot at 16:30 read `your gear changed since this plan (54 items)`, and hovering it opened a tooltip the height of his screen ending in `locator.click: Timeout 20000ms exceeded`, Playwright's call log and its colour codes drawn as little boxes. Behind it, read from `Data/companion.log` and his own SavedVariables (committed as `spec/fixtures/captures/Lootpath-20260916-162655.lua`): his 16:26:34 reload flush stored `equipped 14` - inventory slot 7, legs, gone into a bag - and the companion rated that read twice, at 21:26:35Z and 21:27:30Z, dying both times after a minute of card selection.

  - **QE Live's rule is QE Live's, and it is cited rather than restated.** `src/General/Modules/TopGear/TopGear.tsx:852` is the button: `disabled={checkSlots(gameType).length > 0 || !btnActive}`. `checkSlots` (`:307`) counts the items a pass has SELECTED, skipping vault items, and names every slot standing at zero - Head, Neck, Shoulder, Back, Chest, Wrist, Hands, Waist, Legs, Feet at one each, Finger and Trinket at two. **The issue's citation was `checkTopGearValid` (`:208`), which is a different function**: it has weapons commented out and it only feeds `btnActive` (`:743`). The button's own expression calls `checkSlots`, which DOES count `2H Weapon`, `1H Weapon` and `Offhand`, with a rule at `:339-346` that a two-hander satisfies all three. So "weapons are NOT checked" is wrong about the button, and it is recorded here rather than built on.
  - **The weapon half is deliberately not mirrored, and the reason is a limit, not a preference.** A SimC profile carries `main_hand=` and `off_hand=` item strings and nothing that says which of the three kinds a main hand is. A companion-side weapon check would therefore refuse every two-hander in the game, and the owner plays a staff. The disabled button itself is the guard for that half.
  - **What the refusal is about is what is WORN.** A pass selects the equipped baseline plus whatever it clicked, so an empty worn slot poisons any pass whose clicks happen not to fill it - which is exactly what the log shows: passes 1 and 2 each clicked a Legs card and ran, and pass 3's 22 cards were the 14-piece baseline and eight trinkets, with no Legs among them. The pool had legs in it; the character did not. `lib/profile.js` `missingSlots()` reads the profile's own `equippedSlots` and the run stops before the browser with `refusing to rate a profile with an empty slot (legs); the previous verdict is untouched`, exit **9**, a `skipped` status carrying the slot name, and `log.skipped` rather than `FAILED:` - the sibling of R-7b's `emptyGear` in every respect.
  - **The driver never clicks a disabled button.** `lib/fork.js` `clickGo()` reads `isEnabled()` first and throws a one-sentence `REFUSED`-class error - `QE Live's Go! button is disabled for this pool - 22 of 30 selected, 14 baseline` - instead of retrying for twenty seconds. It is used at BOTH `Go!` sites, Top Gear and the Upgrade Finder: the same one-line refusal, and the Upgrade Finder had the same twenty-second hazard.
  - **A failure's `message` is one sentence, always.** `lib/status.js` has said "one sentence for the strip's tooltip" since C-9 and nothing enforced it. `oneSentence()` now takes the first line, strips `ESC [ n m`, caps at 200 characters and is applied in `status.failed` and again in `render`; the whole text stays in `companion.log`, which is where a reader who wants the call log should be. The addon caps too - `ns.Companion.OneLine`, same rule - because a status file written before this is still on the owner's disk.
  - **The nudge row's hover was already one line, and the premise is refuted.** `buildNudgeRow`'s `OnEnter` has only ever added `nudgeModel.text` and `nudgeModel.tooltip`, and the client dispatches `OnEnter` to the topmost mouse-enabled frame, so the row does not inherit the strip's. The dump in the screenshot is the STRIP's tooltip, one row up inside the same widget - the nudge row is a child of the strip and the strip grows to carry it. Nothing was changed for it; a guard was added instead, with a dump on the status file, and the cap above is what fixes the surface that really said it.
  - **The `54` is not the verdict's set, and that premise is refuted too.** `Drift.Compare` compares two LIVE scans: the baseline is whatever `Drift.Rebase` read at the first check of the session, not the plan's item list. Measured over his own file on 2026-09-16: the 15:29:53 read and the 16:26:34 read carry the **same 54 distinct gear keys** (equipped and bags, never the bank), 0 appeared and 0 went, and they differ by exactly one worn slot. So 54 is every key he owned, counted against an EMPTY baseline - a scan that ran before the client would answer about gear, the same silence R-7b and R-7c measured at the other end of a session.
  - **A read that is wearing nothing is not a baseline.** `Drift.IsReadable` refuses it in `Rebase` (nothing is stored, so the next check takes another one) and in `Check` (the last thing that was true stands). R-7b's rule, at the other end.
  - **And the count is what a player would count.** `Drift.Read()` returns `{ keys, slots }` off one scan; `Drift.CompareSlots` counts the worn slots that went bare or stopped being bare; `Drift.Compare` still counts the loose pieces that appeared or went; `Drift.CountText` says them apart - `(1 slot)`, `(2 items)`, `(1 slot and 1 item)`. **A swap is still not drift**, which is R-6's own decision and its own guard: the rating is made over the pool of everything the player can put on, so a piece moving between the bags and the character does not change the answer. Only the two edges are counted, and neither edge is a key `Compare` already counted. On the owner's two reads that is `(1 slot)`.
  - **The third `skipped` says what to do about it.** `Drift.LOAD_SKIPPED_SLOT` - `a gear slot was empty when your gear was read, so it couldn't be rated. Put something in that slot and /lootpath refresh.` - chosen by `ns.Companion.EXIT_EMPTY_SLOT`, never by reading the message, which is how the other two are chosen.
  - **Proven red, one at a time (thirteen), with the build committed first and `git status` between each:** the empty-slot refusal itself (3 of 7 emptyslot tests fail); QE Live's two-ring rule; the `isEnabled` read in `clickGo`; `oneSentence` in `status.failed`; `oneSentence` in `render` (3 tests, the golden among them); `Companion.OneLine` in `StatusTooltip` (the tooltip comes back seventeen lines with the escapes in it); the `EXIT_EMPTY_SLOT` clause in `StatusText`; its branch in `LoadLine`; `CompareSlots` in `Check`; the empty-read refusal in `Rebase`; the `IsReadable` guard in `Check` (which reports `{ count = 69, pieces = 54, slots = 15 }` - the bug itself); the `slot` wording in `CountText`; and the nudge row's hover, broken by giving it the strip's tooltip lines. All five gates green: 1273-plus busted and 253 companion tests.
  - **Never on a real screen:** every word of this. The owner restarts the watcher, equips legs, refreshes; then takes a piece off once and refreshes to see the refusal sentence.
**2026-09-16, night (M5-2b, WKE-601) - text that does not fit is moved or shortened by clauses, never cut mid-word.** The owner's screenshot of the Vault tab at his UI scale in the 620-wide window cut text in three places at once. Three decisions, one per place.

  (a) **The status strip moved DOWN, below the portrait ring, onto its own full-width row.** His words, 2026-09-16 16:30: "the copy is being covered by the Spec symbol in the top left corner - let's move it down". It had started at the frame's own left inset 30 points down, which is beside the ring, so the line's first characters were under it. The row now starts at the ring's bottom edge plus 4: the ring's bottom is 55 points under the frame's top, read from the template this window inherits - `PortraitFrameBaseTemplate`'s `PortraitContainer` sits on the frame's TOPLEFT at (0, 0) and its `portrait` texture is 62 x 62 anchored TOPLEFT at (-5, 7), `Blizzard_SharedXML/Mainline/SharedUIPanelTemplates.xml:544-566`, the same file and the same kind of read as the 58-point title inset already recorded here. Every tab's panel hangs off the strip's BOTTOMLEFT, so the body simply moves down with it; that cost is what the owner priced in.

  (b) **The line is fitted by dropping WHOLE clauses from the right.** `UI.StatusStripModel` now hands the drawer the clauses the line is made of and `UI.FitStripText` measures candidates against the row's real width with the client's own `GetStringWidth` (`FontString.lua:115`), returning the longest prefix that fits. The order is the one M3-16b / V-2 settled - spec, source and age, vault pick, companion - so the companion clause is the first to go and the spec the last to stay, and a wait or a spec/gear disagreement still takes the whole row alone. **Whenever anything was dropped, the WHOLE line heads the strip's tooltip**, the same move M3-16b and V-2 made with a fact before it: nothing is lost, it is one hover in. With no width to fit into - every headless caller, and a row the client has not laid out yet - nothing is shortened, which is exactly the behaviour before this issue.

  (c) **The Vault tab's closed dropdown says the scenario's PLAIN name; the menu keeps the sentence.** His screen read `Everything upgraded (Catalyst and f...`, because `DropdownSelectionTextMixin:UpdateToMenuSelections` (`Blizzard_Menu/MenuTemplates.lua:604-638`) writes the SELECTED ROW's own text on the control and that row carries the Settings page's explaining label. `SetSelectionText` (`MenuTemplates.lua:591`) is the template's own way to say otherwise - its answer wins over the row translation - so the caption is `as offered` / `catalyzed` / `this week` / `everything upgraded` and the explanation stays one click away, where the Settings page and the tab still agree word for word. The control is sized to the longest of the four names, measured through its own font string where there is one. Both calls stay inside `pcall`, for the same reason the `SetDefaultText` beside them does: a template that kept the name and dropped the mixin leaves a long caption, not a broken tab.

  (d) **The currency strip wraps.** His screen ended `... Veteran Mistcrest 35 · Champio`: the chips were laid left to right on one row with nothing measuring them. `Panel.ChipLayout` is pure - chips, the room the panel has, and a measure - and a chip that would cross the right edge starts the next row instead; the strip's own height follows the rows it took, and nothing under it needs that space. Headless, and wherever the client answers no width, a character estimate stands in and the layout is the single row it always was.

  (e) **The stub grew two modelled methods, both audited in `spec/stubs_spec.lua`** (the T-1 rule: a method is modelled when a panel calls it, and asserted absent on the widget that does not have it). `FontString:GetStringWidth` answers `Stub.CHAR_WIDTH` per character - proportional, never a claim about any font - and records every string it was asked about. `DropdownSelectionTextMixin:SetSelectionText` joins `SetDefaultText` on the same mixin, and `dropdown.stub:Caption()` reads the closed control's words the way `UpdateToMenuSelections` does: the selection function first, the selected row's text next, the default text last.
**2026-09-17 (M5-3b, WKE-608) - the link is right about the item and silent about the key level, so the row says the level in its own words.** The owner's check of M5-3a (2026-09-16 ~20:22, `main` 5034b30, after one `/lootpath capture journal` and a reload) hovered `War Trial Vestments` on the Upgrade Map by run - Den of Nalorakk, Mythic Keystone 10, the row drawn at **305** - and read `War Trial Vestments - Mythic+ - Item Level 292 - Upgrade Level: Champion 1/6`. The base-item 28 is gone and the right track shows, and **the tooltip's 292 is not the row's 305**. That is the §11 item M5-3a filed as unprovable headless, now measured by the one person who can: the journal link carries no explicit level (bonus 3524 alone, no modifier 9; the previewed level rides on the item context), the walk read 305 off it with the Adventure Guide previewing key 10, and a later `SetHyperlink` on the same link draws what the link says by itself.

- **The row says the level, and no link is ever built with a level modifier.** A hover on a drop whose level differs from what its link draws carries one grey line directly under the item: `Drops at 305 from a +10 · shown at 292 above` - the row's level, the key level the walk previewed, the link's own level. When they agree there is no line. A raid drop is read at no key level, so its wording names none (`Drops at 311 · shown at 292 above`). When the client will not answer, the line is `shown at its own level above` and nothing numeric: there is no second number, and neither one would have been read from anything.
- **One function decides which line a hover gets** - `ItemLine.LevelNote(item, linkLevel)` - for both this case and the link-less `levelNote` M5-3a added, which is the same mechanism's first case. `ItemLine.ShowTooltip` calls it once and draws whatever it returns in grey.
- **The link's own level is read at hover time**, `C_Item.GetDetailedItemLevelInfo(link)` (Ketho's `ItemDocumentation.lua`: `actualItemLevel, previewLevel, sparseItemLevel`), through the file's existing `probe` - `pcall` plus `ns.Safe`, like every other client read in `ItemLine.lua`. Nothing is asked of the client until someone hovers.
- **Only a drop row can ever get the line.** The row hands in `dropLevel` and `keyLevel` as their own fields rather than the hover reusing `itemLevel`, which every caller sets and the client often fills in itself; `candidateRow` sets both, `RoadRow` sets them on `KIND_DROP` alone, and no other tab passes them. Nothing changed about what the journal walk stores.
- **The key level is asked of the panel's one existing answer.** `Panel.RunKeyLevel(difficultyID, previewLevel, entry)` already decided whether a row was read at a key level and which one (and already honours an entry carrying its own, WKE-543); the hover asks it, and `Panel.BaseLevelNote` now goes through it too instead of its own copy of the rule. One behaviour change falls out: an entry with no difficulty at all gets the plain base-level wording rather than the previewed key level, because naming a +10 for a row whose difficulty is unknown would be a guess.
- **Proven red, one at a time, with the build committed first and `git status` clean between each (nine):** the keyed wording (2 failures, both specs); the equal-levels silence (2); the no-answer wording turned numeric; the drop-only gate (the hover falling back to `itemLevel`); `candidateRow`'s `keyLevel`; the difficulty test inside the key-level answer (2, one of them M5-3a's raid wording); `InitElement` handing the level on; `RoadRow`'s `dropLevel` on every kind of road; and `RoadRow`'s key level ignoring the raid difficulty.
- **Headless, this is the stub's word for the client's.** `spec/itemline_spec.lua` and `spec/upgrademap_spec.lua` register what `GetDetailedItemLevelInfo` answers for the link (292, then 305) and read the tooltip's lines back; `spec/roadsrow_spec.lua` pins the two numbers on the drop roads. That the LIVE client draws the line under the real tooltip is the owner's hover, below.

**2026-09-16 (M5-2a, WKE-593) - the minimap button is drawn to LibDBIcon's retail geometry, and it carries its own events.** The owner's screenshot showed Lootpath's button between two LibDBIcon buttons, further out than both, with a square icon overrunning the ring and a question mark instead of his Restoration icon. Four things were settled while fixing it.

  (a) **The radius is the library's, 5, not our 10.** `lib.radius = 5` (LibDBIcon-1.0 minor 55, read from the installed DandersFrames copy - read, never vendored; the 2026-09-09 decision that the launcher costs no library stands). Every other addon's button sits at `width / 2 + 5`, so at 10 ours was five points off the ring they share on every angle. `UI.MINIMAP_MARGIN` is 5 and `UI.MINIMAP_RADIUS` follows it to 75. **The square minimap's diagonal pull-back is NOT the margin:** it is a flat 10, which is the literal LibDBIcon uses (`sqrt(2*w^2)-10`), and it now has its own name, `UI.MINIMAP_DIAGONAL_INSET`. The two were equal only by accident while the margin was 10.

  (b) **The geometry is LibDBIcon's `WOW_PROJECT_MAINLINE` branch, point for point.** Ours had been the library's CLASSIC branch: a 20-point icon in the `BACKGROUND` layer, nothing behind it, under a 53-point border. Retail is the border 50 at `TOPLEFT`, a `UI-Minimap-Background` disc 24 centred in `BACKGROUND`, and the icon 18 centred in `ARTWORK` - the dark disc and the smaller icon are what make square icon art read as inside the ring. The icon is trimmed by **5% of whatever coordinate RANGE it carries**, not of the axis, which is what LibDBIcon's `updateCoord` does and is why a class circle's quarter of the sheet is trimmed by a quarter as much and stays centred on its own art.

  (c) **And the icon is masked round, which LibDBIcon does not do.** A spec icon is square art like any other. The mask is the file `PortraitFrameTemplate` puts on its own portrait - `Interface/CharacterFrame/TempPortraitAlphaMask`, read under `.luals/` at `Blizzard_SharedXML/Mainline/SharedUIPanelTemplates.xml:564` - applied through `TextureBase:SetMask(file)`, the one-file form, confirmed in the exported annotations (`Core/Widget/Base/TextureBase.lua:142`). So the button and the window's ring crop their icon the same way. The call is behind a `type(...) == "function"` check, so a client without it keeps the trimmed square rather than nothing.

  (d) **The button owns its icon; the window no longer touches it.** `UI.MinimapIcon()` answers the same three steps `UI.ApplyPortrait` takes, from the same two readers - spec icon, else class circle with its four coordinates, else `INV_Misc_QuestionMark` - and `UI.ApplyMinimapIcon()` puts it on with the trim. The button registers `PLAYER_LOGIN`, `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` and `PLAYER_SPECIALIZATION_CHANGED` **on itself**, because it is built in `ns.onReady` at `ADDON_LOADED`, where the spec read is nil on the owner's client, and the only refresh used to be the window's own handler - and the window is lazy, so until it had been opened AND the spec had changed, the `ADDON_LOADED` question mark was what stayed. The window's `PLAYER_SPECIALIZATION_CHANGED` branch now redraws the ring **only**: a second call from there would be a second path to one fact, which is what this decision took out. **Which of the two login events first answers `C_SpecializationInfo.GetSpecialization()` is NOT measured** - that needs a real client and the owner runs every in-game step. Both are taken, applying the icon twice costs two texture sets, and the measurement is left to the human-required step. A question mark is now only ever a client that names neither spec nor class.

**2026-09-15 (C-11, WKE-572) - a Top Gear run is a sequence of passes, and an item's rating comes from the pass that saw it.** The owner's decision on WKE-558, taken 2026-09-14 evening, was option (c): not a patron tier, not living within thirty. The fork's cap is never edited (§7, 2026-09-07: the fork is read and driven, never changed in what it decides). What was built:

  (a) **The baseline is read at import, once, before anything is clicked.** It is the cards QE Live made active, which his own engine says are the equipped set, the vault options and any clone of one of those. It is in every pass's pool and nothing ever deselects one. After pass 1 "active" means "pass 1 clicked it", so a driver that read the baseline later would keep the wrong set.

  (b) **Each later pass deselects the previous pass's bag items and asks about cards nothing has asked about yet.** No card outside the baseline is asked twice; the grid is checked ident-for-ident between passes, because every click is by position and a grid that moved would choose a pool nobody named. The loop stops on the first of: nothing left out, no room past the baseline (a second document there would be the first one's pool again), or `topGearPasses`.

  (c) **Every pass is its own document. Nothing is merged.** `pass` and `considered` travel beside C-8's `excluded`, in the same shape, so the addon asks one identity question (C-10) of both lists.

  (d) **Pass 1 is the plan and the later passes cannot reach it.** They are filed on `qePassesByScenario`, which no surface that draws a week's plan reads. This is the same deliverable C-6 wrote for the scenarios and it fails the same way if it is broken: a later pass's pool holds no vault option and no Catalyst clone, so a best set drawn from one would tell the owner to skip his vault.

  (e) **No percent from a later pass is printed beside a pass-1 row, and the issue's step 3 is answered to that extent and no further.** The issue asked for a pass-2 item to be rated "against your best set" in the Upgrade Map's `+x%` / `behind` words. It cannot be, honestly: a later pass's differentials are against THAT pass's top set, which is built over the equipped baseline plus the leftovers and is not your best set. What IS honest is the membership question, so the road model says `rated · better than what you wear` when the pass put the item in its own top set, and the existing third phrase `not in your best set` when it did not - the second is sound because a pool that held everything the character is wearing and did not pick the item is a pool the fuller one could not have picked it out of either. The tooltip's sentence for the first case is `This beats what you've got on. The plan was built before anything had rated it.`, which takes the plan's position without inventing an imperative the plan has no grounds for.

  (f) **`not rated · beyond the rating's item limit` is kept, and now means what it says.** The issue asked for it to be retired from every surface. It cannot be while the pass bound exists: four passes over the owner's 63 cards ask about 30 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 60 of them, so three can still be left. The phrase is now reached only by an item NO pass was ever shown, which is what the last pass's `excluded` list is, and is empty in any run that finishes inside the bound.

**2026-09-15 (C-12, WKE-577) - a question is asked when the question has an answer, not when the vault is full; and the run says which questions it left alone.** The 2026-09-08 premise behind `hasVaultGear` (C-6, §5) was that with nothing in the vault there is nothing to catalyse or upgrade that is not already yours. It is wrong about the week a player is actually in, and the owner's first refresh after claiming his vault reward is the proof (§9): he held the Venom-Cursed Lynx's Spaulders, a Catalyst candidate his morning's `thisWeek` document had put in his best set, and the Lightgrasp Worldroot he had just crested to 315, two steps short of 321. Those two moves were his week, and the companion asked about neither, because the vault was empty.
  (a) **Each what-if is gated on its own question.** `catalyzed` when QE Live made at least one Catalyst clone out of what the character holds; `maxed` when at least one held item came back above the level the `asOffered` import valued it at; `thisWeek` when either, because it is the two together. `asOffered` is ungated and always asked. A vault section with gear in it, and `--force`, still waive all three outright - the gate could only agree, and a pool read to hear it agree is a read for nothing.
  (b) **The fork decides, because only the fork knows.** Catalyst eligibility is a season of slot and source rules in his `Item.canBeCatalyzed`; an upgrade cap is his `CONSTANTS.itemLevelCaps`. Lootpath restates neither and never will. So the gate is settled INSIDE the run, after that pass's import, by reading the same Top Gear cards C-8 and C-10 already read and counting them - clones for one half, and "higher than the base pass said" for the other, keyed by item ID so that a bonus list his engine may rewrite cannot make an upgrade look like a different item. **What a skipped pass saves is its Top Gear documents, not its import**, and that is the honest price: the alternative was a table of season rules in this repo, which the healer-value rule and the evidence rule both forbid.
  (c) **It fails open.** A pool that could not be read, a base pass that was never read, or a gate kind this build does not know all ask the pass anyway and say so. The defect being fixed here is a question skipped for want of evidence; it must not come back in through the guard.
  (d) **A run that asked fewer questions says so once, in one sentence, written in one place.** `lib/config.js` `scenarioNote` composes it - the scenarios in a reader's words, the distinct reasons said once each - and the same string goes into the log, into `Data/CompanionStatus.lua`'s `message` (the strip's tooltip) and into `Data/QEVerdict.lua`'s `scenarioNote` (the Vault tab). The pass-by-pass lines in the log keep the four contract names, because that is the grep; the sentence does not, because it is read on the Vault tab by a person who never chose those words.
  (e) **The Vault tab's plan footnote says it when, and only when, the plan on screen is not the plan on the label.** `Roads.Plan` already fell back to the first stored scenario and already reported that it had (`fellBack`); the tab drew the fallback without a word, which is what the owner saw. The note becomes the footnote in exactly that case, after the charge footnote rather than instead of it. With the highlighted scenario's own document stored, the note is about questions that sentence never claimed to answer and is not said there.
  (f) **The capture was NOT extended, and the issue's parenthetical is refuted.** It asked whether `Modules/Inventory.lua` records `upgradeLevel`/`upgradeMax`, and to extend the capture if not. It does not - it carries `bonusIDs` and no upgrade fields - and it cannot: the only documented read of them is `C_ItemUpgrade.GetItemUpgradeItemInfo`, which answers only after `SetItemUpgradeFromLocation` in an OPEN upgrade vendor window (`.luals/.../ItemUpgradeDocumentation.lua`). That is a vendor-side capture the owner has to stand at a vendor to run, it is WKE-574's (M3-17) subject and its recorded exception, and building the gate on it would have left this defect unfixed until he next visited one. The fork's own numbers need no vendor and no capture.
- **2026-09-16, later - the mask came off the minimap icon: the client refuses tex coords on a masked texture (M5-2a fix, WKE-593).** The owner's first reload on `832788c` threw `Texture:SetTexCoord(): Cannot set tex coords when texture has mask.` at `MainFrame.lua:647`, inside `ApplyMinimapIcon` called from `MinimapButton` at load - so the button was left half built (icon set, no border, no badge, no events) and the Lua Error window was the first thing on screen. The pairing is refused by the client outright, and it was never proven: the stub recorded `SetMask` without modelling what it forbids, so 1273 tests were green over a button the client cannot build. **Decided:** the trim stays and the mask goes. The trim is LibDBIcon's own shape, it is what the neighbouring buttons look like, and it is the only way the class-circle fallback's quarter-sheet coords reach the texture; a mask cannot replace it. The stub's `SetTexCoord` now throws the client's exact sentence when a mask is set, so the pairing is a red test and not a screenshot: on the unfixed code 1289 tests error at the same line the client named. **Not decided:** whether a `MaskTexture` through `Texture:AddMaskTexture` allows tex coords beside it - neither Baganator's GW2 skin nor LibCustomGlow, the two installed users of it, pair the two, so it is unconfirmed and stays in §11 as a real-client try, not a build.
- **2026-09-16, evening - Lootpath is for healers, and outside a healing spec it says so and nothing else (H-1, WKE-596; decided with the owner).** §1 has always said healers; the code assumed it. In Guardian the owner's bags and window kept telling him to put his healing gear on, because a refresh or a reload flush in that spec captured the Guardian set as worn and the plan then wanted every slot swapped. Three things decided, all the owner's: (1) the `inventory` capture is REFUSED in a non-healer spec, through the same `refuse(data)` R-7b added, so the last healing read stays newest and the plan is untouched; `env`, `vault`, `currencies` and `upgrade` still capture, and `Companion.Refresh` says `you're in Guardian; switch to Restoration to refresh your plan` and stops; (2) every in-place surface is fully silent - no bag mark, no tooltip block, no nudge, no badge - rather than one line on every hover; (3) the window is one screen: `Coming soon for Guardian. Lootpath plans healing gear for now. Switch to Restoration and your plan is here.` with the plan's age under it. The gate is keyed on the spec's ROLE (`GetSpecializationInfo`'s fifth return, `HEALER`), never on Druid, and the healing spec's name comes from the client's own spec list; a nil role is NOT gated, because the spec read is empty at `ADDON_LOADED` and on a real logout (§9 2026-09-16), and an unknown must behave as today.
  - **2026-09-17 (H-1a, WKE-606) - the status strip is hidden with the panels, not kept above them.** H-1 left the strip's four facts on the row over the screen and dropped only its spec clause. The owner, on his check: "Good except for still showcasing the Restoration Druid copy at the top left." Every fact on that row is a fact about the healing set - whose numbers, how old, which vault pick, what the companion last did - and the screen under it already says the age. So the strip and the nudge row are hidden while `ns.Companion.Gate()` names a non-healer role, in `UI.RefreshStrip` (the redraw, wherever it comes from) and in `UI.ShowTab` (the window opening) from the same live read; `frame.stripModel` is cleared with it, which is what makes the hover and the click silent even where a hidden frame could still be asked. **Import and Options were children of the strip** - a child of a hidden frame is hidden with it in the client - so they are children of the FRAME now, anchored to the strip's row exactly as before, because a point is resolved whether or not the frame it hangs off is shown. Nothing about the gate itself changed: a nil role is not gated, and breaking that is one of the five guards.
- **2026-09-16, evening - "the plan" is never said on screen (the owner's rule; WKE-599 carries it).** Hovering a bag item the rating said to skip, the owner read `Skip this one, the plan uses your Dreamwatcher legs.` and six more lines, wrote `Pass - use your Dreamwatcher legs` as what it should say, and ruled the phrase out: "I don't like the usage of the phrase 'the plan' or 'your plan' - we need to remove that phrase." The principle behind `docs/ROADS-UX.md`'s "the plan first" - the answer before the reasons, in a guildmate's words - stands; the noun goes. Every surface says what the thing is instead: the rating and its age (`rated 1h ago`), the set (`your best set`), the action (`use your Dreamwatcher legs`), or nothing. 599 adds the `spec/voice_spec.lua` guard and sweeps every string; 594's and 596's strings were reworded in their issues before they are built. The memory note `feedback-plan-first` carries the same correction.
- **2026-09-17 (E-1a, WKE-605) - the destination slot is ASKED OF THE CLIENT, and `C_Item.EquipItemByName` is gone from `EquipPanel.lua`.** The owner checked E-1 on 2026-09-16 ~20:15 on `main` `5034b30` with his legs slot EMPTY and both leggings in the bags: Equip all put on the 295 again. That is exactly the case E-1's own Premise check left behind - a row with `dstSlot == nil`, because `dstSlot` is the scanned `slotIndex` of the item being REPLACED (`Match.lua:259`) and an empty slot has nothing to replace - so the row fell through to the by-name path and the client resolved the name to the first copy in the bags. **Premise refuted:** the issue asked for the mapping Blizzard's own UI uses from `itemEquipLoc` to an inventory slot, mirrored from `.luals/`. **Blizzard ships no such table.** Searched under `.luals/` on 2026-09-17: `INVTYPE_HEAD` appears twice in the whole tree (a heirloom branch in `Blizzard_HeirloomCollection.lua:243` and an Encounter Journal filter list at `Blizzard_EncounterJournal.lua:155`), `INVTYPE_FINGER` twice, and neither is a mapping; `Constants.lua:151-173` lists the `INVSLOT_*` numbers but joins them to nothing; `C_Item.GetItemInventorySlotKey(invType)` hands back the `INVTYPE_*` string again (`ItemDocumentation.lua`, used that way at `DressUpModelFrameMixin.lua:502-503`) and `GetInventorySlotInfo(invSlotName)` wants a slot NAME (`Wiki.lua:5069-5074`). Writing the join ourselves would be the remembered table the 2026-09-06 decision forbids. **The decision: ask the question from the other end, the way Blizzard's own paper-doll flyout does.** `GetInventoryItemsForSlot(slot, returnTable)` (`Wiki.lua:5064-5067`) fills a table with `[packedLocation] = itemID` for every bag and bank item that CAN be equipped in that inventory slot; `PaperDollFrame.lua:2064-2066` is the flyout's only call and `Blizzard_TutorialLogic.lua:1158-1200` walks `INVSLOT_FIRST_EQUIPPED..INVSLOT_LAST_EQUIPPED` calling it exactly as `EquipPanel.DestinationSlot` now does. Each packed key is unpacked by **Blizzard's own** `EquipmentManager_GetLocationData(location)` (`Shared/EquipmentManager.lua:1-29`) - called, not copied, so a change to the packing can never leave a stale copy of the arithmetic in our file - and the slots whose answer names this row's own `bag` and `slotIndex` are this copy's candidates. The EMPTY one is taken, lowest first, with `GetInventoryItemID("player", slot)` (`Wiki.lua:5037-5042`) telling empty from full - **an empty one or none**: this is reached only where Match said nothing is worn in that slot, so a client that names no free slot at all is a disagreement, and the row refuses rather than displacing a piece nobody asked about. **So the two-slot and two-hand cases need no rule of ours at all:** the client offers both finger slots for a ring and both trinket slots for a trinket and the empty one is taken; whether a two-hander may also go in the off hand is the client's answer (Titan's Grip), and with both hands free the main hand comes first because it is the lower number. **Three functions are added to the four E-1 named, all read-only and all named at the call site**, making seven. **The by-name path is deleted**, not demoted: with a slot for every equippable row there is no case left for it, and E-1's source guard is flipped - the test now fails if the string `EquipItemByName` appears in `EquipPanel.lua` at all. A row the client names no slot for, or a record with no bag slot to pick up from, refuses in one sentence - `can't tell where this goes - equip it by hand` - and picks nothing up; Equip all stops there as it stops at any refusal. **Unmeasured on a real client:** all of it, as E-1 (§11).

Run /lootpath refresh: it asks for them the way the Great Vault window does.`

**2026-09-14 (night), the floor stays, and the addon says when it is behind (owner):** asked whether the finished product must have players refreshing and reloading, the answer given was that two reloads per refresh is the floor of this architecture (2026-09-07), that the only ways below it are an engine inside the addon or a screen-pixel export for the first half, and that the floor is tolerable if the plan is fresh at login, the stale state is honest from the bags alone (576), and the refresh is rare. It runs before `RequestNames` and, when it fills anything, the map is built once more over the now-named roads - because a sentence is written inside the build, and a name that lands after it reaches the row but not the sentence. What stays sentence-less is unchanged and is the right boundary: a road to something you do NOT have - a journal drop, a crafted row, a delve row - where "Skip this one" would read as "skip the dungeon". Held means the inventory scan's records, which is equipped, bags AND bank; a piece in the bank is a piece you own.
  (b) **A tooltip carries no clause whose referent is on another screen.** Four left it, and the Upgrade Map row keeps all four, because on the panel every referent is visible. The crest COST clause (`crest type and cost not readable`) is 568's vendor-window gate: on the row it answers "what will this cost me", beside the crest counts; on a tooltip nobody asked, nothing is beside it, and it can never become readable. The RIVAL clause (`the same charge as the vault Spaulders road`) is principle 6's own rule turned on itself - "a reference is never to a road that is not on the same screen", and a tooltip about one item is never that screen. A NAMELESS road said `item 244572 (331)`; an ID is not a name, so the tooltip says what kind of thing it is (`a crafted piece (331)`) and the cache now asks the client for the name once per item ID and rebuilds when it lands. And a NO-RATING road took one of three lines under a best-set pick: on the tooltip "other roads" are rated roads only, forward ones first. Principle 10's three is a cap, not a quota. **`crest type and cost not read` - the "not read YET" clause - was deliberately left on**: it can change, where "not readable" cannot, and the owner named only the permanent one.
  (c) **`Why this?` says where to go.** On the Upgrade Map row it opens the row; on a tooltip it cannot be clicked and principle 9's rule is that a verb only exists where it goes somewhere. Principles 10 and 11 both write the line as an always, so it keeps its place and names its destination: `Why this? · /lootpath map`, and `/lootpath map` opens the window on the Upgrade Map. It shows rather than toggles - a reader who typed it off a tooltip asked to see the tab, never to close a window.
  (d) **A missing mark explains itself, and the explanation is a command rather than a screenshot.** Nothing on the owner's screen told "the adapter never installed" from "the bag addon never draws the widget" from "the lookup answers false", and each is a different fix. `/lootpath glow` prints all three plus one item's whole lookup - the key the link makes, whether the map has it, what the mark answers, and whether the item's own road is one the plan points at - and takes a shift-clicked link or falls back to the first bag slot. `/lootpath capture glow` records the same four facts for every bag slot, with the map's own key list beside them, so a transcript settles a key mismatch instead of a hover doing it one item at a time.
  (e) **The corner was wrong, and it was read rather than reasoned.** Baganator's `Core/Config.lua:46` ships `icon_top_left_corner_array` as `{"junk", "item_level"}`, and `ItemViewCommon/ItemButton.lua:174-177` walks one corner's widgets in array order and **breaks on the first that returns true** - only one widget is ever shown per corner. `API/Main.lua:185-196` inserts a `defaultPosition` at the priority INDEX, so R-2's `{ corner = "top_left", priority = 1 }` would have put Lootpath first in top-left and taken the item level off every slot the plan marks. The same rule that kept Lootpath out of Baganator's upgrade-plugin slot applies to a corner: a mark that costs the reader something he already had is not the mark he asked for. `top_right` ships empty. **Two of the issue's three candidate causes are refuted by that source, not by a screen:** `AutoInsert` is gated per widget id on `icon_corners_auto_insert_applied`, so a widget new to a saved profile IS inserted into an existing corner array; and registering late is handled, because `RegisterCornerWidget` fires `PluginsUpdated`, which rebuilds the per-corner callbacks and asks for an item-widget refresh. **Which cause it actually was is still open and is the owner's next step** (§11): the fix here removes one, and the command names whichever remains.
  (f) **`hour(s)` was a format string on a screen.** `UI.AgeText` built `second(s)` / `minute(s)` / `hour(s)` / `day(s)`; the voice rule is that it sounds like a person. `UI.Plural` writes English's own plural once and every surface that prints an age reads it. None of the four bands can actually produce a 1 - the minute band runs to 90 minutes and each band rounds into the next at 1.5 - so the singular is asserted on `UI.Plural` itself rather than through a moment that cannot happen.

- **2026-09-15 (V-2, WKE-573) - the strip drops the content type, and what that buys is measured, not assumed.** Three things were settled while building it. **(a) The two words moved rather than went.** `UI.VerdictNoteText` now names the export as well as the content type - "Showing the Dungeon Top Gear export (...)" - and that sentence is the strip's first tooltip line, so hovering the strip still answers what the line used to say. A separate tooltip line was rejected: the content type was already in that sentence and a second one would have said it twice. The Import dialog shows the same sentence and gains the export's name with it, which is the same fact in the same words. **(b) The width is asserted in CHARACTERS, against the owner's own cut line, and the test says so.** The stub has no pixels (9) and this repo holds no screenshot a headless test can measure, so no font metric was added and none was invented. The budget is the 104 characters 11 recorded as visible on his 2026-09-14 screen at the window's default width. The font is proportional, so 104 characters is a proxy and a LOWER bound on the real width - which is what makes it safe to assert against rather than a pixel claim, and the test's comment states the whole of that. Measured on the owner's own state (Dungeon export, companion-written, five days old): **122 characters before, 103 after**; the `never seen` clause comes to 97. **(c) The FAILED clause still does not fit, and this is said out loud rather than left to be found.** `companion: FAILED at qe live (07:00) - see companion.log` brings the line to **132 characters**, and dropping one fact cannot close a 28-character gap. A test asserts that it is over the budget and that the companion's whole sentence is in the tooltip, which is where that reader is sent. Shortening the clause, or wrapping the strip, stays available and is not taken without the owner. **(d) The glow command samples gear.** `/lootpath glow` with no link took bag 0 slot 1 and reported on the Hearthstone (the owner's run, 2026-09-14 night). It now walks bags 0..4 for the first slot whose `ns.ItemData.Instant(link).slot` is non-nil - the same static-data slot every other surface uses - and names what it sampled. `C_Item.GetItemInventoryTypeByID`, which the issue named, was NOT added: `GetItemInfoInstant` is already in `ItemData`'s declared list and already answers the question, so no new client call enters the addon for a diagnostic. With no gear in the bags it says `item: no equippable gear in your bags to sample` and still prints the shift-click instruction. **(e) The plurals (the issue's part 3) were already done** by R-2a (PR #99, `34ea350`): `UI.Plural` exists and the strip, `Tooltip.HeaderText` and `Companion.StatusText` all read ages through `UI.AgeText`. Verified, not rebuilt. The `(s)` forms that remain in the addon are other nouns on other surfaces (items, drops, rewards, rows) and are outside this issue.
**2026-09-14 (evening), five decisions by the owner, each with the options as presented:** (1) **The 30-item rating limit** (558): (a) a patron tier, (b) live within 30, (c) a second pass over the leftovers. **Chosen (c)**, WKE-572: every pass is its own document, nothing merged, no number combined; the phrase `beyond the rating's item limit` retires once every held item is in some pass. (2) **The vault leaving the profile** (557): (a) the capture calls Blizzard's own `C_WeeklyRewards.OnUIInteract()` and waits for the update, (b) keep the fresh-login habit, (c) the strip tells the player to log in again. **Chosen (a)**: the second recorded exception to "captures only read" after the journal's view state (2026-09-06); it marks the vault as looked at and claims nothing. (3) **The status strip**: drop "Dungeon Top Gear" or wrap to two lines. **Chosen: drop it**, WKE-573; the content type lives in the tabs' own controls and the strip's tooltip. (4) **Crest costs** (568 q2): (a) a capture places an owned item in the open vendor window and reads `GetItemUpgradeItemInfo`, (b) drop cost clauses everywhere. **Chosen (a)**: the third exception, WKE-574; `UpgradeItem` is never called and a test asserts it; vault items and drops stay unreadable. (5) **The companion starting with Windows** (C-9): run `install-startup.ps1` once and reboot, or keep starting it by hand. **Chosen: run it.** Recommended and chosen were the same five; the reasoning offered for each is in the session of 2026-09-14 evening and, in one line each, above.

- **2026-09-14 (R-3a, WKE-570) - an imperative belongs to a road the plan is going forward on, and to no other.** The owner read `do: equip it` on a Head row rated 0.95% behind the helm he was wearing. Three things were decided in fixing it. **(a) One gate, asked twice.** Principle 12 (the glow: in your best set, or a positive percent, under the highlighted plan) and principle 16 (the imperative is bounded to the road's own next step, and a road rated behind what you wear has no next step) are the same test, so they are one function - `Roads.IsForward` - which R-2's glow will call rather than write again. **(b) The gate runs over the finished slot, not inside the builders.** The defect was not one bad string: `do: equip it`, `do: raid it`, `do: run the key`, `do: take one vault reward` and `do: get the spark` were each written where its road is built, and any one of them could have been fixed while the next escaped. `Roads.GateImperatives` walks all three groups after every builder has run and finds an imperative by its `do: ` prefix, so a phrasing added later is gated without being enumerated. **(c) What a gated row says instead is the plan's own words, and only where they are true.** `keep what you've got on` is the slot sentence's own clause, and it is right only when the slot's plan pick IS the piece worn. On the Shoulder slot, whose plan is to Catalyst a bag item, it would be a lie - so those rows simply end after their facts, and the badge's `referent` ("taking the vault weapon instead") is what says where the plan went. Where the phrase does apply it applies to EVERY rated-behind road of the slot, including a Delves row that never had an imperative, because two rows carrying the same verdict must not end differently. A road nothing rated gains no phrase either way: not knowing is not a verdict. The Keep row keeps `nothing to do`; it is not an imperative. **What this costs, named rather than hidden:** three rows on the owner's own week lose a `do:` that was not wrong in itself - the vault Spaulders' `do: take one vault reward` and two Mythic+ rows rated `not in your best set`, one of which is `+0.38%` once crested. The vault still hands over one reward and the plan sentence above still says to take it; a row whose own rating points behind is not the place to say so.

- **2026-09-14 (R-4, WKE-565) - Delves and Crafted are cards by run, roads by slot, and they name no key level.** The Upgrade Finder documents the companion writes carry 33 delve rows and 18 crafted ones each; the by-run view had nowhere to put them and the by-slot view already does, through R-3. Four things were decided while building it:
  (a) **The by-slot half is `ns.Roads`', and is not drawn twice.** R-1 gave the road model a craft and a delve road per slot and R-3 renders them under `Other rated sources`; this build pointed that walk at `ns.UFImport.SourceRows` (one place where these rows are found, ordered and deduplicated) and added the one thing only the export knew - the stats line the crafted rating assumed - rather than adding a second list of the same rows under the candidates. The first cut of this PR did add that second list; `main` moved under it and the owner returned it for reconciliation.
  (b) **No key level on these rows.** Measured over the committed run: the five dungeon documents (+2 through +10) carry all 51 of these rows with identical `upgradePercent`, and the Raid document differs on 33 of them - so what values a crafted item is the content type, never the Mythic+ key. A grey `(at +2)` would tell the reader a dependency his own files deny. The document is still carried on the row, and the note comes back the moment two stored documents really disagree.
  (c) **A card's denominator says "ranked items", never "drops".** A run's denominator is every drop the Adventure Guide lists for it; a Crafting or Delves card has no loot table behind it, only the rows he ranked, and `13 of 18 ranked items are upgrades` is the honest wording of that. For the same reason `counts.drops` and `counts.rated` stay the walk's own figures and the cards are counted separately.
  (d) **They carry no difficulty and are shown under every filter**, and the difficulty dropdown gains no entry for them: a difficulty is a property of a walked run, and inventing "Crafting (18)" as a filter row would invent one. Said once on screen (`Panel.EXPORT_NOTE`) rather than on every row.
  Also decided by what could not be read: a crafted row says `spark and materials not read` and, where the export's settings name them, `the rating assumes Crit / Haste`; a delve row says `key and Bountiful state not read` - the issue's suggested wording was `Bountiful delve - not read`, and "Bountiful" is not something any committed file or client call confirms about these rows, so the row names what is unread instead of asserting which delve it came from.

- **2026-09-13 (T-1, WKE-560) - the headless stub models one widget's mixin chain per widget, and its own helpers live off Blizzard's namespace.** The rule PR #72 stated for dropdowns is now the rule for every kind and every template the stub recognises, and the audit that applied it found the fix had been only the visible half:
  (a) **The leak was in `newRegion`, not in `attachTemplate`.** Every widget - `Frame`, `Button`, `EditBox`, `ScrollFrame`, `FontString`, `Texture` alike - was built from one constructor that handed out the union of `Region`, `FontString` and `Texture`, and `newFrame` added `ScrollFrame`'s five scroll setters on top. So a bare `Frame` answered `SetText`, `SetTextColor`, `SetJustifyH`, `SetTexture`, `SetAtlas`, `SetTexCoord` and `SetScrollChild`; a `FontString` answered `SetAtlas`; a `Texture` answered `SetText` and `SetWordWrap`. Nineteen names in all. The templates were the symptom; the constructor was the cause.
  (b) **Subtracting a superset is still a superset.** PR #72 gave `SetDefaultText` / `GetDefaultText` / `SetSelectionText` to the `DropdownButton` KIND and then set them to `nil` inside `attachTemplate` for anything that was not `WowStyle1DropdownTemplate`. `attachTemplate` returns immediately when the template is not a string, so `CreateFrame("DropdownButton", nil, parent)` never reached the subtraction and answered `SetDefaultText` headlessly - the intrinsic does not have it (`Core/Widget/Intrinsic/DropdownButton.lua:9` is `DropdownButton : DropdownButtonMixin, Button`; `SetDefaultText` is `MenuTemplates.lua:582`, `DropdownSelectionTextMixin`'s). **A template is now added to and never subtracted from.**
  (c) **A gap is safe; a superset is not.** The stub deliberately models less than the client where no panel needs more - `CheckButton:SetChecked`, `DropdownSelectionTextMixin:SetSelectionText` and `SetTooltip`, `DropdownButtonMixin:Pick`, `ScriptRegion:SetScript` on a `FontString`. A missing method turns a test red where the client would have worked, which costs a session; an extra one turns a test green where the client breaks, which cost the owner a crash on screen.
  (d) **Stub-only affordances moved to `widget.stub`.** `Button:Enter` / `:Leave`, `dropdown:Pick(index)` / `:SelectedIndex()` / `:SelectByText()`, `scrollBox:Acquire()` / `:ReleaseAll()` and `GameTooltip:Text()` were all names the client does not have, and `Pick` was worse than absent - `DropdownButtonMixin:Pick` is real (`DropdownButton.lua:341`) and takes a menu description and an input context, not an index, so the stub was occupying a real slot with a different contract. All eight are now `widget.stub:X()`.
  (e) **One gap the audit exposed was real and is now modelled.** `DropdownButton` inherits `Button`, and `UpgradeMapPanel` calls `SetText` on the difficulty control (real twice over: `Button.lua:199` and `DropdownTextMixin:SetText`, `MenuTemplates.lua:522`). Taking the union apart turned 31 tests red at `UpgradeMapPanel.lua:1876` in one run, which is exactly the signal the audit was for; the Button surface is now given to `DropdownButton` because a `DropdownButton` is one.
  (f) **A released scroll-box row stops answering for its old data.** The real view sets `frame.GetElementData` on acquire (`ScrollBoxListView.lua:90`) and clears it on release (`:114`); the stub set it and never cleared it.
  (g) **Two panel comments were corrected against what the annotations actually say.** `VaultPanel.lua` claimed "Blizzard's generated annotations do not record that inheritance" for `WowStyle1DropdownTemplate` -> `DropdownSelectionTextMixin`. They do: `Blizzard_Menu/Mainline/MenuTemplates.xml:3` declares `mixin="WowStyle1DropdownMixin"` and `MenuTemplates.lua:753` composes it. What the GENERATED API documentation omits is FrameXML's templates, which is a different claim. The `pcall` stays and now says which client it is for.
- **2026-09-13 (C-9, WKE-559) - the companion writes two more files, and starts with Windows.** Three things were settled building it.
  (a) **The addon-folder exception is now three files, and the rule that made it one still holds.** The 2026-09-07 decision let the companion write `Data/QEVerdict.lua` into the addon folder because an addon can read no file it did not ship with. `Data/companion.log` and `Data/CompanionStatus.lua` join it under exactly the same terms: written by the same program on the owner's own machine, into that same folder and nowhere else, data and never code, the status chunk through the verdict writer's own escaper, and the addon still loads nothing but its own Lua at load time. Nothing else was granted: no network, no second directory, no file the addon writes.
  (b) **"Nothing happened" and "nothing to do" are different states, and the status file is what tells them apart.** A failed run writes NO verdict - that is C-1's rule and it is right, because a half-answer is worse than yesterday's - so from inside the game a companion that crashed looked exactly like a companion with nothing to do: an export a few hours old, either way (§11, 2026-09-09). `skipped` is therefore its own state beside `idle`, `running` and `failed`, and the strip says `profile unchanged, no run (23:06)` rather than dressing it as a successful run. The chunk is written at every stage change, not at the end, so a run in progress says so instead of leaving the last run's words up for the minute QE Live takes.
  (c) **The login-time start is a Task Scheduler task for the current user, and "never two watchers" stops being a rule people remember.** `install-startup.ps1` registers an at-logon task running `start-companion.ps1` (the fork's dev server if nothing answers its port, then `node companion.js --watch`); interactive, no stored password, idempotent, and it never stops a watcher the owner started himself. Because nobody can now know by hand whether one is already running, the watcher takes `<stateDir>/watch.lock` and a second one exits 7 naming the pid that holds it - and a lock whose process is gone is taken over rather than honoured, so a machine that lost power mid-run never needs a file deleted by hand. **The reboot itself is the owner's step and nothing here claims it was taken.**
- **2026-09-12 (R-3, WKE-564) - a slot's rows ARE its roads, the plan leads both surfaces, and Explain is counted over what is drawn.** Four things were settled while building surface 2, each of which the next surface would otherwise re-decide.
