No difficulty filter is passed: the tab's dropdown narrows what the READER asked to see, and a bag hover is not that question. **(b) The plan sentence is written only for a road the plan is ABOUT**, which is the set group - a piece you hold, a Catalyst clone, a vault option, or what you wear. A journal drop, a crafted row and a delve row are in the `item` group and the plan takes no position on them, so there is no sentence; "Skip this one" on a dungeon drop would read as "skip the dungeon", which no document said. The issue asked for the item's part of the plan on every hover and this is the honest half of that. **(c) The block appears only for an item the map has an entry for** - every piece in your bags, every vault reward, every drop the walk found, every row the export carries. A chat link, a merchant's stock and an auction row get nothing, because "not rated" there would be a sentence about a question nobody asked. The phrase belongs on an item you HOLD, and the cache puts it there. **(d) One glow interface, one adapter per bag addon** (the owner's question, 2026-09-14): the core exposes `ns.Glow.Wants(key)`; adapters live in `UI/Bags/` and the `.toc` order is the preference order. Baganator goes in as a corner widget, never as an upgrade plugin, so Pawn's arrow keeps its slot. ElvUI, Bagnon and AdiBags are future adapters, never core changes. **(e) The glow is the ITEM's, not one road's**: an item is marked when ANY road into it is wanted, because taking any of them is what the mark is about. **(f) Two of the issue's own instructions were refuted against the committed files and the truth was built instead** - the Hide of Pestilence glows (it is the tier chest in every set of this week, the M3-15 correction of 2026-09-09, so its Catalyst road reads "in your best set", which is exactly what principle 12 marks; the bag piece the rating really leaves behind is the Miststalker's Spaulders), and `ns.Roads.TOOLTIP_ROADS` is counted by the tooltip itself rather than trusted from the model, because with exactly three groups the model can never hand over a fourth road and a cap that cannot be exceeded is a cap no test can prove.

- **2026-09-14 (night) - The two-reload floor stays, and the addon says when it is behind (R-6, WKE-578).** The owner asked whether the two reloads could go. They cannot: SavedVariables reach disk only on a reload or a logout and the client reads an addon's files only at load (2026-09-07, above), and nothing since has moved either. **What was decided instead is that the player is never asked to know that.** The rules the build follows: (a) **one string builder**, `ns.Drift.Model`, so the strip row, the launcher tooltip and anything later cannot disagree; (b) **the click runs the command's own function**, never a copy of it; (c) **`ReloadUI` is reached only from an OnClick**, which is the hardware event the client requires, and never from a timer; (d) **the nudge is drift in what you can EQUIP** - equipped and bags, never the bank, because opening a bank frame is a window opening and not gear moving, and never a non-gear item, which cannot produce an `ns.Inventory` record at all; (e) **an item the plan already knew is not drift however it moves**, because the key is the same; (f) **the wait line quotes only a run that actually rated something**, rounded to 15 s, and says `usually about a minute` when nothing has been measured; (g) **C-9's FAILED beats the wait**, because "it died" is a truer sentence than "it is coming"; (h) **the wait gives up after ten minutes** rather than standing all session over a watcher that was never restarted (§11, 2026-09-09) - that bound is a judgement, not a measurement, and is labelled as one in the code.
  - **Premise refuted 2026-09-14 (night): the issue's "fresh at login is the default story" does not hold on its own.** WKE-578 asked for the README and CHANGELOG to say "log out, and your plan is current next time you log in". They did not, because it was not true: **the addon took its snapshots only when `/lootpath refresh` was run**, so a logout flushed whatever was last captured, the companion fingerprinted an unchanged profile and skipped, and the next login loaded the same plan. The docs said the true version - refresh once before you log out - and the companion's log named which case each run was. **A capture at `PLAYER_LOGOUT` would make the issue's version true and is the obvious follow-up; it was not built here, because the issue said "add nothing to the client for this" and widening is not this lane's call.** **Closed 2026-09-15 by R-7 (WKE-579), below: the capture at logout is built, the sentence is true, and the docs say the plain version.**
  - **And the log line cannot say "run after logout" outright.** A logout and a plain `/reload` produce the same write and the SavedVariables record no difference between them. What the file does record, since R-6, is how each snapshot was TAKEN; the companion compares the newest `env` snapshot's stamp with the one the last written run read (`envCapturedAt` in the fingerprint state) and says `run after a logout or a plain reload - nothing new was captured`, which is what it can prove. **Superseded in the normal case by R-7:** the flush now carries snapshots LABELLED for it, so the line is read off the addon's own label and not inferred. **R-6 was right and R-7 forgot it:** R-7 labelled them `logout` and the log duly said `run after logout` for plain reloads, which is the very claim this bullet said could not be made. R-7a restored the discipline - the label is `flush` and the line is `run after a logout or reload (gear captured at the flush)`. The inferred line survives for what it can still be - an addon from before R-7, and a forced logout or reload in combat, where every capture refuses and the last snapshot flushes again.

- **2026-09-15 - The capture at logout, so "log out and your plan is current next login" is a plain sentence (R-7, WKE-579).** `PLAYER_LOGOUT` runs `ns.Companion.CaptureAtLogout`, the same four captures `/lootpath refresh` takes - `env`, `inventory`, `vault`, `currencies` - and nothing else. The rules it is built to, each of which is a decision and not a detail: (a) **no reload**, because the client is already leaving, and the sequence does not depend on `ReloadUI` existing at all - which is what makes it not a second copy of the refresh; (b) **nothing asynchronous**, because `PLAYER_LOGOUT` is Blizzard's own synchronous event (Ketho's `SystemDocumentation.lua`: `LiteralName = "PLAYER_LOGOUT", SynchronousEvent = true`) and the client stops running Lua after it, so a timer or a listener registered there is a promise nothing can keep - `ns.RunCapture` now registers its abandonment timer only when the capture has NOT already answered, which changes nothing for a capture that is genuinely still running and leaves the logout path timer-free; (c) **M3-16's vault interaction never happens at logout** - the capture is handed `{ skipInteract = "logout" }`, `OnUIInteract` is not called, `CloseInteraction` is not called, and the snapshot records `interact.skipped = "logout"` so the plain read says outright that it is the plain one rather than looking like a refresh that found nothing. This does not widen the second recorded exception to "captures only read"; it narrows it, by naming a place it does not apply; (d) **nothing can fail loudly** - each capture goes through `ns.RunCapture` (which pcalls the capture body) and a `pcall` of its own, and the event handler pcalls the whole sequence, so a capture that throws leaves the ones after it to run and a logout is the last thing the player sees rather than an error; (e) **the `env` snapshot is stamped `capturedOn = "logout"` with the sequence's own `logoutMs`**, written after the sequence because its cost is not known until it is over; nothing in the addon reads either, they are the evidence.

- **2026-09-15 (M3-16a, WKE-581) - `ReloadUI` belongs to the player, so the vault question moves to login and a reload that cannot be immediate becomes a click.** **The evidence is the owner's own screen** (§9): on the first `/lootpath refresh` after M3-16 merged, with the reward unclaimed, all three refresh lines printed - the wait line, `captured gear, bags, bank (closed), vault, currencies - reloading so the companion can read them`, and the second-reload line - and then `Interface action failed because of an AddOn`. Nothing reloaded. The captures sat in memory until the owner typed `/reload` himself. **Cause:** before M3-16 the chain was synchronous, so the `ReloadUI()` at its end was still inside the slash command's execution and the client attributed it to the player's hardware event. M3-16 made the vault capture wait for `WEEKLY_REWARDS_UPDATE`, and `step()` then called `ReloadUI()` from that event's continuation, which the client refuses - the same rule that makes R-6's wait line a click and forbids a timer. The chain's own comment (`the chain is captures, then the vault's wait, then ReloadUI`) described the defect. **So, four decisions:**
  - **(a) The question is asked at login, with no capture and no reload.** The first `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` of a session, when `HasAvailableRewards()` is true and no activity carries a reward, runs M3-16's interaction and simply lets the client fill its own data. It is the same exception the owner allowed on 2026-09-14, one call earlier, and it does not widen it: nothing is captured, nothing is reloaded, `CloseInteraction` still runs on every path out including the timeout, and `ClaimReward`/`SelectReward` are still never named. By the time the player types the refresh the rewards are in `GetActivities()`, the vault capture has nothing to ask for, and the chain is synchronous again. **Never in combat**; a login that lands in a fight asks at `PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED`. **Once per session** - `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` fires after every loading screen, and a vault interaction per zone change is not what was allowed.
  - **(b) One copy of the interaction, not two.** `ns.VaultInteract` in `Captures.lua` is the whole exception in one function, called by the `vault` capture and by `ns.Companion.AskVaultAtLogin`. A second hand-written copy is exactly the thing that drifts out of step with the rule it is allowed under.
  - **(c) A refresh that still had to wait ASKS for its reload.** It never calls `ReloadUI` from the continuation. `StaticPopupDialogs["LOOTPATH_RELOAD_AFTER_REFRESH"]` shows `Gear captured. Reload to send it?` with Reload and Not now, and `OnAccept` reloads - a dialog button is a hardware event, and it is Blizzard's own pattern for exactly this (`GameDialogDefs.lua` lines 482-489 `TOO_MANY_LUA_ERRORS` and 568-575 `ADDON_ACTION_FORBIDDEN`, read 2026-09-15). No timeout on the box, because one that vanished on its own would leave four captures in memory with nothing on screen saying so. A client with no `StaticPopup_Show` is told the same thing in chat.
  - **(d) R-6's stamp is written on both paths.** `Drift.RefreshStarting()` runs before the reload AND before the popup, so the strip's wait line stands with its own `ReloadUI` click behind it and a player who chose Not now still has somewhere to click. The line's wording (`rating your gear`) is R-6's and was not changed here; it is slightly ahead of itself on that path, and whether it should say something else on a refresh that has not been sent yet is a voice question for the owner (§11).
  - **Premise corrected: there is no `env` record saying combat refused.** The issue said a forced logout in combat "means the inventory scan refuses, as it already does; the `env` record says so". It does not: `ns.RunCapture` refuses EVERY capture in combat, before the capture body runs, so a logout in combat stores nothing at all - not even an `env` record - and the last snapshot flushes as it did before R-7. That is the client rule ("nothing runs in combat") and the sequence does not work around it; it returns `{ ok = false, reason = "combat" }` and touches nothing. The companion's inferred line is what covers that case, and the README names it.
  - **`trigger = "flush"` is the fourth value R-6's label can take** (it was `"logout"` until R-7a below), and the companion's fourth log line - `run after a logout or reload (gear captured at the flush)` - is read off it rather than inferred.

- **2026-09-15 (evening) - `PLAYER_LOGOUT` is an unload, not a logout, and the label says only what it can prove; and every capture list is bounded (R-7a, WKE-582).** Two faults in R-7, both read off the owner's 13:58 pull (`spec/fixtures/captures/Lootpath-20260915-135808.lua`, §9), neither a fault in what R-7 set out to do.
  - **(a) The reload is not a logout, so nothing claims it is.** `PLAYER_LOGOUT` fires when the interface is unloaded, which a `/reload` does as surely as a logout. R-7's sequence therefore ran on every reload and stamped each snapshot `logout`: the pull carried **five `env` snapshots with `capturedOn = "logout"` for at most one logout**, and the companion printed `run after logout (gear captured at logout)` for a plain reload - the one thing R-7's own documents said it could not claim. **What could tell them apart is the next load**, not the event: a `/reload` is followed by `PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD` with `isInitialLogin = false, isReloadingUi = true` (Ketho's `SystemDocumentation.lua`), and a real logout by nothing in this session. By then the snapshot is written, so the answer is not to wait for it - it is to stop claiming. Everything the sequence stores says `flush`, which is true of both: `trigger`, `capturedOn`, the vault's `interact.skipped`, `logoutMs` renamed `flushMs`, `Companion.LOGOUT_TRIGGER`/`LOGOUT_VAULT_ARGS` renamed `FLUSH_*`, and `Companion.CaptureAtLogout` renamed `CaptureAtFlush`. The companion's line becomes `run after a logout or reload (gear captured at the flush)` and `run after logout` is retired. A snapshot still labelled `logout` came from an addon at exactly R-7 - the same event, the same four captures - and reads as the same line rather than as an unlabelled write.
  - **(b) It keeps running on reloads, deliberately.** That is not a cost to be tolerated: a reload's snapshot is the reason the SECOND reload of the refresh loop carries the gear the player is in. What the reloads cost is the retention, which (c) fixes.
  - **(c) Every capture keeps the newest four and nothing older.** `storeSnapshot` appended and nothing anywhere trimmed, so the file grew **6.1 MB (09-14 11:30) -> 7.1 MB (09-14 17:13) -> 11.0 MB (09-15 13:58)** - 35 `inventory` snapshots worth 5.85 MB of it, 37 `vault`, 35 `env`, 28 `currencies`, 3 `journal` - and the client reads and writes the whole file at every login and every reload. `ns.CAPTURE_HISTORY = 4` is the refresh loop's two flushes plus two to compare against, `table.remove(list, 1)` on the list AceDB already holds. **Why four and not one:** one snapshot cannot be compared with anything, and comparing a pull against what came before it is how three of this project's findings were made. **Why not "keep the journal walk":** the cold walk is already committed under `spec/fixtures/captures/`, which is where evidence lives; the live file is not an archive. A `/lootpath capture <name>` typed by hand is stored and bounded like any other, and `sync.ps1 -Pull` still copies whatever is there.
  - **The companion reads only the newest, and that is checked, not assumed.** `newestSnapshot` (`tools/companion/lib/simc-profile.js`) is the one reader, called three times for `env`, `inventory` and `vault`; `profile.js` reads the `env` one's `trigger` and `capturedAt`. Nothing walks an older snapshot. The `--snapshot` / `--env-snapshot` / `--vault-snapshot` indexes are debugging flags over a transcript file and are untouched. **The vault's "sixteen snapshots" reading of 2026-09-09 was a scratch script, not the companion.**
  - **Measured, for the first time on a real client:** the sequence's own `logoutMs` in the pull, five runs - **33.13, 22.39, 19.51, 32.02, 32.55 ms** - against the 250 ms the issue named as a budget. R-7's headless figure of 0.67-2.82 ms was the stub's world; this is the owner's bags. Nothing in §11 needs to say the cost is unknown any more.
  - **What this still cannot say:** whether the file stops growing. The bound is proven in the stub only, and the `captures` table was 9.0 MB of the 11.0 MB file, so 2.0 MB of it is something else the bound does not touch. The owner's next two reloads on the merged build are the measurement (§0).

- **2026-09-15 (night) - on reset day the Great Vault WINDOW generates the rewards and the addon's interaction does not; the flush stops reading the vault; the wait says itself where it can be seen (M3-16b, WKE-583).** Read from the owner's own SavedVariables of 2026-09-15 14:27 local, the vault half of which is committed as `spec/fixtures/captures/Lootpath-20260915-142722-vault.lua` (§9).
  - **(a) The finding, and the thing that is NOT built because of it.** M3-16 and M3-16a both assumed that `OnUIInteract` plus one `WEEKLY_REWARDS_UPDATE` fetches whatever the client is holding back. On reset day it fetches nothing: four refreshes asked, the client answered every time (66.7 / 77.1 / 113.2 / 130.9 ms, `timedOut` false), and the read after the answer was the read before it - 10 activities, every `rewards = {}`, 0 reward links, `HasGeneratedRewards()` false. The owner then OPENED the Great Vault window (it opened; on 2026-09-08/09 it would not) and captured with it shown: **11 activities, 5 carrying rewards, `HasGeneratedRewards()` and `CanClaimRewards()` true, 9 reward links.** Six seconds after he shut it, the flush read the same 11 and 9 - the data stays in the client once the window has generated it. **So "held back until something interacts" was the right reading of last week's mid-week state and is not the reading of reset day**, and the addon does not get a second exception to chase it: the owner's decision of 2026-09-14 allowed `OnUIInteract`/`CloseInteraction`, and nothing here widens it. What is built instead is a sentence: `VaultPanel.OPEN_VAULT_NOTE`, shown when `HasAvailableRewards()` is true and `HasGeneratedRewards()` is false, says **"This week's vault rewards have not been generated yet. Open the Great Vault, then refresh: opening it is what makes the client fetch them."** The mid-week `WITHHELD_REWARDS_NOTE` keeps naming the refresh, because there the ask really is the remedy.
  - **(b) The capture reads every update, not the first.** Blizzard's `WeeklyRewardsMixin:OnEvent` re-reads on every `WEEKLY_REWARDS_UPDATE` while the frame is shown; the capture settled on the first and closed, so one update carrying nothing ended the whole ask. It now reads on each update inside `ns.VAULT_INTERACT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` and settles when a read CARRIES rewards or the bound ends, recording `interact.updates = { { ms, activities, links }, ... }` so the next transcript can say whether a second or third update ever brings what the first did not. `timedOut` now means "the bound ended" rather than "nothing fired", and `updateFired` says whether the client answered at all. `CloseInteraction` runs once, at the end, on every path out - unchanged.
  - **(c) The flush never captures the vault.** R-7 read it plainly there and labelled the read; the cost was measured on reset day. The refresh at 19:09:29Z asked and stored its answer, the flush at the refresh's own reload stored the same empty read at 19:09:31Z, and being the newest that is what the companion built the profile from: `0 vault`, `warning: no generated Great Vault reward`, and a reset-day plan with no vault in it. A read that cannot ask can only shadow one that did, so `Companion.FLUSH_CAPTURES` is `env`, `inventory`, `currencies`, and `skipInteract` / `ns.VAULT_SKIPPED_REASON` are gone with the case they existed for. The vault snapshot is the refresh's and the login ask's: the reads that ask.
  - **(d) The companion chooses its vault snapshot.** `chooseVaultSnapshot` (`tools/companion/lib/simc-profile.js`): of the snapshots whose `secondsUntilWeeklyReset` puts them in the same reward period as the newest (60 s of slack for the two clocks), the newest that carries reward links wins, and among those the newest whose `interact.attempted` is true. Links are the point of the snapshot - a read with none of them cannot be the better answer - and the period bound is what stops last week's rewards being carried into this week. The reason travels onto the built profile as `vaultChoice` and the companion logs `vault read used: ...`, because `0 vault` was a choice between snapshots and nothing said so. **This is broader than the issue asked for** ("prefer a read that asked"), and it has to be: the read that carries the owner's nine links is the hand capture he took with the window open, and it did not ask - its gate said `the activities already carry rewards`.
  - **(e) The wait indicator, in the owner's words.** He said it on 2026-09-15: "after I do a refresh and the screen loads and I'm back in game, I'm assuming the refresh is done. If that is not the case we should have an indicator letting the player know the refresh is still happening." Three surfaces, one `ns.Drift.Model`: a chat line at the first load after a refresh; the minimap badge, which R-6 kept off during the wait and which is now on for it (with the window shut the launcher is the only surface there is, and the badge goes out the moment the wait does); and the strip, where **the wait is now the FIRST clause and the only one**. His screen read `...on Druid - companion, written 4 hours ago - vault pick: everything upgraded - companion: run st...`, cut at the window's width, with R-6's wait line on the row below and past the cut. The four facts it displaces move into the strip's own tooltip, the way V-2 moved the content type; the strip's row answers the click while it carries the wait, so `click to load it` is true of the row it is written on; and the nudge keeps the second row, where a player who has not acted yet reads it.

- **2026-09-15 (night) - `ns.EpochFromISO` pairs its two `mktime` calls at `isdst = false`, and the stub grows a modelled clock (V-4, WKE-589).**
  - **The defect.** `time(t)` is C's `mktime` and reads `t.isdst`: absent means "decide for yourself", `false` means "these fields are standard time", `true` means daylight time. `EpochFromISO` built its offset from `date("!*t", now)`, which writes `isdst = false`, and read the stamp from a table that said nothing. The two interpretations were different, so while daylight time was in effect the offset came out an hour too large and every stamp was parsed an hour early. The comment said "nothing here assumes a timezone"; it assumed standard time. **Every age and every wall clock the addon prints goes through this function**, and the owner read the result on 2026-09-15 at 17:22 CDT: `companion, written 62 minutes ago`, and `(16:22)` for a 17:20 event (§9).
  - **The fix, and why this one.** Both tables now say `isdst = false`, so the standard-time interpretation is applied twice and cancels exactly. Three candidates were measured against musl's own `mktime` and `localtime` under `TZ=America/Chicago` (`docker run -e TZ=America/Chicago lootpath-lua`, tzdata installed), on a two-minute-old stamp in summer, the same in winter, a stamp across the November fall-back, and a stamp half a year old: **both-`false` was exact in all four; letting `mktime` decide on both sides, and matching the offset table to the local clock's own `isdst`, were both exact in the first three and an hour out on the fourth.** `Lootpath/UI/VaultPanel.lua`'s `utcOffsetSeconds`/`Panel.EpochFromISO` was read and has ALWAYS paired them this way, so the Vault tab's `reset in` was never affected and nothing there changed; the one function now matches the other.
  - **The stub grew a clock, because it had to.** CI's container is UTC and Alpine carries no timezone database at all, so a fault that only appears during daylight time cannot be made red against the real `os.date` and `os.time` on any machine that runs this suite. `world.setClock(zone)` (`spec/stubs/wow.lua`) replaces both globals with a pair modelling one zone with one daylight rule: `date("!*t")` answers UTC fields with `isdst = false`, `date("*t")` answers local fields with the instant's own `isdst`, and `time(t)` reads `t.isdst` the way `mktime` reads `tm_isdst`. Every one of those three behaviours is asserted in `spec/stubs_spec.lua` against numbers first read from musl, so the model is checked against a real clock rather than against itself. `spec/helpers/addon.lua` carries the owner's own zone (`H.CHICAGO`, `H.chicagoClock`). Nothing else about a timezone is modelled and nothing else should be: one zone with one rule is the whole harness this class of fault needs.
  - **What it was silently breaking, beyond the clocks.** R-6's wait compared `refreshStartedAt` - written correctly in UTC by `date("!...")` - against a parse running an hour late, so the elapsed time was 3600 s too large, `Drift.WAIT_GIVE_UP_SECONDS` (600) was cleared on the FIRST check, and `Drift.Waiting` deleted the stamp before any surface could draw it. **The wait could not have appeared on the owner's client at any point since daylight time began.** Proven red: with the fix removed, the thirty-second wait guard answers `behind` instead of `wait`. §11's open question about R-6's wait is closed by this, not by an eye test.


- **2026-09-15 (night) - a vault reward's phrase is decided by the document's record of its POOL, never by the document's existence (R-3d, WKE-584; C-13, the profile's vault count).**
  - **The premise that was too wide.** C-8 (WKE-558) read in QE Live's own importer that every vault option is active from the moment it is imported (`SimCImportEngine.ts:712`). The vault road took that to mean a reward the plan's document never mentions was in the run and was passed over, so `road.phrase = entry and PHRASE_NOT_IN_BEST_SET or PHRASE_NO_RATING`. **The premise is about a reward the run IMPORTED, and the run imports nothing the profile did not carry.** On reset day before the player opens the Great Vault - and any week the client withholds the links and no login restores them - the companion builds a profile with no vault section, QE Live is shown no vault card, and the document's silence about the reward means it never existed to the rating. The owner read the consequence on 2026-09-15 (section 9): `not in your best set` and `Skip this one, the plan uses your Miststalker legs`, over a 315 vault reward rated 80 minutes before the vault existed. Principle 3 forbids exactly that.
  - **C-13: the count travels.** The companion already knew - `profile.counts.vault`, and it logs `no generated Great Vault reward ... so the profile has no vault section` - but only the log knew. The verdict file now carries `profileVaultCount`, file-level like `scenarioNote` and for the same reason: the profile is the RUN's and not any one document's. A **number, not a flag**, because zero is the whole case and a field written only when it is interesting cannot say zero; absent means the run did not say, which is every file before C-13 and every paste. `ns.Companion` carries it onto each Top Gear verdict, the way it carries the note.
  - **The rule, in one function.** `ns.Roads.VaultConsidered(entry, inputs, reward)` answers **true** (some pass's `considered` holds the reward's key, by C-10's identity join through `ns.Companion.IsConsidered`), **false** (`profileVaultCount == 0`, or a pool was recorded and holds it nowhere), or **nil** (no pool and no count on record - every pre-C-11 file and every paste, where C-8's premise still stands unchanged). The count outranks the pools, because a pool that held no vault card and a pool nobody recorded look identical from the road. A vault option is a baseline card, so it is in every pass's pool or in none of them; the plan's own document and its later passes are all asked, which cannot be wrong either way.
  - **What `false` changes.** The road's phrase becomes `not rated - new since the last refresh`, it joins the **no-rating group** rather than the set group, `Roads.IsForward` and `Roads.IsRated` are false so it does not glow and carries no imperative, and its sentence is `Roads.NOT_RATED_YET_SENTENCE`: **"The plan hasn't rated this yet. Refresh, then look again."** That sentence is asked for BEFORE the group tests in `Roads.ItemSentence`, because the reward is in the vault rather than in the bags and its road is no longer in the set group - the pair of facts that would otherwise leave an offered item sentence-less against principle 16. And where the profile carried no vault at all, `Roads.PlanSentence` replaces the whole Vault tab headline with **"The plan was rated before your vault was generated. Refresh."**: a plan chosen without this week's vault in front of it is not a decision about the vault, and reading a pick out of it on that tab says it is.
  - **Proven red, one at a time:** the count branch (the owner's three rewards go back to `not in your best set` in the set group), the plan sentence, the pool walk (three guards), the `ItemSentence` branch, and the `nil` bound - which, broken, also reddens `spec/roads_spec.lua:781` and `spec/tooltip_spec.lua:428`, the two guards that have protected C-8's reading since 558. On the companion side: the payload field, and the `!== undefined` test that makes a zero a zero (`if (profileVaultCount)` drops it, and the end-to-end fingerprint test goes red with it).

- **2026-09-15 (night) - an emptied vault and a vault that never filled read the same to the client, so the addon's OWN snapshots are what tell them apart (V-3, WKE-587).** The owner's Vault tab at ~15:50, minutes after he claimed the Enigmatic Dreamwatcher's Leggings, read `The vault has not generated this week's rewards yet.` over nine empty cells. It had generated nine, and he was wearing one of them.
  - **What the client can and cannot say.** After a claim `CanClaimRewards()` is false, `HasAvailableRewards()` is false and `GetActivities()` carries no rewards - which is character for character what a fresh character in a week with no progress answers. Ketho's `WeeklyRewardsDocumentation.lua` was read for a direct "claimed this period" read and there is none: the six functions the `vault` capture already names are all there are, and `AreRewardsForCurrentRewardPeriod()` is about rewards the client is HOLDING, of which after a claim there are none, so it is not that read either and is not guessed at.
  - **The evidence that does exist is the addon's.** `ns.VaultPanel.ClaimedThisPeriod(vault, captures, now)`: the client refuses a claim, says nothing is waiting, and one of the stored `vault` snapshots - taken inside the reward period the client is in NOW, and carrying reward links - saw rewards. Rewards do not leave a vault by themselves. The period boundary is the one `IsVerdictStale` already uses, from the client's own fact: `nextReset = now + secondsUntilWeeklyReset`, and this period began a week before that. Everything missing answers false, so a missing fact never produces the claim.
  - **The fourth reading of the same empty list.** `Panel.CLAIMED_REWARDS_NOTE` is `You've taken this week's reward. The next vault opens in 6d 19h.` - the countdown the client's own `secondsUntilWeeklyReset`, through `ns.Roads.CountdownText`, which is `ResetText`'s formatter split out so the two sentences about that number cannot round it differently. Principle 9: no deadline, and nothing about what the reset does. It is tried AHEAD of `NO_REWARDS_NOTE` and behind the two `HasAvailableRewards` branches, because the withheld and reset-day states have their own remedies and the ask is what those are for.
  - **`NO_REWARDS_NOTE` gained the remedy M3-16b found.** It reads `The vault hasn't generated this week's rewards yet. Open the Great Vault once, then refresh.` - the window is what generates the rewards, so the sentence that reports the state now names the one thing that changes it. **Recorded as the cost:** a player genuinely below the first threshold is told to open a vault that will still be empty. That is a harmless instruction on a state the player can see for himself, and it is the better of the two, because the sentence it replaces left reset day with no way forward at all.
  - **The plan is still read out, minus one clause.** `Roads.PlanSentence` takes `week.vaultClaimed` and drops the `Grab ... from the vault` clause and nothing else: the Catalyst charge and the crests are still this week's plan. The Vault tab's headline block, which used to need a gear option to exist at all, is built for a claimed vault too - as the plan ALONE (`headline.planOnly`), with no pick line, no icon and no scenario lines, because there is nothing in the vault to lead with or compare and `no option in this vault is in the answer` about nine empty cells would be a second, worse way of saying what the note already says. The charge footnote the scenario lines would have carried is the plan sentence's own footnote, so nothing is lost with them.
  - **Proven red, one at a time:** `ClaimedThisPeriod` forced false (the claimed vault goes back to the owner's screenshot); the `at >= periodStart` test dropped (a vault that never generated anything claims a reward was taken from it); the `not week.vaultClaimed` guard dropped (`Grab the legs from the vault.` comes back over the leggings he is wearing); `model.claimed` out of the headline's condition (the claimed tab loses the plan entirely). Built over the owner's own reset-day transcript: snapshot 9 of the 14:27 pull is the emptied client's activity list and snapshot 12 is the capture carrying the nine links, so the claim is found in his own data rather than in a stub state.
  - **Nothing of it has been on a real screen.** The owner's next claim is the first look.


- **2026-09-15 (night) - "N of your items weren't rated this time" counts the items NO pass was shown, which is the LAST pass's leftovers (C-11a, WKE-586).**
  - **The defect.** `Modules/Companion.lua` set `verdict.excluded = entry.excluded or file.excluded` for every Top Gear document, so the verdict on screen - pass 1, the plan - carried **pass 1's own** leftover list. Since C-11 that list is precisely the set of cards passes 2 and 3 went on to ask about, and the companion's own guard says so (`fork.test.js`, "a whole run asks about every card, each non-baseline card in exactly one pass"). The header therefore named as unrated exactly the items the run had just rated. The owner read `25 of your items weren't rated this time: ...` on Equip Now and `29 ...` on the Vault tab, over the 14:31 run whose every scenario's pass 3 logged `0 still to ask about` (§9).
  - **The rule, in one function.** `ns.Companion.Unrated(verdict, passes)`: the **last** later pass's `excluded`, or the verdict's own when the run has no later pass. Each pass is shown what the one before it left out, so what the LAST pass left out is what nothing was asked about. `passes` is `ns.QEImport.Passes(contentType, scenario)` - the same list `Roads.LaterPass` walks, so the two tab headers and the `beyond the rating's item limit` tail cannot disagree about which items no pass saw - and is looked up when not handed in, because `Match.Build` is given a verdict and not a run. Three call sites read it and no surface reads `verdict.excluded` for this question any more: `Modules/Match.lua` (Equip Now's header and its tooltip), `UI/VaultPanel.lua` (the tab's line), `UI/UpgradeMapPanel.RoadInputs` (the tail). **Never `or verdict.excluded` at a call site:** a run whose last pass left nothing out has nothing to say, and a nil-coalescing guard at the call reinstates the defect one line lower - which it did, once, and the Equip Now guard caught it.
  - **Which list, and the two agree.** The companion already writes the **file-level** `excluded` as the base pass's last pass (`lib/fork.js` ~988, overwriting per pass for the default scenario), and the owner's live file confirms it: `file-level excluded 0` on a run whose pass 1 left 24 behind (§9). The addon reads the **pass shelf** rather than that field, which is the same answer per scenario instead of per file - the Catalyst passes have clones to leave out that the base pass never had, so the file's one list is not the `catalyzed` run's. No companion change was needed; both sides name the same pass.
  - **Proven red:** `Unrated` reduced to `return verdict.excluded` reddens nine guards across four specs - three in `companion_spec` (the last pass wins; the named-three wording over a pass-3 list; the handed-in passes), two in `match_spec` (the empty header; the header that names only pass 3's leftover), two in `vaultpanel_spec` (the same pair on the tab) and two in `upgrademap_spec` (`RoadInputs` carries the run's list; the tail stays for what the bound really left). The one new guard that stays green under the break is the no-later-pass fallback, which is the case the old code already got right.


- **2026-09-15 (night) - the load after a refresh always says one line, and the chat frame and the strip read ONE decision (R-6a, WKE-590).**
  - **What was silent, and why it was correct.** M3-16b put the wait's sentence in the chat frame because the load is the moment the player is looking there. Its test was `Drift.Waiting`, which is true only between the refresh's reload and the plan the companion writes. On 2026-09-15 at 17:22 local (`main` at `69d4607`) the owner reloaded, ran `/lootpath refresh`, landed back in game and saw no line at all; the strip's tooltip read `The companion's last run: profile unchanged since 2026-09-15T22:20:31Z; the verdict file is current`. C-4's fingerprint had skipped the run in under a second and the status file said `skipped` before the reload had finished loading, so there was genuinely nothing to wait for. **The wait was right and the addon was silent at exactly the moment the player had asked it a question**, which is the thing principle 16 is about.
  - **The rule.** The first load after a refresh always says one line, in the addon's voice, decided off the status file that load carries. A load with no refresh out there - a plain `/reload`, an ordinary login - says nothing at all, because nothing was asked.
  - **One decision, not two readings.** `ns.Drift.Decide(now)` reads `db.global.drift.refreshStartedAt` against the loaded plan's stamp and `ns.companionStatus`, and answers `"done"`, `"failed"`, `"skipped"`, `"unseen"`, `"waiting"` or nil (no refresh out there, or one past `WAIT_GIVE_UP_SECONDS`). It has no side effects; the callers clear. `Drift.LoadLine` words it and says it once; `Drift.Waiting` is `Decide() == "waiting"` and clears the stamp on everything else. **This is why it had to be one function and not two lookups:** the strip's C-9 clause and the wait's own test were already two readings of the same file, and `skipped` fell between them - the strip said `profile unchanged, no run` while the chat frame said nothing.
  - **What it changes on the strip, not just in chat.** Before R-6a only a FAILED run, a newer plan and the ten-minute bound ended the wait. A run C-4 SKIPPED, and a companion that has never written a status file at all, both left `rating your gear, started …` counting on the strip over a run that had already ended or had never begun. Both now end it, and the chat line names the cure in the second case (`the companion hasn't been seen; is it running?`). The wait is the only state that keeps the stamp, because the strip counts from it and a second reload while the rating is going is still waiting.
  - **A consequence worth stating: a wait now stands only where a companion has been SEEN.** Three spec files stood a wait in a world with no status file at all, which no real machine is in after a first run; they now carry the previous idle run a real machine carries. That is the same fact from the other side, not a weakened guard.
  - **Proven red, one at a time (eight):** each of the five states in turn (delete its branch from `LoadLine` and that load goes silent again); the terminal clear (leave `refreshStartedAt` and the next plain `/reload` repeats the line); the strip-and-chat agreement (return `"waiting"` from `Decide` for a skipped run and the strip counts a run that has ended); and the wait's own stamp survival (clear it in the wait branch and the strip loses the clock it counts from).

- **2026-09-16 - an empty read is not a capture; the companion never rates nothing; and the flush label was never broken (R-7b, WKE-591).**
  - **What happened.** The owner logged out for real at 19:19 on 2026-09-15. The flush stored an `inventory` snapshot of `equipped 0` with 20 bag records. At his 22:07 login the companion woke on that write, built `0 equipped, 0 in bags, 0 in the bank, 0 vault, 14 lines`, sent it to QE Live, and died at the fork: `Selected Items: 0/30`, exit 4, the previous verdict untouched. The safety at the far end held. Everything before it was wrong.
  - **What the client actually does, read from his live SavedVariables on 2026-09-16 with `tools/companion/lib/lua-savedvariables.js`** (the 19:19 write itself was four snapshots deep and had been pushed off the end by then; the 22:11:52 logout of the same night is the same failure and was still in the file):

    | snapshot | at | trigger | durationMs | equipped | bag records | total numSlots | bag items |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | inventory[1] | 2026-09-15 22:11:52 (**real logout**) | flush | **0.58** | **0** | 20 | **0** | **0** |
    | inventory[2] | 2026-09-16 12:22:28 | refresh | 15.43 | 15 | 20 | 188 | 161 |
    | inventory[3] | 2026-09-16 12:22:28 (reload) | flush | 29.62 | 15 | 20 | 188 | 161 |
    | inventory[4] | 2026-09-16 12:22:47 (reload) | flush | 14.39 | 15 | 20 | 188 | 161 |

    The `env` read of that same 22:11:52 flush answers `UnitLevel 90`, `UnitClass Druid`, `capturedOn = "flush"`, `flushMs 20.49` - and `GetSpecialization()` 4 with `GetSpecializationInfo(4)` returning id 0 and **no name**. So at `PLAYER_LOGOUT` on a real logout the item layer, the container layer and the spec-info layer are all gone while the plain unit reads still answer. On a `/reload` none of them is.
  - **The decision: an empty read is refused, not stored.** `ns.RegisterCapture` takes an optional `refuse(data)`; `ns.RunCapture` consults it between reading and storing, on the synchronous and the asynchronous path both, and a refusal is `{ ok = false, reason, refusedStore = true }` with NOTHING written to `db.global.captures`. The `inventory` capture refuses when it has no equipped records AND the client still gives the character a level and a class - the same two facts `env` records one capture earlier in the same flush. **Why the pair and not the count alone:** a genuinely naked character is a real state and must still be captured. **Why not storing matters:** R-7a bounds the history at four per name and the loop writes one per reload, so a stored empty read pushes the newest good one towards the edge and the flush after it off the end. The refusal keeps the newest good read newest, which is what makes the plan at the next login the last real one rather than none.
  - **The flush says what it threw away.** A refusal stores no snapshot of its own, so `Companion.CaptureAtFlush` writes `flushRefusals` onto the `env` snapshot of the same flush, beside `capturedOn` and `flushMs`. Without it a pull shows an `inventory` history hours older than the `env` next to it and nothing saying why. Nothing in the addon reads it; it is for the transcript.
  - **The companion never rates nothing.** A profile with `counts.equipped === 0` is refused before the fork is opened, with one line - `refusing to rate a profile with no equipped gear (the newest inventory read is empty); the previous verdict is untouched` - a `skipped` status (not `failed`: nothing broke) and **exit code 8**, its own, because a wrapper could not otherwise tell "QE Live broke" from "we sent it nothing". `--profile-only` is deliberately still allowed to print the empty profile: it opens nothing, writes nothing, and that print is how this gets diagnosed. In game the strip reads `companion: no gear to rate, no run (hh:mm) - see companion.log` and R-6a's load line reads `your gear didn't reach the companion - the last read of it was empty - so the plan you have is untouched. Try /lootpath refresh.` **Both surfaces branch on the exit code, never on the message:** `skipped` now means two opposite things (C-4's "your plan is already right" and this one's "nothing was sent"), and the message is prose.
  - **`PLAYER_LEAVING_WORLD`: the measurement, not a fix.** Ketho's `SystemDocumentation.lua` declares both it and `PLAYER_LOGOUT` `SynchronousEvent = true` and says **nothing** about which fires first or what still answers at either, so the order was not assumed. The addon counts equipped links there - `GetInventoryItemLink` for at most nineteen slots, no item data, no containers, refused in combat - stores no snapshot, and `CaptureAtFlush` carries the count into the flush's `env` as `leavingWorld`. A pull then answers the question outright: links one event earlier and none at the flush is "late", none at either is "already gone". **The whole flush sequence was deliberately NOT moved there.** `PLAYER_LEAVING_WORLD` fires on every zone change and every loading screen, and the sequence costs 17-49 ms measured; that is not a thing to spend on each of them on a guess about ordering.
  - **The third premise is refuted, and nothing was changed for it.** The issue reported `run after a write whose capture does not say how it was taken (an addon from before R-6)` for a `flush` snapshot and asked which side had drifted. Neither had: the addon writes `trigger = "flush"` and `capturedOn = "flush"` (both present on every flush snapshot in his live file), `lib/profile.js` lifts `env.trigger`, and `whatThisWriteCarried` has had the `flush` branch since R-7a. What happened is that R-7a renamed that label on both sides at once and merged at 15:47 that day; the owner's addon was re-synced and **the watcher process in his own window was not restarted**, so it was still running the pre-R-7a `whatThisWriteCarried`, whose only branch was `capture.trigger === 'logout'` (`git show 866e8d7^:tools/companion/companion.js`). A new addon's `flush` fell through it to the catch-all. The line is now pinned by a test over the very snapshot shape that was misread. **The standing lesson: a companion change and an addon change that rename the same field are ONE deploy, and the watcher is half of it.** The watcher is restarted when a PR touches `tools/companion/`, and the owner is the only one who can do it.
  - **The spec you are in, against the spec the plan is for.** The owner asked, the same night, whether being logged in as Guardian had caused the empty read. It had not - the scan never looks at spec, and the `env` read of that flush records class Druid with no spec name at all. But a refresh taken in a non-healing spec captures THAT spec's equipment as "what you wear", and the plan then reads that gear as worn. `profile.js` `specMismatch` already catches the half that can only be seen afterwards (QE Live's own browser profile against the capture); `ns.Companion.SpecClause` is the half the client can say BEFORE the mistake: `you're in Guardian; this plan is for Restoration Druid - switch and refresh`, off the live spec with the newest `env` capture's `specInfo` as the fallback. It is said on the strip - taking the line, with the four facts displaced into the tooltip, exactly as M3-16b's wait does, and losing to the wait - in R-6a's load line under the rating's own news, and by the refresh chain before it captures. **Nothing is refused and no rating is touched:** a player may want a plan for a spec he is not standing in.
  - **A consequence in the tests, worth knowing.** The stub world's character wore nothing, which since this issue is not a character but the refusal itself. Three capture-chain describes now call `H.dress(world)`; a test that means to see the refusal strips the gear again.
  - **Proven red, one at a time (nine):** the synchronous refusal gate (removed from `RunCapture`: the empty snapshot stores and four guards fail); the `inventory` registration's `refuse`; `flushRefusals`; `leavingWorld` on the `env` snapshot; the companion's `counts.equipped === 0` guard (the fork double is reached and the run dies as exit 4 - the 2026-09-15 failure exactly); the strip's exit-code branch; the load line's exit-code branch; `SpecClause`'s sentence; and the strip's displacement.

- **2026-09-16 (evening) - a real logout NEVER reads the gear, so R-7's promise is retired in the words and said on screen instead (R-7c, WKE-594).**
  - **The measurement closes the question R-7b left open.** The owner's 14:25:58 logout of 2026-09-16 was the first real one on the merged R-7b build, pulled as `spec/fixtures/captures/Lootpath-20260916-142559.lua`. Its flush `env` snapshot carries `leavingWorld = { equipped = 0, elapsedMs = 0.069 }` **and** `flushRefusals = { { capture = "inventory", reason = "capture 'inventory' read nothing worth storing: the client answered the equipment scan with nothing" } }`, and no `inventory` snapshot was stored for that flush. So the client answers `GetInventoryItemLink` with nothing for every slot at `PLAYER_LEAVING_WORLD` as well as at `PLAYER_LOGOUT`: **the item layer is gone before either event fires, and no ordering of the two would help.** Four real logouts measured (2026-09-15 19:19 and 22:11:52; 2026-09-16 14:00:11 and 14:25:58), four empty reads; every `/reload` flush beside them reads `equipped 15` in 14-30 ms. §11 said in advance that if neither event saw it the promise would be retired and said plainly on screen; this is that.
  - **The rule, in one sentence:** a `/reload` or a `/lootpath refresh` is what captures gear; a logout keeps what the last one captured. R-7's "log out and your plan is current next login" is gone from `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §5, `docs/ROADS-UX.md`, `tools/companion/README.md` and every player-facing string, and **a guard keeps it gone**: `spec/drift_spec.lua` walks `ns.Drift`, `ns.Companion` and the chat output of `/lootpath help` and `/lootpath status`, and fails on any string that puts a logout together with capturing or with the plan being current. The shape rather than the word, because the one string that may mention a logout is the retirement itself.
  - **Nothing in the sequence moved, and nothing was removed.** The flush still runs on both events and still takes `env`, `inventory` and `currencies` - `env`, `vault` and `currencies` are worth having at a logout, and on a reload the gear genuinely is read. The empty read is still refused and never stored. `leavingWorld` stays on the `env` snapshot as the permanent record of the measurement; it costs 0.07 ms. `ns.CAPTURE_HISTORY` is untouched.
  - **Said on screen, out of ONE decision.** `ns.Companion.GearUnreadAtFlush` answers the newest stored `inventory` snapshot when three things hold: the newest `env` snapshot was taken at a flush, that flush refused `inventory`, and no `inventory` read since is newer. `ns.Drift.Decide` turns that into a **sixth** state, `gearunread`, beside R-6a's five, so R-6a's load line and the status strip cannot disagree about it any more than they can about the other five. Both say `your gear wasn't read at logout - last rated 17 hours ago · /lootpath refresh to rate what you wear now`, the age being the newest stored read's. Two properties are deliberate. It is **last of the six**, after every refresh state, because a player who has just clicked is owed the answer to the question he asked. And it is **self-healing rather than sticky**: the cure is the read itself, so a reload or a refresh stores a snapshot newer than the refusal and the sentence stops, with no flag to clear and nothing to remember. On the strip it displaces the four facts into the tooltip the way the wait and R-7b's spec clause do, and it goes ahead of the spec clause - a plan rated for the wrong gear is wrong whichever spec it was rated in.
  - **The companion says which read it rated.** `whatThisWriteCarried` printed `run after a logout or reload (gear captured at the flush)` for a flush that had captured no gear at all; for a write whose `env` carries `flushRefusals` naming `inventory` it now says `run after a logout that could not read the gear; rating the inventory read of <capturedAtLocal>`, naming the snapshot the profile was actually built from. `lib/profile.js` lifts the refused names onto `profile.capture.flushRefusals` for it. When that newest read is itself empty - the owner's 14:00:11 case - R-7b's exit-8 refusal follows unchanged.
  - **And the nit R-7b left.** The empty-gear refusal wrote `FAILED: refusing to rate ...` and `that run failed with exit code 8` into a log sitting beside a status file that said `skipped`: one run, two words, and the harsher one was the wrong one. `lib/log.js` gains `log.skipped`, which writes `skipped: `; `FAILED:` is for a run that broke. The watcher's per-run line reads the same way off `SKIPPED_EXITS`.
  - **`UI.AgeText` gained a second door, not a second set of words.** A capture snapshot records `capturedAt` as an epoch and no ISO string, so the formatter moved into `UI.AgeTextFromSeconds` and `UI.AgeText` calls it. One vocabulary, two ways in.
  - **Proven red, one at a time (ten):** the `trigger == flush` test (a `refresh` snapshot carrying the field is believed); the `capture == "inventory"` test (a refusal of `currencies` fires the sentence); the newer-read test (the sentence outlives the read that cures it); the `gearunread` branch in `LoadLine` (the load is silent again); the strip's `gearClause` (the sentence never reaches the line); the state's ORDER in `Decide` (it displaces the answer to a refresh the player asked for); the promise guard (putting "log out and your plan is current next login" into `Drift.LOAD_DONE`); `flushRefusals` in `lib/profile.js`; the `flushRefusals` branch in `whatThisWriteCarried`; and `log.skipped` in `companion.js`. Each broken alone with the build already committed, run, and restored. The `type(refusals) ~= "table"` line is nil-safety rather than a guard of its own - removing it changes no test, because the loop below it then finds nothing - and is not counted among the ten.

- **2026-09-16 (night) - every atlas on the Vault tab at the art's own proportions, and the row art as a banner (V-5a, WKE-607).**
  - **The fault was one shape, in three places.** The owner's full-screen pair of 2026-09-16 ~20:19, Lootpath's Vault tab beside Blizzard's Great Vault: "Locks are in place, but the placement of the images is squished and not centered." V-5 gave every atlas the box it happened to sit in - `SetAllPoints` over a cell for the locked/unlocked background and for the pick's glow, `SetWidth(ROW_LABEL_WIDTH - 6)` with top and bottom anchors for the row art - and a texture given two anchors per axis is scaled twice, once per side. Two factors is the squash. **Blizzard gives every one of them exactly one factor:** `useAtlasSize = true` in `WeeklyRewardsMixin:SetUpActivity` (the row art) and in `WeeklyRewardsActivityMixin:Refresh` (both cell backgrounds), and `useAtlasSize="true"` on the CompletedIcon and the SelectedTexture of WeeklyRewardActivityTemplate - all in Blizzard's own shipped files under `.luals/`. The argument is the second of `TextureBase:SetAtlas(atlas, useAtlasSize, filterMode, ...)` (Ketho, `Core/Widget/Base/TextureBase.lua`).
  - **The addon knows the size of no atlas, and never will.** `ns.UI.ItemLine.AtlasInfo(name)` asks `C_Texture.GetAtlasInfo` at draw time and answers `{ name, width, height }` from the AtlasInfo's own `width` and `height` fields (Ketho, `---@class AtlasInfo` in `TextureUtilsDocumentation.lua`), or the name alone when a client answers an atlas with no usable size, or nil when it does not have it at all. `ItemLine.Atlas` is now the name-only half of the same read, so every existing caller is unchanged. One `drawAtlas(texture, name, boxWidth, boxHeight, margin)` in `UI/VaultPanel.lua` is the whole policy: art that fits is drawn at its own size (`SetAtlas(name, true)`), art that does not is scaled by `min(roomW/w, roomH/h)` - one factor, both sides - and every one of them is anchored `CENTER`. The two cell backgrounds, the tick, the pick's glow and the row art all go through it.
  - **The row art is a banner, and the cells pay for it in width.** Blizzard's own header frame is 326x131 and its activity frame 219x126 (Blizzard_WeeklyRewards.xml), so its art is about two and a half times as wide as tall while Lootpath's column was 74 wide against a 104-tall row - narrower than it was tall, which is why the illustration read as compressed sideways. The column is 132 now, the art fitted inside it at its own ratio and centred, with the row's name over the art's left edge (Blizzard insets its own header Name to x=28 of 326). **The trade, measured:** the panel's content frame is created at `PANEL_WIDTH - 40` = 520, so three cells across went from `(520 - 74 - 16) / 3` = 143 to `(520 - 132 - 16) / 3` = 124. The issue said the cells give way first and give way in width, not height; they do.
  - **Premise scaled down: the cell's own aspect stays as it was.** The issue asked for a cell "wider than tall", moving toward Blizzard's 219x126 (1.74:1). It already was wider than tall - 143x104, 1.38:1 - and after the banner it is 124x104, 1.19:1. It cannot be 1.74 here. Blizzard's cell carries four pieces of text; Lootpath's carries six rows (the pick band, the item line, the tags, the verdict, the extras, the footer) and they, not the width, set the 104. Taking the height to 71 to buy the ratio would drop text the tab already shows, and widening the window is not this issue's to do. What was actually complained about - the stretch - is fixed regardless of the cell's own box, because the art no longer takes the box's shape.
  - **Two smaller things Blizzard's XML settled.** A locked cell's fraction now sits bottom-right INSIDE the badge, where Blizzard's own Progress is anchored (BOTTOMRIGHT x=-15 y=15); a cell holding a reward keeps it in the top band, because its footer and extras own the bottom. And the locked sentence is anchored to the background texture rather than to the cell, so it follows whatever was drawn - on a client with no atlas the background still covers the whole cell, which is where that sentence always was.
  - **What the stub learned, and what it is honest about.** `Texture:SetAtlas` takes `useAtlasSize` and sizes the texture the way the client does, so a test can read back the size a texture ended up with; `C_Texture.GetAtlasInfo` answers per-atlas sizes, an entry written `true` still meaning the old 16-square. **One of those sizes is measured:** the owner read `evergreen-weeklyrewards-reward-selected` at **214 x 121** with `C_Texture.GetAtlasInfo` on his own client during R-2b (WKE-575), where the same atlas had been squeezed by `SetAllPoints` into a 15-point square - this fault, in another surface, eleven days earlier. The other five are PLACEHOLDER, said so in the stub, and shaped from the only figures that could be read: the size of Blizzard's frame that carries each one. No test asserts a figure; each asserts that what was DRAWN carries the ratio the client reported, whatever it reported. (The measured atlas sits 5 points inside its frame either way, which is what makes a frame a fair stand-in and not the thing itself.)
  - **Not built, deliberately.** The issue's comparison notes Blizzard's `evergreen-weeklyrewards-divider` between the three rows. It is not one of the three numbered build items, and widening is not this repo's habit; the atlas name and its anchors are recorded here for whoever wants it.
  - **Proven red, one at a time (six), with the build committed first and `git status` between each:** the single scale factor in `drawAtlas` (replaced by the box's own width and height - the cell badges, the pick's glow and the row banner all fail); the `CENTER` anchor on a cell's badge; the banner (put back to V-5's column-shaped `SetSize(width - 6, CELL_HEIGHT)` - the art is taller than it is wide again); the flat fill's full-cell anchors in the no-atlas branch; the tick's fit; and the no-interaction guard (an `OnUIInteract` added to `Panel.Refresh` - three tests fail, this one among them). The tick's guard is worth a note: it only bites on a tick atlas that is not square, because a 12x12 band has the same ratio as a square atlas, so what turned it red was a deliberately non-square box rather than V-5's code.

They are real: Blizzard's own `Blizzard_EncounterJournal/Mainline/Blizzard_EncounterJournal.lua` (Gethe/wow-ui-source, `live`, 3731 lines) calls `EJ_SetLootFilter` (2 sites), `EJ_GetNumLoot` (2), `EJ_SelectInstance` (1), `EJ_SetDifficulty` (5), `EJ_SelectTier` (1), `EJ_GetNumTiers` (1), `EJ_GetInstanceByIndex` (8), `C_EncounterJournal.GetLootInfoByIndex` (4), registers `EJ_LOOT_DATA_RECIEVED` (that spelling; payload `itemID` per Ketho `Event.lua`) and gates its re-read on `EJ_IsLootListOutOfDate()`. **It never calls `SetPreviewMythicPlusLevel`** (0 sites), so that function's effect on loot is unobserved until M3-2.

The real function is `C_EncounterJournal.GetInstanceForGameMap(mapID) -> journalInstanceID?`, whose doc comment says it takes a game mapID, "not a uiMapID". `C_ChallengeMode.GetMapUIInfo(mapChallengeModeID)` returns `name, id, timeLimit, texture, backgroundTexture, mapID`. **Verified 2026-09-06 from QE Live's source, re-read for WKE-518 (branch `dev`; read, never copied):**
- `TopGearJSONExport.ts` is unchanged from the 2026-09-05 reading: 80 lines, `SCHEMA = "qe-live-droptimizer"`, `VERSION = 1`, and the payload exactly as §4 records it. `gameType` is derived, not stored: `player?.spec?.includes("Classic") ? "Classic" : "Retail"`.
- **Both sign conventions are now verified twice, and they agree.** The exporter states them at lines 40-43: "scoreDifference: number (% - positive means alt is worse), rawDifference: number (HPS - negative means alt is worse)". `TopGearEngineShared.js` lines 50-51 computes them inside `buildDifferential(itemSet, primeSet, ...)`, where `itemSet` is the alternative and `primeSet` the top set: `scoreDifference = (primeSet.hardScore - itemSet.hardScore) / primeSet.hardScore * 100` (positive when the alternative scores lower) and `rawDifference = itemSet.hardScore - primeSet.hardScore` (negative when the alternative scores lower). The arithmetic confirms the comment; nothing here rests on the comment alone.
- The exporter renames the two fields on the way out: `scoreDifference` -> `scorePercent`, `rawDifference` -> `hpsDifference`. ~~`rawDifference`'s conversion to real HPS is commented out in his source, so `hpsDifference` is a raw score delta, not an HPS figure~~ **Corrected 2026-09-08 (WKE-535): that reading was of the wrong file.** `TopGearEngineShared.js` does carry the commented-out `/* * player.getHPS(contentType) */`, but `git grep` shows its `buildDifferential` is imported by `TopGearEngineClassic.js` alone; the **Retail** path is `TopGearEngine.ts`, whose own `buildDifferential` (line 487) computes `rawDifference = Math.round(((itemSet.hardScore - primeSet.hardScore) / primeSet.hardScore) * player.getHPS(contentType) * modelDiff)`. The committed Dungeon export agrees with the arithmetic and not with the old claim: its top set scores 5460.909, so a raw hardScore delta for a 0.33% differential would be about -12, and the file says -1194 - which needs an HPS around 350,000, exactly what `getHPS` returns for a modern healer. `modelDiff` is `CONSTANTS.modelDiff = 1.5` whenever the cast model is "Default", and it multiplies BOTH fields. So `hpsDifference` IS an HPS figure on Retail, and `UpgradeMapPanel.ValueText`'s `(+1234.5 score)` understates it rather than lying. **Left as it is in M3-6 and filed**: relabelling the Top Gear line is not this issue's scope, and the wording is the owner's call (§11).
- **The Upgrade Finder join, measured 2026-09-08 (M3-6).** The 2026-09-07 Dungeon export (`dungeon: 7`, `raid: [3]`) lists 357 drops over **315 distinct itemID + item level pairs** - 35 of them listed by more than one drop type, which is the only reason the two counts differ. **228 are ranked above the current set, 87 at exactly zero, none below it**, and `hpsGain` agrees in sign with `upgradePercent` on all 315. - **`InputScrollFrameTemplate`** (`Blizzard_SharedXML/SecureUIPanelTemplates.xml:106`): a `ScrollFrame` whose scroll child is an `EditBox` at parentKey `EditBox` with `multiLine="true"`, `countInvisibleLetters="true"`, `autoFocus="false"`, plus a `CharCount` FontString and a `maxLetters` KeyValue **defaulting to 0**. `InputScrollFrame_OnTextChanged` writes `GetMaxLetters() - GetNumLetters()` into `CharCount`, which is a large negative number at maxLetters 0 - hence `hideCharCount` and `CharCount:Hide()`.
- **The Settings API signatures on 12.1** (`Blizzard_Settings_Shared/Blizzard_Settings.lua`): `RegisterVerticalLayoutCategory(name)`, `RegisterProxySetting(categoryTbl, variable, variableType, name, defaultValue, getValue, setValue)`, `CreateControlTextContainer()` -> `container:Add(value, label, tooltip)` / `:GetData()`, `CreateDropdown(category, setting, options, tooltip)`, `RegisterAddOnCategory(category)`, `OpenToCategory(categoryID)`. `Settings.VarType = { Boolean = "boolean", String = "string", Number = "number" }`; `category:GetID()` is `SettingsCategoryMixin:GetID`. `RegisterProxySetting` is used rather than `RegisterAddOnSetting` because the value lives in AceDB, not in a plain global table.
- **`UISpecialFrames`** is a list of frame NAMES (`Blizzard_UIParentPanelManager` iterates it), which is why the main frame is created with one. `Frame:SetHyperlinksEnabled(enabled)` exists, so the item links in the rows can raise a tooltip.

**Read 2026-09-14 night, R-2a (WKE-571), from Baganator's installed source rather than from a screen** (`C:\World of Warcraft\_retail_\Interface\AddOns\Baganator`, version 823; read, never copied). Three facts settle what a corner widget is and refute two of the issue's three candidate causes:

- `Core/Config.lua:46-49` - the corner defaults. `icon_top_left_corner_array` is `{"junk", "item_level"}`; `icon_top_right_corner_array` is `{}`; bottom-left `{"equipment_set"}`; bottom-right `{"quantity"}`.
- `ItemViewCommon/ItemButton.lua:134-179` - one `Callback` per corner walks that corner's widgets in array order and **`break`s on the first that returns true**. Only one widget is ever shown per corner, so sharing a corner is not sharing: it is displacing.
- `API/Main.lua:185-196, 228-240` - `RegisterCornerWidget` asserts the id is new, stores the plugin, and `AutoInsert`s the `defaultPosition` at the **priority index** (`table.insert(cornerArray, priority, id)` when `priority <= #cornerArray`). `AutoInsert` is gated per id on `icon_corners_auto_insert_applied`, so **a widget new to an already-saved profile IS inserted** - candidate cause 1 ("only offered in the settings") is refuted. `ReportPluginAdded` then fires `PluginsUpdated`, which rebuilds the per-corner callbacks and asks for an item-widget refresh, so **a late registration is handled** - candidate cause 3's "installed too early to matter" is refuted for registration. What a late registration does NOT get is `ApplyItemDetailSettings`, which creates the per-button widget frame and runs only on the `ItemTextures` reason; `Baganator.Constants.RefreshReason` exposes only `ItemWidgets` and `Searches` publicly, so no addon can ask for it. Lootpath registers from `ns.onReady`, which is its own `ADDON_LOADED` - before any Baganator button exists - so this gap cannot be the cause on a fresh login, and it is recorded rather than worked around.

**So R-2's `{ corner = "top_left", priority = 1 }` was a displacement, not a mark**: Lootpath would have been first in top-left and the item level would have gone from every slot the plan marks. The widget is in `top_right` now, which ships empty. **What the blank screen actually was is still unmeasured**, and §11 carries it: the fix removes one cause, `/lootpath glow` names whichever remains.

Also read, and it closes candidate cause 2 as unlikely rather than as proven: `Syndicator/Search/BaseInfo.lua:7` sets `info.itemLink = cacheData.itemLink` unchanged, and Syndicator's live bag cache fills that from `C_Container.GetContainerItemLink` - the same call `Modules/Inventory.lua` scans with. The headless guard the issue asked for exists either way: `spec/tooltip_spec.lua` answers `ns.Glow.WantsLink` off the inventory capture's own link and asserts the key matches the map's.

The `env` of the 22:11:52 flush: `UnitLevel 90`, `UnitClass Druid`, `trigger = "flush"`, `capturedOn = "flush"`, `flushMs 20.49`, `GetSpecialization()` 4, `GetSpecializationInfo(4)` id 0 and **no name**. So the whole item layer, the container layer and the spec-info layer are gone at `PLAYER_LOGOUT` on a real logout while `UnitLevel` and `UnitClass` still answer; on a reload none of them is.
  - **Built back and confirmed exactly.** `spec/fixtures/captures/empty-equipment-flush.lua` is that shape written by hand (the only hand-written file in that folder, and its header says so). Through `tools/companion/lib/profile.js` it produces `0 equipped, 0 in bags, 0 in the bank, 0 vault, 14 lines` - the owner's 22:07 line for line - and `capture.trigger` `"flush"`.
  - **Which refutes the issue's third premise, on the same evidence.** `whatThisWriteCarried` over that profile answers `run after a logout or reload (gear captured at the flush)`, correctly, on `main` as it stood. The line the owner read came from a watcher PROCESS older than R-7a's 15:47 merge (§7, 2026-09-16). Nothing was changed for it; a test pins it.
  - **What is still unmeasured, and it is the human-required step:** whether the equipment scan is empty at EVERY real logout or only sometimes, and whether `PLAYER_LEAVING_WORLD` sees the gear one event earlier. The addon now counts equipped links there and carries the count into the flush's `env` as `leavingWorld`, so the owner's next real logout on the merged build - then a login and `tools\sync.ps1 -Pull` - answers both off one pull. Two data points say "empty on a real logout" and neither says why. **Third data point, 2026-09-16 14:00:11 (`Lootpath-20260916-140011.lua`):** `equipped 0`, 20 bag records with 0 items, `durationMs 0.88`, against `equipped 15` and 14.4-29.6 ms for the three reload flushes beside it - the same failure a third time, so "only sometimes" is now unlikely. But it was taken by the addon loaded BEFORE the sync (no `leavingWorld`, the read stored rather than refused), so it measures nothing about R-7b's addon half. What it does measure is the companion half: the restarted watcher (`6417440`) read the write at 19:00:14Z, built `0 equipped ... 14 lines`, and refused before the fork - exit 8, `state = "skipped"`, `stage = "profile"`, verdict untouched - read from `Data/companion.log` and `Data/CompanionStatus.lua`. **Fourth data point, 2026-09-16 14:25:58 (`Lootpath-20260916-142559.lua`), the first on the R-7b build, and the answer:** the flush's `env` carries `leavingWorld = { equipped = 0, elapsedMs = 0.069 }` and `flushRefusals = { { capture = "inventory", reason = "capture 'inventory' read nothing worth storing: the client answered the equipment scan with nothing" } }`; the `inventory` list has no 14:25 entry (four stored: 12:22:28, 12:22:47, 12:53:39 at `equipped 15`, and the empty 14:00:11). At `PLAYER_LEAVING_WORLD` the equipment is already gone, so neither event can read it and moving the sequence would change nothing. The watcher on that write (19:26:02Z) built `0 equipped ... 14 lines` from the still-newest 14:00:11 read and refused, exit 8. R-7c (WKE-594) is the consequence.
